title: Task Force Officer - FBI Inland Violent Crime Suppression Task Force (IVCSTF) - Riverside, CA
description:
Be part of a team that values safety, inclusion, and excellence

We are one of the largest U.S. railroads transporting the nation’s freight across 28 western states and 3 Canadian provinces. As a member of our team, you will play a role in supporting the movement of essential products and materials that help feed, clothe, supply, and power communities throughout America and the world.

We are committed to a culture where all employees are included, belong, and have equal opportunity to achieve their full potential. Come make a difference with us!

Learn more about BNSF and our Benefits

Job Location: Riverside
Other Potential Locations: Riverside, CA
Anticipated Start Date: 01/16/2027
Number of Positions: 1
Salary Range: $120,000 - $130,000

Apply early as this job may be removed or filled prior to the closing date, which is approximately seven (7) days after the posting date.

The BNSF Police department is dedicated to ensuring the security and safety of the company's vast network of rail operations. This department employs comprehensive strategies and state-of-the-art technology to safeguard the transportation of goods, prevent theft, and mitigate risks associated with railway operations. By collaborating closely with local, state, and federal law enforcement agencies, the BNSF Police team plays a critical role in maintaining the integrity and reliability of BNSF Railway's services.

As part of that mission, BNSF Police participates in the FBI Inland Violent Crime Suppression Task Force (IVCSTF), a multi-agency partnership focused on identifying, investigating, and prosecuting violent offenders, criminal enterprises, and fugitives responsible for violations of state and federal law. Through coordinated investigations and intelligence sharing, the task force leverages federal, state, and local resources to disrupt criminal organizations and remove dangerous offenders from communities.

This position serves as BNSF Police Department's representative on the IVCSTF and is primarily focused on investigating criminal activity impacting the railroad, including transnational cargo theft, robbery, burglary, crimes against persons, organized criminal activity, cartel-linked offenses targeting the transportation industry, and other threats to BNSF Railway's operations, employees, customers, and critical infrastructure.

To learn more about our BNSF Police team, please view this video: BNSF Police

This is a full-time position located in Riverside, California.

Travel is required and can be extensive depending on the operational assignment.

Training for this position is at both corporate headquarters in Fort Worth, TX and on-site at location with an internal trainer.

Relocation package may be provided for the eligible candidate.

Role Description

The Task Force Officer (TFO) will serve as BNSF Police Department's representative assigned to the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Inland Violent Crime Suppression Task Force (IVCSTF). Working in partnership with federal, state, and local law enforcement agencies, the TFO will investigate, disrupt, and support the prosecution of individuals and criminal organizations responsible for violent crimes and other offenses impacting the railroad, BNSF employees, customers, and critical supply chain infrastructure.

This assignment requires a full-time commitment to the task force and dual coordination with the FBI and BNSF Police Department Special Investigations and Training Division. The position combines complex criminal investigations, intelligence gathering, field enforcement activities, and multi-agency operational support. Primary areas of focus include transnational cargo theft, robbery, burglary, crimes against persons, cartel-linked criminal activity targeting the rail industry, violent offenders, fugitives, firearms offenses, and other criminal activity affecting BNSF Railway operations and assets.

Key responsibilities may include:

  • Conducting and leading complex criminal investigations involving cargo theft, organized crime, transnational criminal organizations, railroad-related offenses, threats to critical infrastructure, and other crimes impacting BNSF operations. This includes identifying offenders, developing investigative strategies, executing enforcement actions, preparing case documentation, obtaining judicial authorizations, and supporting prosecution efforts through court testimony and case presentation.

  • Serving as a subject matter expert and liaison between BNSF Police and federal, state, local, tribal, and international law enforcement partners. Represents BNSF interests through regular coordination, intelligence sharing, operational planning, deconfliction efforts, and executive-level briefings with law enforcement and company leadership.

  • Participating in and supporting multi-agency operations, task force initiatives, and special assignments that may involve multiple jurisdictions, states, or international partners. Provides operational, logistical, and investigative support to ensure successful execution of enforcement activities and mission objectives.

  • Maintaining compliance with all task force requirements, security clearances, training standards, and Memoranda of Understanding established between BNSF, the FBI, Department of Justice, Department of Homeland Security, and other partner agencies.

  • Monitoring emerging crime trends, intelligence, and threat information affecting the railroad industry and supply chain. Develops strategic recommendations, promotes continuous improvement, and supports BNSF readiness during elevated threat conditions, critical incidents, and specialized operational deployments.

  • Preparing detailed investigative reports, maintaining regulatory and audit-related records, safeguarding sensitive information, and providing accurate, timely communication to FBI leadership, BNSF Police leadership, prosecutors, and other stakeholders regarding investigative activities and outcomes.

  • Providing investigative guidance, consultation, and support to BNSF Police personnel, company officials, and partner agencies, while responding to major incidents, after-hours calls, and other operational needs as required.

When conducting investigative duties and supporting patrol operations, work is conducted in a safety sensitive environment where the working conditions can include diverse and extreme weather conditions, walking and performing work on uneven surfaces, working around loud noises, fumes, and heavy/moving machinery.

The duties and responsibilities in this posting are representative categories to be used in deciding whether to apply for this position. This is not an exhaustive list of the position’s duties and could be subject to change.

At BNSF Railway, we encourage individuals from all backgrounds to apply, showcasing their skills, experiences and development. We provide resources and tools to help you reach your full potential, fostering a supportive and inclusive environment.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Does not require BNSF's assistance (whether monetary, through sponsorship, or otherwise) now or in the future to obtain, maintain, or extend employment authorization (including H-1B, STEM OPT/CPT, or TN nonimmigrant status).

  • High School diploma or GED.

  • Minimum of five (5) years of law enforcement experience, including at least three (3) years of service with the BNSF Police Department and/or two (2) years of leadership experience with a prior law enforcement agency.

  • Eighteen (18) months of successful experience as a full-time peace officer with a city, county, state federal or railroad law enforcement agency.

  • Successfully completed basic law enforcement training at a recognized state-certified police academy.

  • Must meet or able to meet peace officer commissioning standards in state in which this job is posted and be commissioned as such and maintain a valid State Peace Office License in that state.

  • Must meet all BNSF Police Department requirements and standards for appointment as a Special Agent.

  • Must have a valid driver’s license.

  • Must be physically and psychologically fit for duty, successfully pass all required company evaluations, and pass an extensive background investigation.

  • Must be able to obtain and maintain a Top Secret security clearance.

  • Must meet and maintain all state, federal, company, and task force training, qualification, and retention standards, including annual firearms proficiency and other required law enforcement certifications.

  • Must possess a broad knowledge of criminal law, criminal procedure, and investigative practices.

  • Must possess a working knowledge of railroad operations and transportation-related security risks, including emergency response and incident management.

  • Must demonstrate the ability to lead and coordinate personnel and resources in complex, high-pressure, or critical incident environments.

  • Must be proficient in the use of computer systems, investigative databases, and report-writing applications.

  • Must be willing and able to travel as required and respond to after-hours calls, major incidents, emergency deployments, and operational assignments.

  • Must successfully complete all required company, federal task force, and security-related training associated with the position.

  • Must live or be willing to relocate within 50 miles of the assigned work location.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree.

  • Prior experience as a detective/investigator.

  • Prior experience working as a Task Force Officer (TFO).

  • Experience investigating cargo theft, organized crime, transnational criminal organizations, or other complex criminal enterprises.

  • Experience working closely with federal law enforcement agencies and prosecutors.

  • Current or prior eligibility for a Top Secret security clearance.

  • Strong investigative case management, intelligence gathering, and executive briefing skills.

Union:

  • Allied Services Division, Transportation-Communications Union

  • Dues required per union agreement

At BNSF, you will have access to a comprehensive and competitive benefits package including:

  • An industry-leading 401(k) and renowned Railroad Retirement program.
  • A range of robust health care options for you and your dependents (including domestic partners), including medical, dental, vision, telemedicine, mental health, cancer support, and high-quality care network options.
  • Health care spending accounts (HSA) with employer contributions, as well as life and disability insurance, provided at no cost.
  • Family benefits including parental, pediatric and family building support, adoption and surrogacy reimbursement, and dependent care spending account (with employer match).
  • Access to discounts on travel, gym memberships, counseling services and wellness support.
  • Annual bonus (Incentive Compensation Program)
  • Generous leave / time off policies.
  • For more information, visit Benefits.

title: Civil Structures Lead
description:
You’ll connect Queensland. We’ll connect you to an amazing career.

Our team of over 7,500 and our customers are central to everything we do, we have a proud history as a safe and reliable railway operator, with a commitment to ensuring that our operating systems reflect the highest standards. Queensland Rail inspires innovative thought, passionate motivation, teamwork, and forward thinking, where our people can achieve their own career aspirations.


Why Queensland Rail?

We will provide you with an exciting and diverse career opportunity to join a company that continues to strive in the delivery of a modern and world-class railway provider, you will be able to lead and apply your innovative thoughts to enhance our rail network. For this role we also offer:

  • Highly competitive salary plus 12.75% super
  • Opportunity to be part of a major legacy project.
  • Join a rail industry leader.
  • Collaborative and engaged workplace and team environment.
  • Genuine work life balance
  • Free Citytrain travel to and from work and access to other free or discounted SEQ rail travel.
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP) providing employees with holistic and contemporary health and wellbeing programs.

About this role:

Entering Queensland Rail’s Major Projects division, you will be working on The Wave Greenfield Stage 2 Project as a Civil Structures Lead.

This role provides a critical technical assurance and coordination function, ensuring structural infrastructure is safe, compliant, fit-for-purpose and operationally effective. Working within a complex multi-disciplinary environment, you will collaborate with designers, contractors, project teams and stakeholders to coordinate technical interfaces, review, and assure project deliverables, manage risks and issues and support the successful delivery of structural infrastructure across all project phases.

Your expertise will help ensure project outcomes align with operational requirements, technical standards, and business objectives, contributing to the delivery of a transformative rail infrastructure project for South East Queensland.

About this Opportunity:

This fixed term opportunity is available through to 31 January 2032, offering the successful candidate the opportunity to contribute to a landmark rail infrastructure project.

You will work within a flexible and collaborative environment, supporting project delivery across Queensland Rail's Carseldine and Brisbane CBD offices, Transport and Main Roads offices, stakeholder locations, and project sites. The successful candidate will demonstrate the adaptability and flexibility required to work effectively across these environments, supporting project delivery and stakeholder engagement.

You can expect some of your responsibilities to include:

  • Manage the delivery of the structural engineering works, coordinating delivery, safety, cost and quality outcomes to meet business needs and expectations.
  • Ensure project teams demonstrate professional integrity and sound engineering practice in the development and delivery of structural engineering solutions that meet operational requirements and project objectives.
  • Build and manage relationships with clients, customers, project managers and other stakeholders to facilitate effective structural engineering strategies and governance procedures and where applicable, build capability.
  • Provide program status and outcomes to meet business requirements and to support the development, of accurate and timely program reporting.
  • Ensure structural engineering interfaces are managed including internal delivery, outsourced work and delivery partners interfacing significantly to ensure customer needs are met throughout the project.
  • Achieve the Wave targets, objectives, performance measures, and safety responsibilities, while continually seeking opportunities to improve project performance and innovation outcomes.

What you can bring to the role:

  • Demonstrated expertise in Design, Renewals, Implementation, Testing and Commissioning of rail infrastructure, particularly civil structures, to support safe, reliable, and sustainable railway operations.
  • High level interpersonal, communication, planning, coordination, and negotiation skills to manage, design and document safe and sustainable structural engineering outcomes, particularly:
    • Rail infrastructure works or rail related infrastructure.
    • Maintenance of infrastructure.
    • Asset maintenance.
  • Proven ability to provide technical leadership, specialist advice, and influence across multidisciplinary teams of professional engineers, technical specialists, and project stakeholders.
  • Strong knowledge of statutory, regulatory and policy obligations, to satisfy operational, safety, environment and contractual requirements and processes within a complex rail infrastructure environment.
  • Substantial level of skill in delivering safe, quality, commercial outcomes through business improvements, technology development, and innovation.

For further information on the role, click HERE to read the position description.

Progress that Counts

Joining Queensland Rail means being part of an exciting future where you will welcome millions of international passengers for the 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games. Our Cross River Rail project will transform travel across the South East Queensland network, doubling passenger journeys to 80 million over the next decade.

To support this growth and enhance customer experiences, we're committed to key initiatives, including The Wave project for the Sunshine Coast along with Beerburrum to Nambour upgrade, building three new Gold Coastline stations, implementing the $5.75 billion Logan and Gold Coast Faster Rail Project, introducing 65 new Next Generation Rolling Stock trains, improving station accessibility at eight main stations, boosting North Coast Line capacity and upgrading Central Station.

Your journey matters. Make it with us.

There has never been a more exciting time within Queensland Rail. We offer boundless opportunities to support your career today and for your future.

Apply for our role via our website by clicking the apply button before 11.59pm Monday, November 23rd, 2026

To learn more about this career opportunity, please contact James Conlan via email at james.conlan@qr.com.au

We are a team of thousands and we are proud of our individual journeys and stories. And as we grow, we need more diverse backgrounds and perspectives than ever before. title: Donor Engagement Manager
description:
About the Food Bank of South Jersey
The Food Bank of South Jersey believes that no one should go to bed hungry. Since 1985, it has served the children, families, and seniors of Burlington, Camden, Gloucester, and Salem counties by distributing safe and healthy food, providing nutrition education and cooking courses, and developing sustainable pathways for neighbors to improve their lives. A 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization and member of Feeding America, FBSJ distributed nearly 24 million meals in 2025, through direct distributions and its network of more than 200 partner agencies.

To learn more about how you can become a valued part of the FBSJ team, dedicated to building community awareness and creating an efficient emergency food distribution network to eliminate hunger, visit .

Position Summary

The Donor Engagement Manager serves as a primary relationship development and stewardship lead for the Food Sourcing department, working in partnership with Food Sourcing Coordinators, who manage day-to-day donor and sourcing activities within their respective channels and with the Sr Manager of Food Sourcing on donor strategy and operational alignment. This role is responsible for acquiring, developing, cultivating, and expanding food donor partnerships that support the Food Bank of South Jersey’s sourcing goals. Working closely with Food Sourcing, Operations, and cross-functional teams, the position ensures donor opportunities align with organizational priorities, operational capacity, and mission impact.
The role serves as an ambassador for Food Sourcing, representing FBSJ at community, industry, donor, and partner events while fostering relationships that strengthen the organization’s food sourcing network and mission impact.

Core Responsibilities

• Develop, cultivate, and expand relationships with existing, prospective, and lapsed food donors, industry partners, and community organizations.
• Contribute to and execute on donor acquisition, engagement, stewardship, recognition, retention, and reactivation strategies.
• Build relationships that support sustainable growth and diversification of the Food Sourcing network.
• Represent the Food Bank at donor, community, industry, and networking events.
• Collaborate with internal stakeholders to support successful implementation of donation programs and partnership initiatives.
• Maintain donor relationship management systems, records, and engagement tracking.
• Support the strategic goals of the Food Sourcing department.

Donor Relationship Management

• Establish and maintain a structured schedule of donor visits, meetings, stewardship activities, and relationship-building opportunities.
• Identify opportunities to increase donor participation, donation frequency, retention, and overall engagement.
• Coordinate donor appreciation, recognition, cultivation, and reactivation initiatives.
• Maintain accurate donor contact records, relationship histories, engagement plans, and pipeline activity.
• Conduct donor outreach and prospecting activities consistent with organizational priorities and operational capacity.
• Serve as a relationship resource and ambassador for food donors across the Food Sourcing portfolio.

Collaboration and Operational Alignment

• Provide relationship development and stewardship support to Food Sourcing Coordinators across retail, industry, food drive, and community donor channels, while respecting established channel responsibilities and day-to-day donor ownership.
• Work with both Food Sourcing Sr. Manger and Coordinators to identify donor growth, retention, and engagement opportunities and determine appropriate relationship strategies, follow-up, and support.
• Collaborate with Operations leadership and Food Sourcing team to evaluate and prioritize donation opportunities based on capacity, cost, mission impact, and organizational goals.
• Maintain regular communication with stakeholders regarding large-scale donations, special events, and strategic initiatives.
• Provide donor-related insights and recommendations during planning, sourcing, and operational meetings.
• Support the coordinated development of donor relationships across departments as organizational needs and sourcing priorities evolve.

Donor Education and Compliance

• Promote donor adherence to Feeding America standards, food safety requirements, and organizational policies through education, communication, and training.
• Conduct individual and group donor training sessions on donation guidelines, food safety standards, and operational procedures.
• Support the development of donor training materials and educational resources.

Community and Industry Engagement

• Participate in community events, trade associations, conferences, donor meetings, food drives, media opportunities, public speaking engagements, tours, and donor recognition activities.
• Identify and develop partnership opportunities that strengthen and diversify the Food Sourcing network.
• Collaborate with Communications, Development, Programs, and Community Engagement teams to maximize donor and partner engagement opportunities.

Reporting and Data Management

• Monitor donor activity, donation trends, performance metrics, and engagement outcomes to identify opportunities for relationship growth and follow-up.
• Maintain documentation and reporting consistent with organizational requirements.
• Assist with reports, presentations, and leadership communications as needed.

Leadership Capabilities

• Builds and maintains trusted relationships with donors, community leaders, and industry partners.
• Fosters teamwork and collaboration across departments and external stakeholders.
• Identifies opportunities for donor growth, process improvement, and partnership development.
• Communicates organizational priorities, donor impact, and mission outcomes effectively.
• Demonstrates sound judgment, initiative, problem-solving ability, and attention to detail.
• Represents FBSJ and the Food Sourcing department with professionalism, responsiveness, and a strong commitment to donor service and mission impact.

Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in business, marketing, supply chain, nonprofit management, or a related field, OR an equivalent combination of education and at least four (4) years of progressively responsible experience in the food industry (such as food retail, wholesale, manufacturing, distribution, or food banking/food sourcing) or other sales or relationship management experience, including non-donor-related experience.
• Minimum of three (3) years of experience in donor or account relationship management, business development, or food procurement/sourcing; experience working with food donors, retailers, manufacturers, or distributors strongly preferred.
• Working knowledge of food safety standards and donation handling requirements
• Proficiency with donor/customer relationship management databases (e.g., Salesforce) and Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook).
• Excellent written and verbal communication, presentation, and negotiation skills, with the ability to represent the organization professionally to donors, partners, and the community.
• Strong organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple relationships, priorities, and deadlines independently.
• Valid driver’s license with an acceptable driving record, and reliable transportation for local travel to donor sites, partner locations, and events throughout the four-county service area.
• Ability to work a flexible schedule, including occasional early mornings, evenings, and weekends, to attend donor and community events.

Behavioral Competencies

  • Adaptability: adapts well to changes in assignments and priorities; adapts behavior or work methods in response to new information, changing conditions, or unexpected obstacles; approaches change positively and adjusts behaviors accordingly.
  • Community/Client Focus: Makes the community and clients and their needs a primary focus of one’s actions; shows interest in and understanding the needs and expectations of internal and external customers (including team members); demonstrates the ability to understand, engage with, and meet the needs of the community or clients they serve.
  • Commitment to Encouraging a Supportive Environment: Actively embracing and fostering a workplace or organizational culture that values and respects the differences among individuals and strives to create an environment where everyone feels included, valued, and has a sense of belonging.
  • Decision Making: the ability to make sound, timely, and effective decisions. Is effective in the process of gathering relevant information, assessing options, and choosing the most appropriate course of action to achieve desired outcomes across various contexts.
  • Results Orientation: the ability to focus on achieving specific outcomes and goals. Setting clear objectives, efficiently planning and executing tasks, and measuring success based on tangible results. Demonstrating a commitment to delivering outcomes, meeting targets, and driving performance.

Technical Competencies

  • Strategic Relationship Building and Management (Existing and Developing)
  • Business Development
  • Knowledge Of Database Systems (Salesforce, Capital CRM, QuickBooks, etc.)
  • Compliance of Food Safety Standards
  • External Communication Skills (with partners and clients)
  • Stakeholder Management

The Food Bank of South Jersey believes in pay transparency and fostering an environment of fairness. The salary for this position is $70,000, commensurate with experience and qualifications.Our approach to compensation is rooted in valuing the expertise and contributions of all our team members.

The Food Bank of South Jersey is an equal opportunity employer. All aspects of employment – including the decision to hire, promote, discipline, or discharge – will be based on merit, competence, performance, and business needs. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, marital status, age, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran status, or any other status protected under federal, state, or local law. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment. We believe and support the safety and security of all of our volunteers and our employees. Background checks will be completed for final candidates.

title: Senior IBM i (AS/400) Storage Replication & High Availability Engineer
description:
Unleash resilient core banking capabilities — elevate high-availability solutions on IBM i!

EU-based opportunity with remote work model.

As a Senior IBM i (AS/400) Storage Replication & High Availability Engineer, you will be working for our client, a leader in the banking industry, focusing on safeguarding and optimizing their core banking system. You will play a critical role in implementing a cutting-edge, storage-based replication setup for a highly available, disaster-resilient environment, helping the client achieve seamless data integrity and operational continuity.

Your main responsibilities:

  • Implement storage-based replication solutions between two IBM i sites, adhering to the design specifications in collaboration with IBM and key stakeholders.
  • Configure and test SAN and fiber link setups, including initial synchronization, cutover, and failover procedures.
  • Manage migration from MIMIX replication, ensuring data consistency and minimal disruption during transition.
  • Develop and deploy monitoring and alert systems for real-time detection of replication issues.
  • Provide expert advice on moving towards active-active configurations or higher availability architectures and assist in their implementation.
  • Create detailed runbooks for switchover, failback, and troubleshooting replication failures for operational handover.
  • Coordinate with Safra’s change management processes, ensuring compliance when touching core banking systems.

You are ideal for this role if you have:

  • 7+ years of experience in IBM i (AS/400) systems administration and real-world delivery of IBM i replication projects.
  • Proven hands-on experience with storage-based replication technologies such as IASP, PowerHA SystemMirror for i, and SAN-level copy solutions like Metro Mirror or Global Mirror.
  • Strong troubleshooting skills with logical replication tools like Precisely MIMIX or Maxava, capable of safely decommissioning or upgrading solutions.
  • Experience in HA/DR design, testing, switchover, failover, and failback processes tailored to regulated banking environments.
  • Fluent English for effective collaboration with US teams, IBM, and Jack Henry.

It’s a strong plus if you have:

  • Experience with IBM Power hardware and IBM Storage solutions (FlashSystem, DS8000).
  • Scripting or tooling expertise for replication health checks and alerting systems (CL, SQL services).
  • Prior work with French or other European banks running AS/400 cores.
  • Relevant IBM i or PowerHA certifications.

Language Required for the role: English (Fluent)
Eligibility to work in Europe: Only candidates with an existing legal right to work in the European Union will be considered for this role.

title: QC Tech 3
description:
Ensuring Chart’s Success…

The New Iberia facility specializes in cold box assembly and fabrication, pressure vessels and other cryogenic equipment as used for the air separation and hydrocarbon industries. The end users of this equipment include all the major LNG, petrochemical and air separation engineering on a worldwide basis. The facility is located at the Port of Iberia.

What Will You Do?

Inspect material for quality and quantity by completing dimensional checks once the material has been received.

Reject and notify management of defects.

Use policies and procedures of the Quality Manual to ensure proper welding procedures are being followed.

Plan for and cause system and document changes to agree with the requirements of ISO 9001 such that will achieve certification and will maintain certification thereafter.

Maintain a Job material traceability program and retain material tracing records for all jobs.

Oversee compliance with ASME requirements in manufacturing and welding.

Oversee inspection processes carried out by either Quality Control Department or Production personnel and maintain records resulting from such processes.

Oversee NDE processes and records.

Required to work at elevated heights up to 75ft.

High school diploma or equivalent.

Ten years’ experience in related position.

College degree preferred.

Train or cause training of his directs reports and will supervise the activities and assignments of Quality Control personnel.

Maintain quality records for each project and be prepared to submit records to customer when requested.

Utilize American Society of Quality Control recommended procedures or equivalent to perform supplier audits for new and continuing suppliers for materials.

Maintain a log of calibration requirements and dates of calibration and periodic re-calibration for measuring tools.

Compile and issue Job Quality Assurance documents for each job and verify completion of the job documents, then archive the documents.

Oversee pressure testing of cold box systems and verify the results of the testing.

Oversee weld mapping, monitoring and weld testing for all products produced that require welding during manufacturing.

Maintain the corrective action program to include Non Conformance Reports (NCR) and the results of frequent barrier code problems.

title: Apartment Service Manager
description:
Service Manager

Lead Maintenance Excellence. Build Strong Teams. Create Exceptional Resident Experiences.

Stoa Group is seeking a full-time Service Manager to lead maintenance operations at one of our multifamily communities. At Stoa Group, being a manager is much more than sitting behind a desk directing others. We believe in leading by example and walking in the shoes of the people you supervise.

As a Service Manager, you will work alongside your team to maintain the community, respond to service requests, manage vendors, and build strong relationships with residents. You will serve as the technical expert for the community while leading a team of maintenance professionals to ensure the property remains safe, attractive, and well-maintained for our residents.

What You'll Do

Maintenance Operations & Technical Leadership

  • Oversee and perform maintenance and repairs involving HVAC, plumbing, electrical, appliances, carpentry, painting, and general building systems.
  • Serve as the community's technical expert while providing training and guidance to maintenance team members.
  • Ensure maintenance issues are resolved efficiently and in accordance with company standards.
  • Manage vendor relationships and oversee contractor work to ensure quality service and timely completion.

Resident Service & Community Experience

  • Build positive relationships with residents by providing exceptional customer service and professional communication.
  • Respond promptly to service requests and prioritize maintenance needs to maximize resident satisfaction.
  • Clearly communicate repair timelines, maintenance processes, and updates to residents.
  • Follow through on commitments and ensure residents feel valued and supported throughout the service process.

Apartment Turns & Property Readiness

  • Monitor apartment vacancies and oversee the make-ready process, including painting, cleaning, repairs, and inspections.
  • Ensure vacant apartments are completed on schedule and prepared for new residents.
  • Collaborate with community leadership to minimize vacancy downtime and maintain occupancy goals.

Preventive Maintenance & Asset Preservation

  • Implement and oversee preventive maintenance programs designed to extend equipment life and reduce costly repairs.
  • Conduct routine inspections of buildings, grounds, amenities, and common areas to identify maintenance needs proactively.
  • Maintain curb appeal and ensure the community consistently meets company standards for cleanliness and safety.

Team Leadership & Emergency Response

  • Lead, coach, and develop onsite maintenance team members.
  • Foster a culture of teamwork, accountability, professionalism, and service excellence.
  • Participate in a rotating on-call schedule and respond to after-hours emergencies when needed.

What We're Looking For

Required Qualifications

  • Five (5) or more years of hands-on maintenance experience.
  • Current EPA Certification.
  • Supervisory experience leading onsite maintenance teams.
  • Strong working knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, electrical, appliance repair, carpentry, and general maintenance operations.
  • Availability to work a flexible schedule, including weekends.
  • Ability to participate in a rotating on-call schedule for after-hours emergencies.
  • Demonstrated proficiency with computers, including word processing, calendar management, and property management software.
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation.

Preferred Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent.
  • HVAC experience.
  • Certified Pool Operator (CPO) Certification.
  • Mold Certification.
  • Ability to earn and maintain future industry certifications as required by EPA, OSHA, and other industry standards.

Core Competencies

  • Maintenance operations
  • Technical troubleshooting
  • Team leadership and development
  • Preventive maintenance
  • Vendor management
  • Resident relations
  • Customer service
  • Communication
  • Organization and planning
  • Problem-solving
  • Accountability
  • Safety and compliance

What Will Make You Successful

We're looking for someone who:

  • Leads by example and is willing to work alongside the team.
  • Takes ownership of the community and approaches challenges like an owner.
  • Remains calm and solution-oriented during maintenance emergencies.
  • Builds trust with residents through exceptional service and follow-through.
  • Communicates clearly and effectively with residents, vendors, and teammates.
  • Anticipates maintenance needs before they become larger problems.
  • Maintains high standards for safety, cleanliness, and community appearance.
  • Thrives in a fast-paced environment while effectively managing multiple priorities.

Our Values

Every Stoa team member is expected to operate by three core principles:

Quality Do it right the first time.

Schedule Execution, not excuses.

Relationships Do what you say you're going to do.

If these values describe how you work, you'll fit in well at Stoa.

Why Stoa?

Stoa Group was established in 2017 to develop, build, and manage large-scale multifamily communities throughout the Gulf Coast and Southeast. As a vertically integrated organization, we take pride in creating exceptional resident experiences while developing outstanding teams and long-term careers.

Our Service Managers play a critical role in protecting our communities, developing maintenance talent, and delivering exceptional service to our residents. At Stoa, you'll have the opportunity to make a direct impact on community performance while working for an organization built on accountability, collaboration, and growth.

What We Offer

  • Retirement plan with company match
  • Paid time off and paid holidays
  • 100% employer-paid health insurance for employees
  • Dental and vision insurance
  • Employee rental discount
  • Professional development opportunities

title: Letter Carrier - Delivery Agent and Postal Clerk
description:
Job Requisition Id: 205400
Business Function: Delivery Agent or Letter Carrier
Primary City: Kenora
Other Location(s):
Province: Ontario
Employment Type: Temporary - New
Employment Status: Temporary
Language Requirement: English or French Essential (Either/OR)
Number of Vacancies 2
Salary: $25.37

Job Description

Canada Post is an exciting place to work! And you can be part of it!

We deliver billions of items to Canadians each year – you can be a big part of making this happen.

In this role, you may be called upon to do on-call delivery agent OR on-call postal clerk work:


• On-call delivery agent (also known as a letter carrier). You’ll be the face of Canada Post in your community and make sure customers and businesses get the mail and parcels they’re waiting for.

• On-call postal clerk- you will have the opportunity to work various shifts, including days, evenings, overnights and weekends. This temporary on-call position is an excellent opportunity to learn about the business of mail operations, as well as the great jobs available at Canada Post.

Job Responsibilities

As a Delivery Agent-What will you do?

• You’ll start your day in the depot, sorting and preparing the day’s deliveries

• You’ll load and drive a Canada Post postal vehicle

• You’ll then spend most of your day outside, delivering mail and packages by foot or by vehicle to customers on your route

• You’ll return to the depot to unload the day’s incoming mail and packages for later delivery

Job Responsibilities (continued)

As a Postal Clerk-What will you do?

• You’ll work inside a sorting facility, sorting mail and packages

• Work various shifts (may include evenings/nights and weekends)

• Operation of material handling equipment

• Receiving and accepting mail items

• Sort, scan and sequence and batch mail items

• Transfers and dispatching of parcels and packets

• Perform other postal clerk duties as required

• Completes reports and documentation

Qualifications

What must you have?

• A valid Class 5 or Class G driver’s licence with a safe driving record for at least 3 years (driver's abstract required)

• The physical ability to lift mail items weighing up to 22.7 kg (50 lb) and carry items weighing up to 15.9 kg (35 lb) regularly throughout the day

• The ability to work in all types of weather

• The availability to be on-call, possibly evenings and weekends

• The ability to read, write and speak English and/or French

These help, too!


• Experience in customer service

• Experience making deliveries or working as a driver

• Experience working in a production environment is an asset

In return, we offer:


• Competitive pay

• Extensive classroom and on-the-job training about your duties and safety on the job

• Opportunities for permanent employment

Other Information

Today’s Canada Post - Canada Post is an e-commerce powerhouse, delivering billions of items every year. We help small businesses grow. We enrich lives in remote communities. We connect Canadians with each other and to the rest of the world. And we do all this by providing residential and business customers with the best possible delivery experience in the country.


We like to promote from within and can offer you a career rather than a job. While, like all of our delivery agents, you’ll start out on a temporary, on-call basis, you’ll have the opportunity to grow with us and obtain a permanent position … even try out new jobs in different areas of the company.

Canada Post’s values and behaviours

Our Values - Trust, Respect and Deliver represent our fundamental promise to ourselves, our expectations of one and another and our shared duty to our country.

Our behaviours – Make the call, Know the destination, Deliver for others, Ignite our pride; embody our values, bringing them to life and guiding our actions.

We’re committed to living these values and practicing these behaviours every day. Learn more about the values and behaviours by visiting the Canada Post website.

title: Employment Specialist
description:
The Employment Specialist is a highly engaged and mission-driven role that provides one-on-one support services to navigate employment process for adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD). This position is ideal for someone who thrives on meaningful connection and purposeful structure—providing hands-on support and advocacy while also developing personalized, goal-driven activities that foster learning, independence, and community integration.

Overview
The Employment Specialist role involves working directly with clients to assess job readiness, develop career plans, and connect them with employment opportunities that align with their skills and goals. This is a part-time position with the possibility of full-time.

Employment Readiness & Client Assessment
  • Maintain an active assignment list of individuals receiving services through DDA who are seeking competitive employment
  • Conduct a comprehensive assessment to understand each person’s strengths, needs, preferences, support systems, and employment interests
  • Complete intake assessments to determine employment readiness, barriers, and vocational goals
  • Develop individualized employment plans in collaboration with each person supported
  • Prepare professional vocational profiles to guide the job development process
Job Development & Community Engagement
  • Visit and engage local community to identify and negotiate work experiences (informational interviews, job shadows, situational assessments, job tryouts).
  • Identify job openings aligned with each client’s skills, interests, and career goals
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with employers, community organizations, and workforce partners
  • Attend community events, job fairs, and networking opportunities to promote the agency and expand employment opportunities
  • Advocate for individuals with IDD and help negotiate job offers and accommodations when needed.
Skill Development & Employment Preparation
  • Provide support with resume writing, job application completion, and career exploration
  • Conduct mock interviews, role-playing, and workplace etiquette training to build confidence and increase job readiness
  • Provide travel training to help individuals gain independence in commuting to and from work
On-the-Job Support & Coaching
  • Deliver on-site and off-site job coaching to ensure successful integration and retention
  • Provide systematic instruction to teach job tasks, build workplace routines, and promote independence
  • Collaborate with employers to develop support fade-out plans and ensure long-term success.
  • Support clients in developing positive workplace relationships with coworkers and supervisors.
Documentation, Reporting & Communication
  • Complete all required documentation including daily notes, attendance records, employment forms, and progress updates.
  • Track measurable outcomes such as employment placements, retention, and skill development.
  • Prepare and submit reports for internal teams, DDA, and other stakeholders.
Collaboration & Professional Development
  • Participate in internal and external meetings to support client success and program growth.
  • Maintain strong communication with all team members involved in a person’s support network.
  • Complete and pass all required training, including ACRE and/or the CESP certification, and renew training as required.
  • Engage in ongoing learning and professional development opportunities.
Education
  • Minimum an Associate degree with 5+ years of relevant experience in IDD services, case management, or housing support
Experience
  • Experience with knowledge of workforce development, vocational rehabilitation, job placement, or career counseling
  • Knowledge of local labor market trends and community employment resources
  • Background in providing on-site job coaching, workplace accommodations, and employment retention support is preferred
Certifications & Licenses
  • Valid Maryland driver’s license with a clean driving record and reliable transportation.
  • Must have the ACRE (Association of Community Rehabilitation Educators), CSEP (Certified Employment Support Professional) preferred
Working Conditions
  • Work occurs in virtual and community settings, including client homes and/or work sites
  • Frequent local travel required; must have reliable transportation
  • Flexible daytime schedule to accommodate evening/weekend commitments
  • Administrative duties include documentation, reporting, and meetings using standard computer equipment.
  • Collaborative, fast-paced environment focused on inclusion and client support.
Compensation: $20/hour
Preferred Additional Qualifications
  • Frederick, MD
  • Bilingual capabilities
  • Background in disability advocacy or services
  • Experience with assistive technology and communication devices
  • Knowledge of evidence-based practices in skill development and community integration.

Title: Senior Camera Tuning Engineer

Role:

  • Own the full tuning chain: black level, lens shading, defect correction, demosaic, noise reduction, sharpening, color matrices, gamma, tone mapping, and overall look
  • Tune 3A (exposure, white balance, flicker) on a wearable platform where convergence behavior during rapid lighting transitions matters more than steady-state accuracy
  • Make low light work without optical stabilization, using multi-frame techniques that respect a strict power budget
  • Handle motion, including ghosting and fusion artifacts from a head-mounted camera that is always moving
  • Build the measurement methodology for model-facing image quality, scoring tuning on downstream task accuracy, and determine whether to ship one tuning or two
  • Define what gets calibrated on every unit in production versus what ships as a single golden tuning
  • Stand up objective and subjective validation, with regression tracking that holds up against a release schedule


Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of camera tuning experience, including at least two shipped products tuned end to end
  • Deep hands-on experience with a vendor tuning toolchain
  • Fluency across the full ISP blockchain, able to look at an image and name the block responsible
  • Hands-on 3A tuning experience, not only 3A configuration
  • Knowledge of objective IQ methodology and standards, including ISO 12233, ISO 15739, ISO 14524, and CPIQ
  • Lab experience with controlled illuminants, chart-based measurement, uniform sources, and reflectance targets
  • Proficiency in Python or MATLAB
  • Ability to defend a tuning decision with data, and change it when the data changes


Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience with Qualcomm Spectra and Chromatix
  • Experience tuning or evaluating imagery for machine-learning consumption
  • Low-light and multi-frame tuning without optical stabilization
  • Wearable, action camera, automotive, or other non-handset tuning experience
  • Experience with Imatest, DXO Analyzer, or Image Engineering toolchains
  • Experience standing up a tuning lab from scratch

title: Patient Service Representative
description:
Come join our team! We are hiring!

We are currently hiring a Patient Service Representative in Milwaukee, WI. This is a full-time position.

Why Progressive Community Health Centers?
Founded in 1999, Progressive Community Health Centers is an independent non-profit organization that operates four clinic locations in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. More than 100 employees support our agency's mission to improve the health and quality of life of the community by providing culturally competent services that address identified needs. We provide high quality, comprehensive care to roughly 16,000 patients annually, a majority of who are low-income. No one is ever turned away from our clinics based on insurance status or ability to pay. We value a patient-centered philosophy and provide range of services that include family medicine, internal medicine, women's health, urgent care, dental, radiology and integrated behavioral health. We also offer supportive services such as case management, health education and benefits enrollment.

Summary

The Patient Service Representative (PSR) performs those tasks that occur early in the revenue cycle process. It is these functions that have an early impact on patient experience and revenue outcomes. The primary role of the PSR is to optimize registration, and appointment scheduling and support in-network referrals. Performs a variety of cross-functional clerical and patient support duties including telephone registration, scheduling, clerical administrative duties, and/or data entry duties. PSRs are responsible for greeting and assessing patients in need of services, performing data collection, and providing patient education. Also, directs patients and visitors to appropriate areas and assists with patient flow.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

  1. Greets patients and visitors and responds to routine requests for information. Answers telephone, screen calls, and takes messages.
  2. Registers patients; obtains demographic and insurance information; verifies insurance coverage, collects co-pays, deductibles, and previous balances; posts payments and updates demographic and insurance information.
  3. Schedules patient appointments and coordinates cancellations, reschedules, and additions to schedules. Provides accurate, detailed information regarding test preparations, time patient to arrive, and any other directional information needed by the patient.
  4. Recommend the next best actions or cross-promotional opportunities to patients to educate them on appropriate additional services or health education campaigns.
  5. Document and provide feedback from callers to the appropriate parties for follow-up and/or resolution. Elevate the voice of patient opportunities to Trainers and Supervisors for implementation in training and/or centralized knowledgebase.
  6. Assist patients in enrolling and increasing customer utilization of MyChart App (EPIC EMR).
  7. Coordinates the scheduling of more complex patient appointments, tests, and procedures. Instructs the patient on pre- and post-procedure protocols (i.e. medication guidelines, food/beverage consumption guidelines, check-in procedures, directions to facilities, etc.).
  8. Updates insurance, financial responsibility, and other data when changes or additions occur, and communicates to patient as appropriate. Ensures insurance and patient information obtained is complete and accurate, applying acquired knowledge of government and third-party payor requirements.
  9. Identifies, reports, and resolves problems regarding registration or authorizations to appropriate individuals and departments.
  10. Monitors patient flow to ensure they are cared for most efficiently and courteously. Offers various assistance to patients including arranging transportation needs, providing directions, locating wheelchairs, etc.
  11. Performs visit closure including checking out patients after visits, scheduling follow-up appointments, and providing patients with a visit summary.
  12. Perform other job-related duties as may be assigned.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:

This position requires a High School diploma or equivalent education with 1 year of healthcare experience. Working knowledge of Medicaid, Medicare, and Commercial health plans is required. Experience with Epic practice management system preferred but not required. The ability to work with various cultural, ethnic, and socio-economic populations. Able to work in a fast-paced, team environment that requires accuracy and attention to detail.


It is mandatory that all employees, employed providers and volunteers are vaccinated. All hired candidates must submit proof of vaccination prior to their orientation. This is a mandatory requirement for Progressive Community Health Centers. The purpose is to minimize exposure to and transmission of the influenza virus in the workplace by providing occupational protection to employees and thereby preventing exposure to members of the community, which we serve.

title: Senior/Principal Software Systems Engineer - Software Test Engineer for High Confidence System Environments, Onsite
description:
About Sandia

Sandia National Laboratories is the nation’s premier science and engineering lab for national security and technology innovation, with teams of specialists focused on cutting-edge work in a broad array of areas. Some of the main reasons we love our jobs:

  • Challenging work with amazing impact that contributes to security, peace, and freedom worldwide
  • Extraordinary co-workers
  • Some of the best tools, equipment, and research facilities in the world
  • Career advancement and enrichment opportunities
  • Flexible work arrangements for many positions include 9/80 (work 80 hours every two weeks, with every other Friday off) and 4/10 (work 4 ten-hour days each week) compressed workweeks, part-time work, and telecommuting (a mix of onsite work and working from home)
  • Generous vacation, strong medical and other benefits, competitive 401k, learning opportunities, relocation assistance and amenities aimed at creating a solid work/life balance*

World-changing technologies. Life-changing careers. Learn more about Sandia at: http://www.sandia.gov


*These benefits vary by job classification.

What Your Job Will Be Like

Are you interested in joining a high performing and closely collaborative verification, validation, and integration (VV&I) team within the Use Control mission area supporting the nation's nuclear deterrent? We are seeking a motivated software systems engineer interested in specializing in software system VV&I including test and qualification support.

On any given day, you may be called on to:

  • Develop knowledge of complex systems, respective requirements, and design documents
  • Work independently within a diversely skilled Agile team
  • Provide test engineering strategies and process improvements
  • Learn and leverage model-based systems engineering (MBSE) tools and methodologies for testing
  • Independently work on a high consequence system in a classified environment
  • Lead the development and implementation of software test procedures to verify sophisticated software against requirements
  • Develop the design and implementation strategies for tracking requirements, tests, and results
  • Collect evidentiary packages to document verification and validation results
  • Investigate, evaluate, and recommend development for testing automation tools and techniques
  • Interact with team members involved in systems, hardware, and software
  • Support the integration of hardware and software elements, performing integration tests, and evaluating interfaces between the hardware and software

Due to the nature of the work, the selected applicant must be able to work onsite.

Salary Range

$102,400 - $199,700

*Salary range is estimated, and actual salary will be determined after consideration of the selected candidate's experience and qualifications, and application of any approved geographic salary differential.

Qualifications We Require

  • Master's degree in Management of Information Systems, Computer Science or in a relevant field plus one year of relevant experience; or equivalent combination of education and experience
  • Minimum five (5) years of experience in developing software using at least one well-established programming language such as C++, C#, or Java
  • Ability to obtain and maintain DOE Q-level security clearance with Sigma 15 clearance which may require non-lifestyle polygraph testing

Qualifications We Desire

  • Minimum of five (5) years developing software that has been released to an operational environment
  • Minimum of five (5) years of software test engineering including test plan and procedure development, test data management, and software verification and validation
  • Familiarity with embedded software development and projects
  • Familiarity with Rust language
  • Experience writing automated software tests
  • Experience with Windows operating environments
  • Knowledge and/or practice regarding Agile software development practices
  • Knowledge of Use Control systems
  • Experience with Software Testing methodologies and techniques
  • Experience with Systems Engineering, Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) model development and tools (sysML, Cameo, or other)
  • Experience with configuration management and controls
  • Self-directed, organized, able to work independently as well as in a team environment
  • Ability to prioritize work and make decisions while working on multiple tasks
  • Ability to quickly learn new tools, approaches, and concepts and to understand and follow defined testing and engineering practices and standards
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills
  • Active DOE Q security clearance or DOD equivalent

About Our Team

The High Confidence System Environments (6616) organization enables Sandia mission product development through our use of practical cutting-edge software and systems engineering principles. We define, develop, test, and qualify well-engineered software architectures and products for critical systems in high consequence mission environments. Our projects leverage our key competencies including software engineering; secure embedded software development; systems engineering (requirements engineering; MBSE; technical planning, monitoring, and control); software quality engineering; and software verification, validation, and integration.

Posting Duration

This posting will be open for application submissions for a minimum of three (3) calendar days, including the 'posting date'. Sandia reserves the right to extend the posting date at any time.

Security Clearance

Sandia is required by DOE to conduct a pre-employment drug test and background review that includes checks of personal references, credit, law enforcement records, and employment/education verifications. Applicants for employment need to be able to obtain and maintain a DOE Q-level security clearance, which requires U.S. citizenship. If you hold more than one citizenship (i.e., of the U.S. and another country), your ability to obtain a security clearance may be impacted.

Applicants offered employment with Sandia are subject to a federal background investigation to meet the requirements for access to classified information or matter if the duties of the position require a DOE security clearance. Substance abuse or illegal drug use, falsification of information, criminal activity, serious misconduct or other indicators of untrustworthiness can cause a clearance to be denied or terminated by DOE, resulting in the inability to perform the duties assigned and subsequent termination of employment.

EEO

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status and any other protected class under state or federal law.

NNSA Requirements for MedPEDs

If you have a Medical Portable Electronic Device (MedPED), such as a pacemaker, defibrillator, drug-releasing pump, hearing aids, or diagnostic equipment and other equipment for measuring, monitoring, and recording body functions such as heartbeat and brain waves, if employed by Sandia National Laboratories you may be required to comply with NNSA security requirements for MedPEDs.

If you have a MedPED and you are selected for an on-site interview at Sandia National Laboratories, there may be additional steps necessary to ensure compliance with NNSA security requirements prior to the interview date.

title: C-IGNITE Proposal Success Specialist, Office of Research and Innovation
description:
Hiring Department

The Collaboratory for Integrating Growth, Innovation, and Research Excellence (C-IGNITE) in the Office of Research and Innovation (ORI) at the University of Missouri-Kansas City (UMKC)

Job Description

The Proposal Success Specialist primarily supports faculty and research teams in developing competitive, complex, multidisciplinary, and multi-PI research proposals from concept through submission. Most of the position’s effort is focused on direct proposal development, including grant writing, proposal review, faculty engagement, team coordination, and submission readiness. The position also supports funding intelligence and emerging research areas, including appropriate use of AI/LLM-enabled research tools.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Analyze funding solicitations and translate sponsor requirements into proposal strategies, outlines, compliance requirements, timelines, and action plans.
  • Draft and edit proposal sections, including project summaries/abstracts, broader impacts, management plans, budget justifications, partnership and community-engagement sections, and letters of support.
  • Review proposals and pre-proposals for sponsor alignment, responsiveness, competitiveness, consistency, and gaps; provide substantive feedback and follow through on revisions.
  • Lead proposal-development activities for complex, multidisciplinary, and multi-PI submissions, coordinating faculty, collaborators, and external partners through milestones and deliverables.
  • Work directly with faculty to shape research concepts, assess readiness and competitiveness, facilitate team development, and strengthen proposal strategy.
  • Prepare and coordinate ancillary proposal documents, including facilities and resources descriptions, data management plans, support materials, and other sponsor-required components.
  • Coordinate proposal timelines, internal reviews, final routing, and submission activities with Sponsored Programs and other university offices.
  • Support resubmissions by analyzing reviewer critiques, identifying proposal weaknesses, and helping research teams develop targeted responses and improvements.
  • Maintain accurate, timely records of proposals, opportunities, meetings, action items, deadlines, and project status in shared C-IGNITE systems.
  • Proactively identify gaps, ask questions early, communicate risks, and take ownership of assigned proposal-development work through completion.
  • Monitor funding opportunities and support research-intelligence activities that help identify potential faculty–funding alignment; use AI/LLM-enabled tools where appropriate, with human review and primary-source verification.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications

A Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education and experience and at least 5 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master’s degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience.
  • At least 3 years of direct grant-writing or proposal-development experience.
  • Experience developing complex federal, multidisciplinary, multi-PI, or collaborative research proposals.
  • Experience drafting and editing substantive proposal components and ancillary documents.
  • Strong ability to communicate complex information to scientific, academic, corporate, and non-technical audiences.
  • Experience with federal agencies, sponsored research, interdisciplinary collaboration, or industry/community partnerships.
  • Experience with research-intelligence tools, funding databases, or AI/LLM-enabled research methods is desirable.

Anticipated Hiring Range

The anticipated hiring range for this position has been established as $70,000–$80,000 annually

Salary is determined by a variety of factors, including but not limited to, the individual’s particular combination of education, skills, and experience, as well as organizational requirements.

Your total compensation goes beyond the number on your paycheck. The University of Missouri provides generous leave, health plans, and retirement contributions that add to your bottom line.

title: Commissioning Electrical Heat Trace (EHT) Lead
description:
Hiring now. Qualified candidates are being interviewed this week.

GrizzlyTrek is hiring a Commissioning Electrical Heat Trace (EHT) Lead for our valued client's commissioning and startup (CSU) team in Edmonton, Alberta. You will be the EHT subject matter expert on an integrated field leadership team, taking newly installed EHT systems through walkdowns, testing, functional checks and troubleshooting to first time start-up, and directing E&I electricians to mitigate EHT deficiencies.

A Journeyman Electrical Interprovincial Red Seal is required, with 7 to 15 years of experience, including 5 years leading commissioning and start-up.

At a Glance

  • Pay: $80.00 per hour
  • Location: Edmonton, Alberta. Field based, working on site.
  • Ticket: Journeyman Electrical, Interprovincial Red Seal (required)
  • Experience: 7 to 15 years of work experience, including 5 years leading commissioning and start-up
  • Scope: EHT inspection, testing, functional commissioning, documentation and troubleshooting

The Seat

You will work inside an integrated field leadership team, planning, managing and preparing equipment and systems for first time start-up. Your scope is newly installed EHT: cable routing, component installation, insulation and sensor placement, heating cable integrity, control panels, temperature controllers and alarms. As the EHT subject matter expert, you mentor less experienced members of the team and direct E&I electricians to mitigate EHT deficiencies.

What You'll Do

  • Walk down newly installed EHT systems to confirm compliance with isometric drawings, P&IDs and vendor specifications, including cable routing, component installation, insulation and sensor placement
  • Perform insulation resistance (megger) tests, continuity checks and loop resistance tests on heating cables to verify integrity
  • Commission and test heat trace control panels, temperature controllers (PLC, RTD and thermocouple) and alarm systems to confirm proper operation
  • Diagnose and resolve electrical, mechanical and controller faults, including repairing cable damage and replacing faulty components, and direct E&I electricians to mitigate EHT deficiencies
  • Prepare, update and maintain test reports, pre-functional checklists and red-line drawings, and develop daily EHT progress reports for the CSU Coordinator
  • Understand the Completions process, identify system scoping requirements and priorities, take part in inspections, system walkdowns and the Punchlist and Mitigation Plan, and manage test records and documentation as required under the CMS Plan
  • Within the EHT scope, assist the CSU Manager with review and edits of Commissioning Plans, Procedures and Strategy
  • Identify, schedule and manage EHT vendor and contractor needs on site, and monitor progress
  • Act as the EHT subject matter expert and mentor to the project team, sharing CSU experience and teaching less experienced members

What You Bring

  • Journeyman Electrical Interprovincial Red Seal
  • 7 to 15 years of work experience, including 5 years leading commissioning and start-up of electrical, instrumentation and automated electrical and mechanical equipment and process control systems
  • Strong electrical, instrumentation and automation background
  • Familiarity with refrigeration, gases and distillation
  • High level of understanding of automated EHT equipment commissioning

Nice to Have

  • Commissioning and start-up experience on EHT equipment in industrial gas, power generation and chemical facilities, including cryogenic technologies, air separation, syngas and CO2 capture

Why EHT Leads Take This Job

This seat makes you the EHT lead on an integrated field leadership team: walking down newly installed systems, proving heating cable integrity, commissioning control panels and controllers, and directing E&I electricians to clear deficiencies before first time start-up. It pays $80.00 per hour.

Benefits

  • Life insurance plus AD&D with critical illness and cancer coverage
  • Extended health: drugs, hospital, hearing, orthotics, vision, and paramedical including mental health
  • Dental coverage, including orthodontic coverage for children
  • Travel insurance up to $5,000,000 per incident
  • Ongoing training and career development support

We welcome applications from all qualified candidates and proudly support Indigenous employment.
