title: R&D Systems Research Analyst - PV Performance Modeling & Analytics, Onsite
description:
About Sandia

Sandia National Laboratories is the nation’s premier science and engineering lab for national security and technology innovation, with teams of specialists focused on cutting-edge work in a broad array of areas. Some of the main reasons we love our jobs:

  • Challenging work with amazing impact that contributes to security, peace, and freedom worldwide
  • Extraordinary co-workers
  • Some of the best tools, equipment, and research facilities in the world
  • Career advancement and enrichment opportunities
  • Flexible work arrangements for many positions include 9/80 (work 80 hours every two weeks, with every other Friday off) and 4/10 (work 4 ten-hour days each week) compressed workweeks, part-time work, and telecommuting (a mix of onsite work and working from home)
  • Generous vacation, strong medical and other benefits, competitive 401k, learning opportunities, relocation assistance and amenities aimed at creating a solid work/life balance*

World-changing technologies. Life-changing careers. Learn more about Sandia at: http://www.sandia.gov


*These benefits vary by job classification.

What Your Job Will Be Like

We are seeking a systems research analyst (job title: R&D S&E, Systems Research and Analysis) to conduct research related to PV performance modeling, data analysis, and analytics. The successful candidate will develop and evaluate models and analytical methods for understanding and improving PV system performance. Research may include terrestrial and space PV applications, performance modeling, analysis of measured PV and environmental data, model validation and benchmarking, uncertainty analysis, performance metrics, and operational analytics. If you are a self-motivated and dedicated problem solver, this position may be a great fit.

The successful candidate will be integrated into an existing team of researchers both within and external to Sandia to help forward the science of PV performance modeling and analytics.

On any given day, you may be called on to:

  • Further develop existing performance models to include additional physics and/or address new environments.
  • Develop, test, and verify new analytical methods for assessing PV performance.
  • Perform model calibration and verification.
  • Contribute to open-source tools.
  • Process and analyze field and experimental PV performance and meteorological data.
  • Participate in department and project meetings.
  • Attend and present at PV related conferences and workshops.
  • Publish research findings in scientific journals and government and/or industry reports.
  • Travel periodically.

Due to the nature of the work, the selected applicant must be able to work onsite. This position is located in Albuquerque, NM.

Salary Range

$102,400 - $199,700

*Salary range is estimated, and actual salary will be determined after consideration of the selected candidate's experience and qualifications, and application of any approved geographic salary differential.

Qualifications We Require

  • A Bachelor's degree in a relevant discipline, or an equivalent combination of directly relevant education and engineering or scientific experience that demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and ability to perform independent research and development.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a DOE Q-level security clearance.

Qualifications We Desire

The ideal R&D S&E, Systems Research and Analysis candidate for Sandia National Laboratories will in addition possess the following:

  • Graduate degree in a highly related field where an independent research project was a graduation requirement (e.g., independent project, thesis, or dissertation).
  • The ability to understand, synthesize, and draw insights from multiple types of data streams (e.g., technical, economic, policy) through the use of various analytical tools.
  • Experience working as part of multi-disciplinary teams examining complex systems.
  • Knowledge of the fundamentals of good project management, especially as it pertains to the execution of federally-funded work (e.g., proposal development through annal review, final delivery, and closeout).
  • Experience working with federal sponsors in the defense and intelligence sectors, as well as their domestic FFRDC partners, international partnering agencies, and foreign governments.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills, ability to work effectively in multidisciplinary teams delivering critical information to customers in a succinct manner.

Also, for this posting we are seeking individuals with the following experience:

  • Master¿s degree in engineering, physical sciences, mathematics, computer science, or a related technical field.
  • Demonstrated research experience in one or more relevant areas, such as PV, energy systems, computational modeling, data science, artificial intelligence, time-series analysis, or O&M analytics.
  • Strong programming and scientific computing skills, preferably in Python.
  • Demonstrated ability to conduct independent research, critically evaluate scientific literature, and develop rigorous analytical approaches.
  • Demonstrated ability to communicate research through publications, presentations, or other technical outputs.
  • Demonstrated ability and motivation to learn new technical areas and work effectively in collaborative research environments.
  • Experience with PV performance modeling, including terrestrial or space PV applications, or analysis of PV systems.
  • Experience with PV operational data, monitoring, or O&M (operations and maintenance) analytics.
  • Experience with model validation, uncertainty analysis, and/or benchmarking.
  • Experience analyzing large datasets and developing scientific software, especially in an open-source environment.
  • Experience with pvlib-python and other relevant scientific software.

About Our Team

The Photovoltaics and Materials Technology (PMT) department develops and validates materials and technologies that improve the performance, reliability, and safety of photovoltaic systems for energy and national security applications. Sandia focuses on emerging PV technologies and collaborates with dozens of companies and universities to develop and test new module architectures, tracking systems, integrated power electronics, encapsulants, and specialized coatings. We also develop materials, such as thermally stable polymers, electrodes, and electrolytes for advanced batteries and other applications. Our team applies HPC modeling and advanced indoor and outdoor testing capabilities to evaluate and predict system performance, degradation, and failure mechanisms.

Posting Duration

This posting will be open for application submissions for a minimum of three (3) calendar days, including the 'posting date'. Sandia reserves the right to extend the posting date at any time.

Security Clearance

Sandia is required by DOE to conduct a pre-employment drug test and background review that includes checks of personal references, credit, law enforcement records, and employment/education verifications. Applicants for employment need to be able to obtain and maintain a DOE Q-level security clearance, which requires U.S. citizenship. If you hold more than one citizenship (i.e., of the U.S. and another country), your ability to obtain a security clearance may be impacted.

Applicants offered employment with Sandia are subject to a federal background investigation to meet the requirements for access to classified information or matter if the duties of the position require a DOE security clearance. Substance abuse or illegal drug use, falsification of information, criminal activity, serious misconduct or other indicators of untrustworthiness can cause a clearance to be denied or terminated by DOE, resulting in the inability to perform the duties assigned and subsequent termination of employment.

EEO

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status and any other protected class under state or federal law.

NNSA Requirements for MedPEDs

If you have a Medical Portable Electronic Device (MedPED), such as a pacemaker, defibrillator, drug-releasing pump, hearing aids, or diagnostic equipment and other equipment for measuring, monitoring, and recording body functions such as heartbeat and brain waves, if employed by Sandia National Laboratories you may be required to comply with NNSA security requirements for MedPEDs.

If you have a MedPED and you are selected for an on-site interview at Sandia National Laboratories, there may be additional steps necessary to ensure compliance with NNSA security requirements prior to the interview date.

title: Litigation Director
description:
About the Organization
The Children's Law Center (CLC) is a non-profit legal services organization that represents children in custody, visitation, guardianship, paternity, family offense, and related child protective (abuse or neglect) proceedings in the Family Courts and the Integrated Domestic Violence Parts of the Supreme Court of the State of New York, and in appeals therefrom. CLC represents approximately 5,000 children annually in the Bronx, Brooklyn, Queens and Staten Island, providing holistic and zealous representation and support in the Court, the community and the legislature. CLC's mission is to empower our clients, prevent trauma and promote wellbeing.

Position Description
Reporting to the Executive Director, the Litigation Director leads an interdisciplinary, client-centered legal program ensuring excellence in the protection of rights of CLC clients in Family Court proceedings, while also identifying and actively addressing systemic challenges faced by children in those cases. The Litigation Director provides leadership and ownership of all aspects of CLC’s trial practice including strategy, practice standards and skills development; supervision of borough directors; hiring and training of staff and maintaining a well-functioning, respectful and diverse legal organization. Additionally, the Ligation Director will oversee the pro bono and special project supervisor, pursuing affirmative litigation and amicus briefs as appropriate.

The Litigation Director also brings strategic direction and support to CLC’s trial practice professionals, establishing and maintaining our reputation as a national leader in legal advocacy for children involved in Family Court. They will advance the day-to-day development of the legal staff teams and ensure that CLC maintains the highest quality standards of representation and interdisciplinary client service.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:
  • Participates in the development and implementation of initiatives to enhance organizational culture while cultivating staff’s understanding and alignment with CLC's mission and values, emphasizing a strategic focus on vulnerable children, including those facing systemic racism, living in poverty, with disability or exposed to family violence, mental health conditions, substance misuse and other forms of family disruption;
  • Supervises, develops, mentors, supports, and evaluates the Borough Legal Directors, to ensure the effective performance of their duties to meet the role and expectations of their position;
  • Develops litigation strategies that support the inclusion of children’s voices in decisions that impact them and to achieve their expressed wishes; provides trial assistance and/or representation on particularly complex cases;
  • Provides support to ensure CLC leaders and staff comply with organization policies and procedures, applicable court procedures and regulations;
  • In collaboration with the Executive Director and the HR Director, the Litigation Director supervises the trial team’s talent management life cycle, including recruiting, onboarding, performance management, career development, succession planning and learning;
  • Partners with the Executive Director and members of Executive Team to identify, create, fund and support innovative approaches to meet staff and client needs, including educational, emotional and community resources, including the Children’s Voice Project;
  • Ensures collaboration between the Legal Directors team and other members of the Leadership team to ensure staff requests are reviewed, addressed and accurately communicated in a timely manner;
  • With support from the Managing Attorney, provides leadership to CLC’s new lawyer and Continuing Legal Education (CLE) training programs;
  • Works with the Senior Director of Operations and the Borough Legal Directors to ensure that CLC’s case management numbers are accurate, and reports can be provided to CLC leaders, staff, the Board of Directors, and funders;
  • Utilizes case management data to spot trends impacting clients and staff;
  • Partners with the Executive Director and other Directors to represent CLC to Judges, Family Court and community stakeholders as well as government and private funders;
  • Collaborates with CLC Finance team, external bank team, CFO, development, technology, archival, facilities and case management professionals to ensure the effective utilization of CLC’s budget;
  • Understands, supports, and communicates to CLC trial leadership contract compliance expectations of the Office of Court Administration (OCA), the Family Court and the Fiscal department;
  • Enhances respectful communication amongst staff and addresses client, staff, and court needs;
  • Collaborates with the Executive Director, Senior Director of Administration and the Board of Directors, to effectuate CLC’s multiyear budget and operational plan to ensure all staff, client and organizational needs are met;
  • Maintains a high level of professional skill and knowledge by participating in conferences and educational opportunities, reading professional publications, maintaining professional networks, and participating in professional organizations. Communicates appropriately, updates to Leadership and Legal staff.
Qualifications:
  • Admitted to practice law in New York State; admission to the federal courts is a plus.
  • Eight or more years of relevant legal and litigation experience, with knowledge of family court practice and policy, including custody, domestic violence, and child welfare law.
  • Three or more years of supervisory experience at the staff and managerial levels, including coaching and counseling employees through performance and other employee relations matters.
  • Understanding of trauma-informed legal representation of children and a desire to work in a busy public interest organization engaged in individual representation and systemic advocacy on behalf of children.
  • Demonstrated advocacy and interviewing skills, along with strong mediation and settlement skills.
  • Demonstrated experience working on interdisciplinary teams through a diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging lens.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead and support change throughout an organization.
  • Proficiency with case management systems, databases, spreadsheets, word processing, and email.
  • Prior non-profit experience preferred.
Skills & Attributes:
  • A creative and strategic mindset with a demonstrated ability to translate vision into action plans.
  • Proven leadership, sound judgment, and strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills, including the ability to handle difficult situations effectively.
  • Ability to identify and address issues of concern to clients and staff.
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills (oral and written), including prompt communication across all levels of the organization so that plans and projects are evaluated swiftly and conflicting demands are prioritized.
  • Fosters a collaborative approach among leaders and staff.
  • Excellent time management, project management, and organizational skills, including the ability to work independently, prioritize, and process information while handling multiple tasks and decisions under tight deadlines.
  • Ability to conduct presentations and trainings and serve as a designated point person.
  • Exercises discretion and preserves confidential information.
  • Passion, commitment, confidence, self-motivation, and a sense of humor, with the ability to thrive in a challenging environment.
  • Proficiency in languages other than English desired but not required.

Note: Studies have shown that women and people of color are less likely to apply for jobs unless they believe they are able to perform every task in the job description. CLC will consider any equivalent combination of knowledge, skills, and experience to meet minimum qualifications. We encourage you to think broadly about your background and skill set for this role.

Position Type: Full-Time

Salary Range: $185,000-$205,000 annually, dependent upon experience.

Hybrid: This position currently requires the individual’s physical presence (hybrid, minimum three days per week) at CLC’s offices in New York City. Days per week is subject to change and is dependent on Court requirements as well as grant requirements.

Benefits: At The Children’s Law Center, we provide a comprehensive benefits package to support your wellbeing. Our offerings include health, dental, and vision insurance, a 401(k) plan including employer contribution and match, paid time off, and opportunities for professional growth. We are dedicated to creating a supportive and balanced work environment where you can thrive both personally and professionally. As an employee of The Children’s Law Center, you may be eligible for federal loan forgiveness programs. For more information, please visit https://studentaid.gov/pslf/.

As an equal opportunity employer, The Children's Law Center is committed to fostering an inclusive and equitable work environment. All qualified applicants will be afforded equal employment opportunities without discrimination.

title: Senior Finance Business Partner
description:

Role Description

Turn financial insight into decisions that shape production, strengthen Quality and create lasting impact.

Join us in creating a future legacy in medical dermatology

At LEO Pharma, we are global leaders in medical dermatology. We have 118 years’ experience in bringing innovation to healthcare. And we are eager to do much more. Each year, close to 100 million people have a better day because of our medicines.

At LEO Pharma, how we work matters. We build trusted relationships and deliver with impact. We focus on where we can make the greatest difference and have the courage to explore new possibilities. You will also collaborate with Supply Chain, Finance Shared Services, Group Financial Controllers and Group FP&A, connecting perspectives across functions to support better decisions.

You will be part of a collaborative and international environment that values initiative, sound judgement, constructive challenge and shared accountability.

You do not need to upload a cover letter, but feel free to add a few sentences in your resume or CV on why this position has your interest. Please refrain from adding a photo to your CV.

Join LEO Pharma, a global leader in medical dermatology, as we go beyond the skin to make a lasting impact. Our innovative approach sets us apart. We are dedicated to leaving a legacy that positively impacts patients, colleagues, and our planet.

At LEO Pharma, we believe in the power of individuals to drive change. Our flat organizational structure empowers you to make a visible impact and offers versatile roles for professional growth. title: Intern, R&D Undergraduate Summer - TITANS - Southwest Analysis Laboratories for Semiconductor Advancement (SALSA), Onsite
description:
What Your Job Will Be Like

We seek undergraduate student interns to join our SALSA (Southwest Analysis Laboratories for Semiconductor Advancement) TITANS Cybersecurity team for Summer 2027! Qualified candidates will be part of a larger family, namely Technical Internships To Advance National Security (TITANS), focused solely on cybersecurity, software, hardware and math analytics.

TITANS Cybersecurity (also known as the Center for Cyber Defenders or CCD) is seeking students who want to have a career in cybersecurity. We are focused on developing the next generation of experts in the field of computer security from the software stack down to microelectronic hardware components. You will use your foundational computer science/engineering, electrical engineering, materials science, math, analytics, and data science skills, but your work will be directed to cybersecurity topics. This posting is for who are currently pursuing graduate degrees in the field of Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Physics, or any closely related field of study and are interested in furthering their knowledge in the area of cyber security and information protection while working on their graduate degree.

Your job could consist of:

  • Manual and automated failure analysis and vulnerability assessment
  • Intrusion prevention/detection and response, penetration testing, and forensics
  • Information protection, and resiliency
  • Authentication and authorization
  • Cryptography
  • Mobile devices and smart technologies

And many more areas of research!

We are also looking for candidates with expertise in electrical engineering, physics, and materials science interested in:

  • Debugging hardware prototypes
    • Printed Circuit Board Layout
    • Design analysis
    • Prototype assembly
  • Identifying and fixing integrated circuit issues (failure analysis)
    • Focused Ion Beam (FIB) tools
    • Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM)
    • Laser Scanning Microscopy (LSM) tools
  • Design either at the integrated circuit or circuit board level, including tools such as
    • K Layout
    • Altium
    • Cadence Tool Chain
  • FPGA/microcontroller/embedded systems development
  • Electronic measurement equipment experience including oscilloscope, power supplies, waveform generators, etc.
  • RF or electromagnetics expertise

Your projects will be real-world cybersecurity hardware problems or embedded engineering challenges contributing to a cybersecurity challenge or mission space affecting national security. There's no busy work in the CCD! Your solution will exercise foundational math and analytic techniques and best practices in SW or HW engineering to help improve cybersecurity of our nation.

Due to the nature of the work, the selected applicant must be able to work onsite.

Salary Range

At Sandia, we value the important work done by our interns and its contribution to National Security. Because of this, our interns earn competitive pay rates. Our pay structure is based on earned credit hours, classification, and degree level. Your pay rate will be determined during the hire process and included in your offer package. You can view the Intern Pay Rate chart here.

Qualifications We Require

You bring the confidence and skills to be eligible for the job by meeting these minimum requirements:

  • Currently attending and enrolled full time in the spring term immediately preceding the internship (or scheduled to graduate in the spring) in an accredited undergraduate program
  • Pursuing a science, engineering, or math major
  • Minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0/4.0
  • Ability to work up to 40 hours per week during the summer
  • Ability to secure and maintain a U.S. security clearance which requires U.S. citizenship

Note: If you have not earned a HS diploma or equivalent, please apply to a high school intern position.

Qualifications We Desire

  • GPA of at least 3.2 on a 4.0 scale
  • Pursuing an undergraduate degree in an engineering or science related field, such as Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Physics, or other relevant disciplines

Posting Duration

This posting will be open for application submissions for a minimum of three (3) calendar days, including the 'posting date'. Sandia reserves the right to extend the posting date at any time.

About Our Team

The CCD gives computer science interns practical experience with computer systems, network operations, and information protection. The year-round program combines research with education and provides a venue for interns to perform experiments on attacking and defending computer systems with proper guidance and protective measures in place.

About Sandia

title: Senior Supplier Development Engineer
description:
Job ID: 116003

The Leonardo DRS Naval Power Systems business is a trusted provider of innovative naval gas and hybrid power systems, control technology and support solutions for the U.S. Navy and navies around the world.

Job Summary

The Senior Supplier Development Engineer serves as the technical bridge between Leonardo DRS’s requirements and the external suppliers that fabricate and machine its hardware. Working closely with suppliers and DRS engineering personnel, this role helps mature designs into producible, repeatable products by incorporating manufacturability early in the design process, resolving fabrication and machining issues at the source, and selecting or developing qualified suppliers that can build to print successfully the first time.

Job Responsibilities

  • Assess prospective and incumbent suppliers’ welding, machining, and inspection capabilities, including equipment, certifications, qualified personnel, capacity, and process controls.
  • Participate in concept and detailed design reviews, representing supplier capabilities and manufacturing constraints before drawings are released.
  • Lead design-for-manufacturability and cost-reduction efforts with engineering and suppliers. Identify opportunities to simplify weldments, optimize joint design and weld volume, reduce machining setups and tolerance stack-ups, and lower material and process costs.
  • Review drawings, models, and specifications for build readiness, including weld symbols, geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T), surface finishes, nondestructive testing (NDT) callouts, and process requirements.
  • Evaluate supplier manufacturing plans for completeness and risk, including fabrication sequences, weld procedure specifications and qualifications (WPS/PQR), fixturing, distortion controls, machining plans, and in-process inspections.
  • Support quoting and proposal activities by providing technical input on potential sources of supply, evaluating supplier estimates against proposed manufacturing processes, and identifying cost drivers.
  • Serve as a day-to-day technical point of contact for suppliers. Work with DRS engineering to resolve technical questions, drawing clarifications, and deviation requests in a timely manner.
  • Drive first-article, prototype, and pre-production builds. Help suppliers develop the processes and capabilities needed to complete accurate first-article inspection packages, qualify weld procedures and personnel, and close technical risks before rate production.
  • Visit supplier facilities as needed to support design reviews, process and build validation, first-article activities, and issue resolution. Observe manufacturing processes firsthand and identify risks and improvement opportunities.
  • Lead or support root-cause investigations and corrective actions for supplier nonconformances, including build defects, dimensional escapes, requirements gaps, and process failures.
  • Support the transition to stable production by helping establish documented work instructions, inspection criteria, and process controls; assist with production ramp-up and capacity growth.
  • Drive continuous improvement across the supply base by sharing lessons learned, standardizing effective practices, and incorporating supplier producibility insights into internal design standards.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering or related technical field or equivalent experience and a minimum of 5 years of experience in heavy fabrication, weldment manufacturing, and/or precision machining environments.
  • Proficient technical expertise and application domain knowledge
  • ASQ certification or Black Belt preferred
  • Proficient with ISO Standards, Six Sigma tools, statistics
  • Ability to understand military specifications and to read blueprints
  • Excellent interpersonal, negotiation, communication and writing skills
  • Self-directed and comfortable owning issues to closure across organizational boundaries
  • Willingness to travel (50%)
  • Ability to define problems and drive to root cause and effective corrective action

U.S. Citizenship required.

The salary range for this position is $96,702 - $138,285. This range reflects the good faith estimate of pay the employer is willing to offer at the time of posting. Several factors can influence the pay scale, including but not limited to: Federal contract labor categories and contract wage rates, collective bargaining agreements, geographic location, business considerations, scope, and responsibilities of the position, local or other applicable market conditions, and internal equity. Other factors include the candidate’s qualifications such as prior work experience, specific skills and competencies, education/training, and certifications. In addition to base pay, employees may be eligible for: annual performance-based bonuses, equity awards, and overtime pay (for non-exempt employees as applicable. Our benefits package includes comprehensive health insurance (medical, dental, vision), employer matching 401(k) retirement plan, paid time off including vacation, holidays, and sick leave (including ant state-mandated paid sick leave), parental leave benefits, tuition reimbursement, professional development support, and life and disability insurance coverage.

Taking care of our people is a top priority at Leonardo DRS. We are proud to offer competitive salaries and comprehensive benefits, including medical, dental, and vision coverage, a company contribution to a health savings account, telemedicine, life and disability insurance, legal insurance, and a 401(k) savings plan. We champion wellness programs that focus on physical, emotional, and financial well-being. title: Chief Executive Officer, Multicultural NSW
description:
Chief Executive Officer

Multicultural NSW

Location: Based in Parramatta

Employment Type: Ongoing Full-Time

Salary: Total Remuneration Package: from $386,755 to $438,144

Multicultural NSW is dedicated to fostering a harmonious and cohesive society by celebrating the rich diversity of the state of NSW. We champion equal rights and responsibilities for all individuals and emphasize a shared commitment to New South Wales and Australia.

Each year, Multicultural NSW partners with over 300 community and faith organisations, supporting a variety of festivals and events that engage nearly 3 million people across the state, to enrich, the lives of our residents.

About the role

The Chief Executive Officer (CEO) is the head of Multicultural NSW and a member of the Advisory Board. Reporting directly to the Minister, the CEO provides strategic leadership to advance social cohesion, strengthen community resilience and support one of the most culturally diverse jurisdictions in the world.

Leading a high-profile agency within the NSW public sector, the CEO drives multicultural policy, research and community engagement initiatives, oversees the Multicultural Policies and Services Program (MPSP), and works across government, industry and community sectors to deliver positive outcomes for the people of New South Wales.

What you’ll do

As Chief Executive Officer, you will provide strategic leadership to advance the NSW Government's vision for a cohesive, inclusive and resilient multicultural society. You will:

  • Provide authoritative advice to the Premier, Minister and Government on multicultural affairs, community relations and social cohesion.
  • Lead the strategic direction and performance of Multicultural NSW, ensuring alignment with Government priorities and community outcomes.
  • Drive policy, research and reform initiatives that strengthen social cohesion, community resilience and intercultural understanding.
  • Foster influential partnerships across government, community, faith and industry sectors to deliver meaningful outcomes for diverse communities.
  • Oversee the NSW Government's response to humanitarian and refugee settlement programs and multicultural initiatives.
  • Lead the delivery and governance of key agency functions, including community grants, language services and community development programs.
  • Ensure effective oversight of the Multicultural Policies and Services Program (MPSP) and agency compliance across the NSW public sector.
  • Champion organisational excellence, innovation and continuous improvement to position Multicultural NSW for future success.

If you are a values-driven executive with a demonstrated ability to lead complex organisations, influence stakeholders and deliver strategic outcomes, we encourage you to apply.

Download the role description

What we’re looking for

  • Demonstrated executive leadership experience in a complex public, private or not-for-profit environment.
  • Strong understanding of multicultural communities, social cohesion and community engagement.
  • Proven ability to influence and build productive relationships with ministers, senior executives, community leaders and stakeholders.
  • Experience leading organisational transformation, strategic reform and service delivery outcomes.
  • Strong policy, governance and stakeholder engagement capabilities.
  • Tertiary qualifications in a relevant discipline or equivalent executive experience.

We focus on hiring people who share our commitment and goals of inclusion, collaboration, adaptability, courage, and integrity. If you meet the essential requirements and the role resonates with you, please apply – you do not need to meet every desired requirement for us to want to talk to you.

We do work that really matters

At Multicultural NSW, we work to build a more inclusive, cohesive and resilient New South Wales. We partner with communities, government agencies and stakeholders to strengthen social cohesion and support multicultural communities across the state. Join us and lead work that makes a meaningful difference to the lives of people and communities throughout NSW.

Are you ready to join us?

Click apply, attach an up-to-date résumé (maximum 3 pages) and a cover letter (maximum 2 pages) outlining how you meet what we are looking for.

Applications close Sunday 22 November at 11:59pm (AEDT)

For more information about the role or If you’ve got a question about applying or would benefit from an adjustment in the recruitment process to help you perform at your best (including an alternate method submission of the application), please contact DCJ Senior Executive Recruitment Team on seniorexecutiverecruitment@dcj.nsw.gov.au.

Inclusion and Diversity lies at the heart of how we recruit

We continue to hire great people with a wide variety of skills, experience and backgrounds. This includes people with disability, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander People, women, people identifying as LGBTIQ+, culturally and linguistically diverse people, carers and other diversity groups.

To find out what DCJ are doing to build an inclusive and diverse workforce, visit Inclusion and diversity on the DCJ website.

What Your Job Will Be Like

Are you interested in joining a high performing and closely collaborative verification, validation, and integration (VV&I) team within the Use Control mission area supporting the nation's nuclear deterrent?   • Support the investigation, evaluation, and recommendation development for testing automation tools and techniques
  • Interact with team members involved in systems, hardware, and software
  • Support the integration of hardware and software elements, performing integration tests, and evaluating interfaces between the hardware and software

Due to the nature of the work, the selected applicant must be able to work onsite.

Salary Range

$87,400 - $168,800

*Salary range is estimated, and actual salary will be determined after consideration of the selected candidate's experience and qualifications, and application of any approved geographic salary differential.

Qualifications We Require

  • Bachelor's degree in Management of Information Systems, Computer Science or in a relevant field; Or equivalent combination of education and experience
  • Experience in developing software using at least one well-established programming language such as C++, C#, or Java. Use of a programming language for performing assignments in a university class would qualify.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain DOE Q-level security clearance with Sigma 15 clearance which may require non-lifestyle polygraph testing

Qualifications We Desire

  • Master's degree in Management of Information Systems, Computer Science or in a relevant field
  • Minimum of one (1) year experience with C++/C# or three (3) years experience developing software that has been released to an operational environment
  • Familiarity with embedded software development and projects
  • Familiarity with Rust language
  • Experience supporting software testing or formal software verification and validation practices
  • Experience writing automated software tests
  • Experience with Windows operating environments
  • Knowledge and/or practice regarding Agile software development practices
  • Knowledge of Use Control systems
  • Knowledge of Software Testing methodologies and techniques
  • Experience with Systems Engineering, Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) model development and tools (sysML, Cameo, or other)

  • Ability to quickly learn new tools, approaches, and concepts and to understand and follow defined testing and engineering practices and standards
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills
  • Active DOE Q security clearance or DOD equivalent

About Our Team

The High Confidence System Environments (6616) organization enables Sandia mission product development through our use of practical cutting-edge software and systems engineering principles. We define, develop, test, and qualify well-engineered software architectures and products for critical systems in high consequence mission environments. Our projects leverage our key competencies including software engineering; secure embedded software development; systems engineering (requirements engineering; MBSE; technical planning, monitoring, and control); software quality engineering; and software verification, validation, and integration.

This posting will be open for application submissions for a minimum of three (3) calendar days, including the 'posting date'. Sandia reserves the right to extend the posting date at any time.

Security Clearance

Sandia is required by DOE to conduct a pre-employment drug test and background review that includes checks of personal references, credit, law enforcement records, and employment/education verifications. Applicants for employment need to be able to obtain and maintain a DOE Q-level security clearance, which requires U.S. citizenship. If you hold more than one citizenship (i.e., of the U.S. and another country), your ability to obtain a security clearance may be impacted.

Applicants offered employment with Sandia are subject to a federal background investigation to meet the requirements for access to classified information or matter if the duties of the position require a DOE security clearance. Substance abuse or illegal drug use, falsification of information, criminal activity, serious misconduct or other indicators of untrustworthiness can cause a clearance to be denied or terminated by DOE, resulting in the inability to perform the duties assigned and subsequent termination of employment.

EEO

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status and any other protected class under state or federal law.

NNSA Requirements for MedPEDs

If you have a Medical Portable Electronic Device (MedPED), such as a pacemaker, defibrillator, drug-releasing pump, hearing aids, or diagnostic equipment and other equipment for measuring, monitoring, and recording body functions such as heartbeat and brain waves, if employed by Sandia National Laboratories you may be required to comply with NNSA security requirements for MedPEDs.

If you have a MedPED and you are selected for an on-site interview at Sandia National Laboratories, there may be additional steps necessary to ensure compliance with NNSA security requirements prior to the interview date.

title: Senior Manager, Wholesale Credit Risk
description:

We bring together the people, ideas and capital that nurture progress and growth, helping to create a better world – for our customers, our people, our investors, our communities and the planet we all share.

These include market-leading subsidised private health cover, enhanced parental pay and support when returning to work, bonus leave days and wellness programmes including discounted gym memberships.

Global Risk & Compliance is a specialist and expert risk management function supporting HSBC across all aspects of risk management and compliance. The team manages a varied and dynamic range of risk types, including operational, credit, compliance, regulatory, market and reputational risks. Our people use their skills, insight and integrity to manage established and emerging risks, helping HSBC deliver sustainable growth.

We’re currently seeking an experienced credit professional to join the Wholesale Credit Risk team as Senior Manager, Wholesale Credit Risk, based in Sydney. Reporting to the Head of Approvals, you’ll assess and make decisions on complex corporate credit proposals within your delegated Credit Approval Authority. You’ll provide independent, commercially focused credit guidance while maintaining sound asset quality and a conservative credit culture across HSBC’s lending activities in Australia.

This role has no direct or indirect reports.

Key responsibilities will include:

  • Assess and make decisions on corporate credit proposals, including annual reviews, new-money requests and amendments, within delegated Credit Approval Authority.
  • Provide expert credit guidance at both transactional and portfolio levels, helping shape credit appetite and support sound asset quality.
  • Deliver high-quality financial analysis, including consistent risk-grade assessments and clear presentations of financial risk.
  • Identify and escalate credit concerns promptly and appropriately, including relevant matters to the Special Credit Unit.
  • Contribute to Worry, Watch and Monitor forums, sector reviews and other credit risk governance activities.
  • Provide early advice and guidance on large and complex transactions, including highly structured transactions across sectors such as leveraged finance, project finance and commercial real estate.
  • Support HSBC Australia’s growth and strategic priorities by promoting an efficient, commercially focused credit approval process that responds to customer needs.
  • Ensure compliance with HSBC’s credit risk management framework, policies and procedures, applicable regulatory requirements and internal control standards.
  • Provide input into business and functional requirements relating to corporate risk, including credit systems development and policy formulation.
  • Monitor key risk indicators and work with first line controls teams to support effective operational risk management.
  • Develop subject-matter expertise in a relevant sector, product or specialist area supporting Wholesale Credit Risk coverage.
  • Build effective relationships with senior stakeholders across Corporate and Institutional Banking, Product areas and regional and local Risk functions.
  • Support team engagement and effectiveness by providing coaching, mentoring and assistance to colleagues as required.
  • Maintain current knowledge of macroeconomic, financial market, country, sector, counterparty and product developments, ensuring changing risk profiles are reflected in credit assessments.

To be successful in the role you will need:

  • A university degree in Finance, Economics, Business Administration or a related discipline.
  • Extensive experience in corporate credit analysis and related risk management.
  • Significant experience assessing complex corporate exposures across a broad range of industries.
  • Experience in highly structured transactions, including leveraged finance, project finance and commercial real estate.
  • Strong financial analysis, technical credit and problem-solving skills, with sound commercial judgement and a clear focus on credit quality.
  • The ability to make timely, independent and well-reasoned credit decisions within delegated authority.
  • Experience contributing to credit appetite, policy development, risk governance and portfolio-level risk management.
  • Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, with the confidence to engage and influence senior leaders across Risk, Corporate and Institutional Banking and Product teams.
  • The ability to work autonomously while contributing effectively to a collaborative team environment.
  • A proactive approach to identifying emerging risks and escalating concerns appropriately.
  • The ability to work under strict time pressures while meeting service-level commitments.
  • A strong understanding of regulatory requirements, internal controls and operational risk management.
  • A commitment to HSBC’s values and to fostering a sound, conservative and commercially aware credit culture.

We will conly consider candidates who hold Australian or New Zealand Permanent Residency/Citizenship or currently have unrestricted work rights in Australia with no limitations.

We value different perspectives, we succeed together, collaborating across boundaries, we take responsibility, holding ourselves accountable to get things done. title: Mentor Liaison/Employment Specialist
description:
Position Summary:
The Veteran Services Specialist will coordinate and support Veterans Place's mentorship
program in partnership with the Allegheny County Veterans Court, with a focus on serving
justice-involved veterans. This position will recruit, train, and support volunteer mentors;
coordinate mentor and mentee relationships; assist with Veterans Court engagement; and provide
ongoing participant support. The position will also deliver employment services, including
career counseling, resume development, job readiness, employer connections, and employment
placement. The Specialist will serve as a primary point of contact for mentorship and
employment services while building relationships with employers, volunteer mentors, Veterans
Court, and community partners.
Key Responsibilities:
Mentorship & Participant Support:
• Serve as the primary point of contact for the mentorship program and provide ongoing
guidance and support to volunteer mentors.
• Recruit, screen, select, and onboard veteran mentors from the community.
• Coordinate mentor and mentee matching based on individual needs, goals, and
compatibility.
• Develop, organize, and facilitate structured mentor training, including All Rise's
nationally recognized trauma-informed training curriculum.
• Ensure mentors complete all required training prior to participating in Veterans Court.
• Conduct regular check-ins with mentors and mentees to monitor engagement, address
concerns, and support successful mentoring relationships.
• Attend Allegheny County Veterans Court at least twice per month and maintain
communication with court personnel regarding participant progress and concerns.
• Advocate for justice-involved veterans and communicate any issues that may affect their
participation in Veterans Court.
• Organize and facilitate group mentoring sessions, workshops, and peer-support activities.
• Coordinate access to additional Veterans Place services and community resources,
including housing, recovery, healthcare, and other supportive services.
Program Coordination:
• Provide individualized employment services to veterans, including career counseling, job
readiness assistance, resume development, and interview preparation.
• Assess participants' employment interests, skills, experience, and vocational goals to
identify appropriate career opportunities.
• Develop and maintain individualized employment plans that address career goals and
barriers to employment.
• Assist veterans with job searches, applications, interview coordination, and connections
to potential employers.
• Establish and maintain relationships with local employers to identify job opportunities
and advocate for veteran candidates.
• Organize resume workshops, mock interviews, and other employment-readiness
activities.
• Provide referrals to training programs, educational opportunities, and supportive services
that improve employment outcomes.
• Conduct follow-up with employed veterans to support job retention and career
advancement.
Documentation Reporting & Program Outcomes:
• Maintain accurate and timely documentation of participant interactions, mentor
engagement, employment services, and program progress.
• Track mentorship program activity, including mentor recruitment, training completion,
mentor/mentee matches, and participant engagement.
• Monitor employment outcomes, job retention, and participant progress.
• Assist with program reporting, grant compliance, and evaluation activities.
• Maintain confidentiality and ensure documentation complies with organizational policies
and applicable program requirements.
Community Partnerships & Outreach:
• Develop and maintain relationships with Allegheny County Veterans Court, community
organizations, veteran service providers, employers, and volunteer networks.
• Represent Veterans Place at court proceedings, community events, outreach activities,
and partner meetings.
• Identify opportunities to expand mentor recruitment, employment partnerships, and
resources available to participating veterans.
• Collaborate with internal Veterans Place departments to coordinate services and provide
comprehensive support to participants.
Qualifications:
• U.S. military veteran preferred.
• Bachelor's degree in Human Services, Social Work, Business, Human Resources, or a
related field preferred. Related work experience may be accepted in place of a degree.
• Experience in mentorship, peer support, case management, workforce development, or
working with veterans and/or justice-involved populations.
• Knowledge of trauma-informed practices and the challenges faced by veterans
experiencing homelessness, housing instability, or involvement with the justice system.
• Experience working with Veterans Court or other treatment court programs preferred.
• Strong interpersonal, communication, organizational, and relationship-building skills.
• Ability to develop relationships with, engage, and support volunteer mentors.
• Comfortable with public speaking, group facilitation, and community outreach.
• Ability to manage multiple responsibilities independently while collaborating with
internal staff and external partners.
• Proficiency in Microsoft Office and digital platforms; experience with BestNotes or
similar client management systems preferred.
• Must have a valid driver's license and the ability to travel to various locations.
• Must successfully complete required background checks and pre-employment screening.
Physical Demands:
• Stand or Sit, must be able to remain in a stationary position 50% of the time.
• Talk/hear, has the ability to communicate information and ideas so that others will
understand. Must be able to exchange accurate information in these situations.
• Carry weight and lift, able to move or carry up to 20 pounds across office for various
needs
Work Environment:
• The Veteran Services Workforce Liaison operates in a fast-paced, mission-driven
environment requiring adaptability, collaboration, and a strong commitment to serving

title: North Nashua Closing Baker
description:
Crumbl Closing Baker / Crew Member

Love cookies, good energy, and a job that keeps you moving? Crumbl is looking for dependable, motivated team members to join our closing crew! You'll help mix, bake, decorate, serve guests, and finish each night with a clean, organized store.

This position is focused on closing shifts from approximately 4:00 PM to 10:30 PM. Availability on both Friday and Saturday is required.

Pay and Schedule

Earn $15–$18 per hour, including tips, with team members averaging approximately $16 per hour.

Both full-time and part-time opportunities may be available. Applicants must have dependable, year-round availability and be able to work closing shifts-especially Fridays and Saturdays.

Full-Time Benefits

Eligible full-time team members receive:

  • Two weeks of paid vacation
  • Health insurance options
  • One guaranteed weekend day off
  • 50% off Crumbl products
  • Employee referral bonuses of up to $1,000
  • 15% tuition discount through Southern New Hampshire University

What You'll Do

As part of our closing crew, you'll:

  • Mix dough, bake cookies, and prepare our rotating weekly flavors
  • Decorate and package cookies with attention to detail
  • Welcome guests and help them choose from the week's menu
  • Take orders and process payments
  • Clean and sanitize equipment, workstations, and guest areas
  • Restock supplies and prepare the store for the next day
  • Work with your teammates to complete closing tasks efficiently

What We're Looking For

You don't need professional baking experience-we'll teach you everything you need to know! We're looking for someone who:

  • Can consistently work from 4:00 PM to 10:30 PM
  • Is available every Friday and Saturday
  • Is dependable, positive, and ready to work
  • Enjoys working as part of a team
  • Stays focused in a busy, high-energy environment
  • Takes pride in leaving the store clean, organized, and ready for tomorrow

Requirements

Applicants must be at least 16 years old and have reliable transportation to and from work-including transportation home after closing. This active position requires standing for extended periods and lifting up to 25 pounds.

Ready to Join the Closing Crew?

If you're a night owl who loves teamwork, great energy, and seriously delicious cookies, apply today! Join Crumbl and help us make every evening-and every box-a little sweeter.

title: Sr. Raw Materials Engineer
description:
Requisition Number: 79694

The company built on breakthroughs. ​
Join us.​

Corning is one of the world’s leading innovators in glass, ceramic, and materials science. From the depths of the ocean to the farthest reaches of space, our technologies push the boundaries of what’s possible. ​

How do we do this? With our people. They break through limitations and expectations – not once in a career, but every day. They help move our company, and the world, forward. ​

​At Corning, there are endless possibilities for making an impact. You can help connect the unconnected, drive the future of automobiles, transform at-home entertainment, and ensure the delivery of lifesaving medicines. And so much more.​

​Come break through with us.



Corning’s Environmental Technologies segment manufactures ceramic substrates and filter products for emissions control in mobile and stationary applications around the world.

Role Purpose

The Sr. Raw Material Engineer provides technical leadership for raw materials used across Corning Environmental Technologies. This role is a primary technical interface with raw material suppliers and works closely with manufacturing plants, research and development, and sourcing to ensure material quality, supply assurance, and manufacturing performance. The engineer will lead supplier-facing technical activities including material qualification, technical assessments, issue resolution, specification alignment, and material improvement. The successful candidate will combine deep materials knowledge, data-driven problem-solving, and strong external collaboration to improve material quality, reliability, cost competitiveness, and long-term supply capability

Key Responsibilities

  • Serve as the technical lead for assigned raw materials and supplier relationships, including specifications, qualification requirements, technical assessments, and engineering documentation
  • Lead technical engagement with suppliers to resolve material quality, performance, supply, and processability issues
  • Lead and support qualification of new materials, material changes, suppliers, and alternative sources
  • Partner with sourcing and suppliers to improve material quality, reliability, supply assurance, and cost competitiveness
  • Assess supplier technical capability, process controls, material characterization methods, and readiness to meet Corning requirements
  • Apply material characterization and manufacturing data to understand the relationship between raw material properties and process performance
  • Partner with manufacturing teams to troubleshoot and resolve raw-material-related process and product issues
  • Lead resolution of material-related nonconformances, including technical problem-solving, corrective actions, and follow-through with suppliers and internal stakeholders
  • Identify and implement opportunities for material improvement, alternative sourcing, improved specifications, and enhanced characterization methods
  • Communicate technical findings, risks, and recommendations across supplier, manufacturing, engineering, sourcing, and R&D organizations

Travel: Up to 25%, including domestic and international

Experiences/Education - Required

  • Bachelor’s degree in Materials Science and Engineering, Ceramic Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related technical discipline
  • 7+ years of relevant engineering experience in raw materials, materials characterization, manufacturing or process engineering, supplier engineering, or material qualification
  • Demonstrated experience working directly with suppliers on technical, quality, qualification, or manufacturing-performance issues
  • Demonstrated engineering problem-solving and analytical capability
  • Ability to analyze technical data and develop sound engineering recommendations
  • Strong collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to influence across technical, manufacturing, sourcing, and supplier organizations

Experiences/Education - Desired

  • Advanced degree in relevant engineering or materials discipline
  • Experience in supplier technical assessments, supplier development, or supplier quality engineering
  • Experience with statistical analysis, experimentation, and structured problem-solving methods
  • Experience leading cross-functional technical projects
  • Experience in ceramics, minerals, powders, or other industrial raw materials

This position does not support immigration sponsorship.

Job Title: Business Analyst, Office of the CIO (Equities)

The pay range for this position at commencement of employment is expected to be between $175,000 and $200,000 per year* (see below footnote for additional compensation and benefits information).

Company Overview

Nomura is a financial services group with an integrated global network. By connecting markets East & West, we service the needs of individuals, institutions, corporates and governments through our four business divisions: Wealth Management, Investment Management, Wholesale (Global Markets and Investment Banking) and Banking.

Driven by the insights of some 28,000 people worldwide, we put our clients at the center of everything we do, delivering unparalleled access to, from, and within Asia. For further information about Nomura, visit

Aon’s Benefit Index®, Nomura’s benefits rank #1 amongst our competitors

Division Overview: NAM International

NAM International brings together a legacy of investing in public and private markets on a global scale. Through active management, we deliver differentiated and innovative solutions across equities, fixed income, multi-asset, and private credit supported by a team of disciplined and tenured investment professionals. Building upon Nomura’s century long heritage, our teams are responsible stewards of clients’ capital. We approach everything we do with accountability, curiosity, and integrity to help clients across wealth and institutional channels navigate an ever-changing market, capture opportunities around the world, and reach long-term investment goals.

Role Description:

The Business Analyst will work directly for and in close partnership with the CIO of Equities, focused on strategic content and act as a trusted analytical and execution partner; emphasizing quantitative risk analysis, performance attribution, and data-driven decision support across the diverse, multi-strategy equity platform.

The ideal candidate has a strong analytical background and is highly organized, intellectually curious, and comfortable operating with ambiguity and shifting priorities.

Responsibilities: Quantitative Risk & Performance Analysis

  • Conduct cross-desk risk, factor-exposure, and attribution analysis spanning regional, cap-size, and specialized equity strategies
  • Build risk decomposition, scenario, and factor-attribution frameworks using FactSet
  • Investigate specific questions from the CIO (e.g., "what is driving dispersion across our value strategies this quarter?") drawing on data from various analytical tools
  • Apply the firm's proprietary AI tools to accelerate data synthesis and pattern identification across the platform

Strategic Content & Executive Communications

  • Prepare high-quality strategic presentations for the CIO's use with the Executive Committee, Boards, and key clients
  • Translate complex investment and business topics into clear, compelling narratives for senior and external audiences
  • Draft talking points, briefing packs, and pre-read materials ahead of key meetings, offsites, and reviews

CIO–Support Function Liaison

  • Drive follow-through on CIO commitments and cross-functional deliverables, tracking action items to closure
  • Manage information flow to and from the CIO, ensuring the right issues are escalated with recommended paths forward

Special Projects & Firm-Wide Initiatives

  • Support ad hoc strategic initiatives and cross-platform analyses as directed by the CIO of Equities
  • Provide project support for one-off strategic efforts (e.g., new capability build-outs, M&A/lift-out evaluations, operating model changes)

Skills, experience, qualifications and knowledge required:

  • 5–8 years' experience in investment management, quantitative research, or risk analytics, ideally across multi-strategy equity platforms (regional, cap-size, or specialized)
  • Proficiency in FactSet required; working knowledge of Bloomberg expected
  • Familiarity with Style Analytics and/or Barra a plus, not required
  • Comfort adopting AI-driven analytical tools
  • Strong statistical/quantitative skillset (risk modeling, attribution, factor analysis); Python/R/SQL a plus
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication; advanced PowerPoint and Excel skills; data visualization tools a plus
  • Demonstrated ability to manage competing priorities, exercise discretion, and operate independently in a fast-paced environment
  • Experience supporting senior stakeholders and cross-functional initiatives

Nomura Leadership Behaviours

  • Explore Insights & Vision: Identify the underlying causes of problems faced by you or your team and define a clear vision and direction for the future.
  • Making Strategic Decisions: Evaluate all the options for resolving the problems and effectively prioritize actions or recommendations.
  • Inspire Entrepreneurship in People: Inspire team members through effective communication of ideas and motivate them to actively enhance productivity.
  • Elevate Organizational Capability: Engage proactively in professional development and enhance team productivity through the promotion of knowledge sharing.
  • Inclusion: Foster a culture of inclusion and psychological safety in the workplace and cultivate a "Risk Culture" (Challenge, Escalate and Respect).

title: .NET Developer
description:

title: Supervisor, Production
description:

title: Graphic Designer (Part-Time, Independent Contractor)
description:
Just Right Reader is a literacy publisher dedicated to helping children become confident, successful readers through engaging, research-based resources grounded in the Science of Reading. Our growing product line includes decodable and knowledge-building books, classroom resources, teacher guides, lesson plans, literacy games, family resources, and marketing materials designed for students from Birth through Grade 12.

We're seeking a Graphic Designer to support our Product team with the design and development of engaging, polished, and brand-aligned visual materials. This contractor will contribute to a variety of projects, including book design, product materials, flyers, presentations, and other creative assets that support our growing literacy product portfolio.

About This Engagement

This is an ongoing, project-based engagement for a versatile mid-level Graphic Designer who can independently execute a variety of design projects with an understanding of visual storytelling, brand standards, and production quality.

The ideal contractor is creative, detail-oriented, organized, and comfortable managing multiple assignments with varying timelines. Projects will be provided as business needs arise, with clear objectives, deliverables, and mutually agreed-upon deadlines.

Time Commitment & Availability

The anticipated workload is 0-20 hours per week, depending on project volume and business needs. Work is assigned on an as-needed basis, with no guaranteed minimum number of hours or assignments.

Contractors independently determine their work schedules and availability while meeting mutually agreed-upon project deadlines.

Availability Expectations: Contractors should generally respond to project inquiries and assignment requests within 24 hours, when reasonably possible, to support timely project coordination.

Scope of Work

  • Design and develop book layouts, covers, and supporting materials for Just Right Reader's literacy products.
  • Create visually engaging flyers, slide decks, presentations, and other product-related collateral.
  • Develop and adapt creative assets that align with established brand guidelines, visual standards, and product requirements.
  • Support smaller, ad hoc design projects and product-based creative needs as they arise.
  • Prepare and deliver polished, production-ready design files in appropriate formats for print and digital use.
  • Incorporate feedback and requested revisions within the scope of agreed-upon projects.
  • Independently manage assigned projects, including estimating effort, communicating progress, and delivering completed work within mutually agreed-upon timelines.

This engagement does not include internal people management, HR responsibilities, or administrative duties.

Required Experience & Qualifications

  • 3+ years of professional graphic design experience, with a portfolio demonstrating strong visual design and production capabilities.
  • Proficiency in Adobe Creative Suite, particularly Canva, InDesign, Illustrator, and Photoshop.
  • Experience designing multi-page layouts, books, presentations, marketing collateral, and other print and digital materials - including accessibility guidelines.
  • Strong understanding of typography, layout, color theory, visual hierarchy, and brand consistency.
  • Ability to interpret creative direction and independently translate concepts into polished design deliverables.
  • Strong attention to detail, organization, and the ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines.
  • Clear communication skills and the ability to work collaboratively with cross-functional stakeholders.

Preferred Experience

  • Educational publishing, children's books, literacy, or related industries.
  • Familiarity with print production processes, prepress requirements, and preparing files for professional printing.
  • Designing educational materials for teachers, students, or families.

Engagement Details

  • This role is structured as an independent contractor (1099) engagement.
  • Duration: This will be an ongoing agreement that will be evaluated for continuation on a monthly basis per business need.
  • The contractor will determine their own work schedule, methods, tools, and approach, subject to agreed-upon milestones and deadlines.
  • The contractor may provide services to other clients during the term of this engagement.
  • Compensation will be provided on a monthly retainer or project-based basis, as outlined in a separate agreement.
  • Services will be performed remotely; occasional in-person collaboration may occur by mutual agreement.

How to Express Interest

Please submit:

  1. Your resume highlighting relevant design experience.
  2. A portfolio showcasing examples of relevant graphic design work, particularly book layouts, print materials, and presentations.
  3. A brief cover letter explaining your interest in the engagement and how your experience aligns with our needs.
  4. Your preferred rate structure (hourly or project-based) and proposed rates.

Why Join Us:

At Just Right Reader, we're transforming how children learn to read. You'll be part of a passionate, growing team committed to educational equity, literacy innovation, and joyful learning.

  • Mission-driven company focused on improving literacy and education outcomes.
  • Collaborative and innovative work environment with opportunities for growth and development.
  • Competitive salary and benefits package.

Red Hat Certified Engineer (RHCE) · Active Public Trust or security clearance · DHS, DoW or civilian agency experience · Ansible, Puppet or PowerShell DSC · Azure Government or AWS GovCloud · Hybrid identity · ATO and continuous monitoring support

We’re currently seeking a qualified individual to join the Wholesale Credit Risk team in Sydney as Senior Manager, Financial Institutions Credit Risk. Reporting to the Head of Approvals, with a functional reporting line to the Head of Wholesale Credit Risk Management Australia & New Zealand, you’ll assess and make decisions on credit proposals for counterparties within the Institutional Credit Group. This includes banks, funds, non-bank financial institutions, sovereigns and Structured Finance transactions. You’ll provide independent, commercially focused credit advice within delegated Credit Approval Authority, helping HSBC maintain sound asset quality, minimise credit losses and support the strategic growth of the ICG and Structured Finance businesses within approved risk appetite.

This role has no direct or indirect reports.

Key responsibilities will include:

  • Assess and approve credit proposals for banks, funds, non-bank financial institutions, sovereigns and Structured Finance transactions within delegated Credit Approval Authority.
  • Review and make decisions on annual reviews, new-money requests, amendments and other credit matters.

  • Deliver high-quality financial analysis, risk assessments and concise recommendations to support consistent Customer Risk Rating assessments and well-informed decisions.
  • Provide early, constructive credit advice on large, complex and strategically important transactions.
  • Support the strategic growth of the Structured Finance business through timely, independent and commercially focused credit decisions.
  • Identify, monitor and escalate credit concerns promptly and appropriately, including concerns requiring referral to the Special Credit Unit.
  • Contribute to credit risk governance forums, sector reviews, Worry Watch Monitor activities and portfolio management information.
  • Partner with senior stakeholders across CIB, the Institutional Credit Group, Structured Finance, Product Management and regional and local Risk functions.
  • Balance customer and business needs with prudent credit risk management, sustainable growth and economic-profit objectives.
  • Ensure credit decisions, approval conditions, monitoring requirements and related documentation are clear, accurate and completed within service-level commitments.
  • Comply with HSBC’s credit risk management framework, internal policies, procedures, control standards and applicable regulatory requirements.
  • Support operational risk management and the implementation of audit and regulatory recommendations.
  • Share expertise and provide coaching, mentoring and support to Risk colleagues to promote consistent credit standards across the organisation.

To be successful in the role you will need:

  • Significant experience in financial institutions credit risk, wholesale credit risk or a closely related discipline, including assessment and approval of complex and material exposures.
  • Strong technical capability in financial analysis, cash-flow assessment, credit structuring, risk grading and portfolio risk management.
  • Demonstrated experience covering one or more of the following: banks, funds, non-bank financial institutions, sovereigns and Structured Finance.
  • Strong understanding of complex and higher-value transactions, including structured finance, leveraged finance, project finance, commercial real estate or similar areas.
  • Proven ability to assess counterparties, transaction structures, risk mitigants and portfolio implications.
  • Sound commercial judgement and the ability to make independent, timely credit decisions within delegated authority and service-level requirements.
  • Detailed knowledge of credit risk governance, internal policies, control frameworks and regulatory expectations.
  • A strong focus on asset quality, loss prevention, appropriate escalation and maintaining a conservative credit culture.
  • Current understanding of macroeconomic and financial-market developments, and their impact on country, sector, counterparty and product risk.
  • Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to influence senior business and Risk leaders while maintaining independent credit judgement.
  • A collaborative leadership style, with the ability to coach, mentor and share subject-matter expertise with colleagues.

Job Description

This position serves as a Project Purchasing Manager on small- to medium-sized Engineering, Procurement, Fabrication, and Construction (EPFC) projects, or may serve as a regional manager for non-project procurement.

• Serve as project member in the formulation of plans and the execution of the overall material management activity and/or assist in the planning and execution of specialized Material Management activities (material control, procurement, expediting, logistics, inspection, or field material management) for the project or office, as applicable

• Manage the procurement work process and reports the material management status of purchased material and equipment from the time of purchase through receipt at assigned points of use

• Manage the development of all purchasing and Material Management activities from the requisition to close-out, and assign requisitions, including Request for Quotation or Proposal packages to appropriate procurement and other material management personnel

• Responsible for the implementation, management, and monitoring of the Material Management Work Process with the approved Corporate Reference Tool for Material Management to meet project requirements and schedule
