title: New Business Representative
description:
Requisition ID # 175616

Job Category: Project / Program Management

Job Level: Individual Contributor

Business Unit: Energy Delivery

Work Type: Hybrid

Job Location: San Jose

Department Overview

The Strategy and Growth functional area is dedicated to long-term strategic and infrastructure planning. With electricity demand expected to double over the next 15 years, we’re building an energy system of the future for the world’s fourth-largest economy. It includes Energy Policy and Procurement, Strategy and Innovation, Integrated Long-Term Planning, and the Commercial Growth Organization.

Position Summary

This job is represented by Engineers and Scientists of California (ESC) and subject to collective bargaining.

This is a Beginning Level Classification. Additional consideration may be given to candidates who reside within 50 miles of the headquarters.

The headquarters for this position will either be located in San Jose or Cupertino.

This position is charged with customer contact, project coordination, billing, and contract preparation in connection with less complex installation of new business gas and/or electric facilities. NBRs will not prepare job estimates. This does not preclude job owners from preparing invoices or contracts based on simplified charge methodology.

A New Business Representative may be assigned no more than 50% of their workload in SNBR-level jobs at the same time and must work under the guidance of a Senior New Business Representative or IPE.

Employees hired into this classification from outside the bargaining unit will not have their bids or transfers considered under the provisions of title 21 for a period of 24 months following their employment date (“employment date” means the date placed into the regular classification, not date of hire with PG&E if different)

Employees in this classification may still bid to higher classifications in the same line of progression while still within the 24-month period.

This position is hybrid, working from your remote office and your assigned work location based on business need. The assigned work location will be within the PG&E Service Territory.

PG&E is providing the hourly rate that the company in good faith believes it might pay for this position at the time of the job posting. This position is subject to collectively bargained hourly wage rates and increases. The starting wage rate for this position is $51.01 per hour. This wage rate is specific to the locality of the job. The wage rate is based on multiple factors, including, but not limited to, specific skills, education, licenses or certifications, experience, market value, geographic location, collective bargaining agreements, and internal equity.

Job Responsibilities

SAFETY

  • Maximize public and employee safety by ensuring that job designs are performed to Company and State standards and meet all compliance requirements.

PROJECT MANAGEMENT

  • Prepares pre-design job packages with all required information including field sketch layouts for the scoping of construction and accurate field data including pictures measurements.
  • Manages scope and schedule and cost for all assigned projects, from initiation to meter set.
  • Coordinates all other departments or individuals who are involved with the project and works to define the project’s background, objective, design scope, schedule, roles, and responsibilities.
  • Coordinates with internal and external stakeholders to complete the project in a timely manner. Includes understanding of project schedules and working closely with the work and resource group to prioritize work using available tools or technology.
  • Proactively manages a new business portfolio of work to ensure compliance to standard work or ensures variances are in accordance with company guidelines. Effectively monitors project schedule and prioritizes work in coordination with dependency partners and construction execution teams.
  • Schedules and conducts project meetings, provides all pertinent data and addresses potential project risks including schedule setbacks and coordinates actions before setbacks occur.
  • Ensures that project is performed as planned or manages project delays in accordance with company guidelines.
  • Looks for ways to minimize costs on projects for both the applicant and PG&E.
  • Ensures that the correct type of financial order, work category, etc., has been applied and actively monitors costs.

FIELDING

  • Fielding including job site visits and customer meetings are required. Fielding will include but not limited to site visits for pre-design job package creation. facilitating pre-construction meetings, verifying site readiness and any emergent issues that might require a site visit.
  • NBRs will gather information on field conditions for pre-design packages for single locations. A single location is defined as one or more of the following:

a. Electric: Nearest point of electric distribution to panel, service work only if within 200 feet for Under Ground (UG) or 150 Over Head (OH).

b. Gas: Nearest point of gas distribution main to single meter location, service work only, if within 200 feet.

If a and/or b occurs more than once within a single premise, NBRs will field these as well (Example: House and Pump). At all other locations, the Job Owners Checklist is required, and the Field Notes Template is optional for each NBR, who will consult with their assigned mentor or supervisor as to whether collecting that information will be efficient.

COMMUNICATION

  • Communicates project status (e.g., scope, schedule, and cost) to all stakeholders throughout the project, as applicable.
  • Facilitates resolution of project-related disputes. Continuous formal communication (both written and verbal) with all stakeholders is given a high priority throughout all stages of the project.
  • Prepares contracts, as applicable, to ensure compliance with standards and tariffs.
  • Provides applicants, estimating, engineering, clerical and construction partners with complete and accurate information on rate and rule applicability, potential costs and timelines.

MANAGING CUSTOMER EXPECTATIONS

  • Proactively communicates to project stakeholders, both internal and external.
  • Negotiates reasonable estimating and construction dates that address customer’s anticipated schedules and meets compliance requirements, including communications and timelines. May provide customer with an initial non-binding cost.

TARIFFS

  • Ensures that all charges mandated under the applicable tariffs are identified in the contract and secured before beginning construction. This position is responsible for ensuring correct tariff interpretation and application, and for working with Law department on exceptional case projects when required.
  • Partner with other PG&E departments and/or rates and tariffs for application of best rates when appropriate.

COMPLIANCE MANAGEMENT

  • Ensures all applicable project documentation is maintained in the system of record.
  • Ensures all project dependencies are met prior to allowing a construction start.

Qualifications

Minimum:

  • Bachelor’s degree from a recognized college or its equivalent experience. Such experience must include three (3) or more years of experience in construction project management or PG&E technical service planning or 12 months of experience as a Hiring Hall (HH) New Business Representative, HH Senior New Business Representative and/or HH Engineering Estimator
  • Must have strong project management, customer contact and communications skills. Basic computer skills including Microsoft Word, Excel, email.
  • Valid California Driver's License and California minimum insurance coverage if using personal car
  • Driving is an essential function of this job, therefore the employee must have and maintain a valid driver’s license.

Desired:

  • Additional consideration may be given to candidates that reside within 50 miles of the headquarters
  • Must have strong project management, customer contact and communications skills. Basic computer skills including Microsoft Word, Excel, email.
  • Familiar with tariffs, rates, contracts/tools, Work Management (WM) SAP and work processes and tools.
  • Works effectively as a member of a team
  • Ability to work with both internal and external customers/clients
  • Facilitation and conflict resolution skills
  • Ability to manage for results and in the process work as a team to build agreement
  • Strong focus on safety
  • Committed to providing superior and proactive customer service
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills
  • Ability to demonstrate initiative and decisiveness
  • Ability to demonstrate sound judgment and forward thinking
  • Problem solving skills
  • Computer skills (SAP, Microsoft Excel, Word, etc.)
  • Conflict resolution skills
  • Measurement skills and ability to use some physical tools (drive stake in the ground, use Range Finder or Height Stick and Shovel, etc.) in the field

Pre-Employment Testing:

  • Internal PG&E Employees: Qualified on the Physical Test Battery (PTB) and Work Orientation Inventory (WOI) prior to applying
  • External and Hiring Hall Candidates: Qualified on the Physical Test Battery (PTB) and Work Orientation Inventory (WOI) prior to interviewing

title: Product Engineer (80-100%)
description:
Introduction

Great products do not happen by chance. They result from clear requirements, sound technical decisions, and effective collaboration throughout the entire product lifecycle. As a Product Engineer, you will help shape our Sensors & Meters portfolio, from initial product concepts and feasibility studies through development and industrialization to continuous product improvement. You will take ownership of technically complex workstreams, coordinate cross-functional contributors, and serve as a key technical contact for a defined part of our product portfolio.

What You'll Do

  • Develop and manage products throughout their entire lifecycle within the Sensors & Meters portfolio, from initial concept through production and ongoing product improvement.

  • Lead product-related activities in development projects and act as a key interface between Product Owners, Product Management, R&D Engineers, Supply Chain, Quality, Operations, and other engineering disciplines.

  • Drive the successful realization of innovative product variants and feature enhancements by coordinating cross-functional activities and ensuring the correct technical implementation.

  • Coordinate cross-functional product design activities, including FMEA, verification, validation, certification, and design transfer to production, while maintaining a holistic view across the product and its interfaces.

  • Define, manage, and document product requirements and specifications, ensuring that technical requirements are clearly understood and correctly implemented.

  • Drive product improvements, cost optimization, and complexity reduction as part of continuous portfolio development.

  • Conduct feasibility studies, evaluate technical concepts, and support competitor assessments to shape and develop the product portfolio.

  • Analyze product issues, determine root causes, implement corrective actions, and support quality cases, including design-related quality topics.

  • Ensure complete, accurate, and well-maintained product documentation throughout the entire product lifecycle.

  • Share knowledge, provide guidance to colleagues, and actively contribute to strengthening engineering capabilities within the team.

Who you are

  • You hold a university degree in physics, electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, or a related technical discipline.
  • You bring several years of substantial experience in product development, product engineering, or product lifecycle management, preferably involving sensors, measurement devices, or technically complex products.
  • You have a strong interdisciplinary understanding of systems and sound knowledge of requirements engineering.
  • You have a proven ability to lead complex technical topics and make decisions based on incomplete or sometimes conflicting information.
  • You know how to coordinate cross-functional teams, drive results, and establish alignment.
  • You have a structured, analytical, and solution-oriented working style combined with a pragmatic approach to execution.
  • You are fluent in English; German is an advantage.

Ready to help shape the next generation of Belimo sensors and meters? We look forward to your application.

People at Belimo

Smart buildings start with dedicated people. We bring talented people together and foster an environment to succeed. At Belimo, respect, trust, and support across departments help ideas move quickly into real-world solutions, because we achieve more together than we ever could alone. .

About Belimo

Belimo is the global market leader in the development, production, and sales of field devices for the energy-efficient control of heating, ventilation and air-conditioning systems. The focus of our core business is on damper actuators, control valves, sensors and meters. Founded in 1975, the company has been listed on the Swiss Exchange (SIX) since 1995.

Compensation & Benefits

At Belimo, we believe in fair, equitable, and competitive compensation. We offer pay that reflects your skills, experience, education, and location. Beyond compensation, you'll benefit from a comprehensive rewards package designed to support your health, financial wellbeing, and long-term success. Belimo is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer.

Wärtsilä is an innovative technology company known for being a forerunner in the Marine and Energy markets. Every day, we – Wärtsilians - put our hearts and minds into turning Wärtsilä's purpose of enabling sustainable societies through innovation in technology and services into reality. Our ultimate aim is to provide increased value to both our customers and society. New, game-changing ideas and continuous improvement have been part of our DNA since 1834. Together, we can create new business opportunities and more sustainable future that we can all be proud of.

We want to transition the world towards a decarbonised and sustainable future. By pushing the boundaries of engineering and technology, we can make it work. We are always on the lookout for future-oriented talent – want to join the ride?

Estamos buscando un Shift Supervisor para liderar las actividades operativas de planta durante su turno, asegurando la continuidad operacional, el cumplimiento de los parámetros de desempeño y la correcta ejecución de las actividades de operación y mantenimiento.
El rol requiere coordinar al equipo de turno, monitorear indicadores operativos, gestionar eventos y contingencias, garantizar el cumplimiento de los procedimientos técnicos, de seguridad y asegurar que la operación de los equipos se realice conforme a los requisitos contractuales y las mejores prácticas de la industria.


 Detalles de la vacante:

  • Ubicación: Pesquería, Nuevo León.
  • Modalidad de trabajo: Presencial.
  • Tipo de contrato: a término indefinido.
  • Turnos: rotativos.

Principales responsabilidades:

  • Supervisar y coordinar la operación de planta y de los equipos asignados durante el turno.
  • Monitorear y gestionar los KPIs operativos para asegurar el cumplimiento de los niveles de desempeño establecidos contractualmente.
  • Garantizar el cumplimiento de los objetivos de producción, disponibilidad y confiabilidad de la planta.
  • Implementar y asegurar la correcta aplicación de procedimientos y estándares de operación y mantenimiento.
  • Coordinar inspecciones, actividades operativas y tareas de mantenimiento conforme a los estándares de seguridad, calidad y medio ambiente.
  • Liderar y ejecutar maniobras operativas, respondiendo oportunamente a eventos, desviaciones o contingencias operacionales.
  • Analizar y registrar parámetros operativos para optimizar el desempeño de los equipos y apoyar la toma de decisiones operativas.

Requisitos mínimos para aplicar:

  • Licenciatura en Ingeniería electrónica / Electromecánica o automatización.
  • Mínimo 2 - 3 años como operador y/o supervisor en cuartos de control.
  • Conocimientos solidos en SCADA / HDMI y generadores de energía.

Requisitos adicionales (considerados un Plus)

  • Inglés intermedio.
  • Conocimiento de motores de combustión.

Last application date:

At Wärtsilä we value, respect and embrace all our differences, and are committed to diversity, inclusion and equal employment opportunities; everyone can be their true self and succeed based on their job-relevant merits and abilities.

Please note that according to Wärtsilä policy, voluntary consent for a security check may be required from candidates being considered for this position, depending on the applicable country.

This is Wärtsilä

Wärtsilä is a global leader in innovative technologies and lifecycle solutions for the marine and energy markets. Our team of 18,300 professionals, in more than 230 locations in 77 countries, shape the decarbonisation transformation of our industries across the globe. Read more on .

title: Senior Project Manager TSSSA & Fleet (Temporary Opportunity until 28/02/2030)
description:
You may have been part of some big projects before, but this work is legacy-building.

You have the opportunity to gain a wealth of expertise and a diverse range of skills, providing insight and knowledge without losing sight of your work-life balance or wellbeing.

In this role, you'll:


Join the Future Fleet Program where we have 2 exciting opportunities in the Rolling Stock delivery team, for Senior Project Managers.

The Future Fleet Program is a $12 billion NSW Government commitment to rebuild train manufacturing in NSW, including a new state-owned train manufacturing facility in the Hunter. FFP will establish a long-term pipeline of passenger train manufacturing and fleet replacement, beginning with Sydney's ageing Tangara fleet and extending to the Millennium, Oscar and Waratah fleets over the coming decades. This is a rare opportunity to help shape and deliver a generational program from its early stages.



In both roles, you will provide leadership, governance and strategic oversight to ensure project activities are delivered safely and efficiently. You will lead procurement readiness and delivery readiness activities, and develop and manage project plans, schedules, budgets and forecasts across the project lifecycle, from design and manufacturing through to testing, commissioning, fleet acceptance and entry into service. You will support technical development and design delivery, and drive operational integration and the development of maintenance strategies with operational and maintenance stakeholders. You will also manage external service providers and stakeholders, lead the development of contract scopes and commercial principles, and manage procurement activities for your work packages.

Both Senior Project Manager opportunities are temporary until 28/02/2030 with the potential to extend. You will receive an attractive remuneration package within the TSSM Band. You will have hybrid flexibility where you can mix work-from-home with office-based days. Positions may be located in Sydney or Newcastle.

Senior Project Manager Fleet: This role is focused on developing the rollingstock package through the procurement phase, through concept development, requirements definition and procurement readiness, to contract award and mobilisation.


• Lead development and scoping of rollingstock package, including project, product, stakeholder and technical inputs
• Lead the development and coordination of operational integration requirements, bringing together stakeholder inputs and managing key interfaces to define the scope for procurement
• Coordinate concept development and definition of stakeholder, operational and technical requirements to inform the procurement approach
• Prepare and manage project plans and schedules for the rollingstock packages, including key procurement readiness activities and deliverables

Senior Project Manager TSSA: This role is focused on developing the transitional and through-life support, maintenance and operational requirements through the procurement and delivery readiness phase.


• Lead development and scoping of rollingstock package, including project, product, stakeholder and technical inputs
• Lead the development and coordination of operational integration requirements, bringing together stakeholder inputs and managing key interfaces to define the scope for procurement
• Manage the development of maintenance concepts and requirements, coordinating inputs across facilities, spares, tooling, training and supporting systems to establish clear procurement scopes and deliverables
• Coordinate asset management and performance requirements, including reliability, availability and whole-of-life outcomes, ensuring these are captured, agreed and incorporated into procurement documentation.

For more information on this position and business unit, view the role description and information pack.

About you


Demonstrated experience working in rollingstock (essential), including delivery, design, integration or maintenance of rail fleet. Proven experience managing large-scale, complex projects, including planning, procurement, scheduling, budgets and risk management. Strong understanding of the rollingstock lifecycle, from procurement and design through to commissioning, acceptance and entry into service. Experience engaging and influencing senior stakeholders, suppliers and multidisciplinary teams. Knowledge of rail safety, standards and assurance requirements.

Who we are


Transport for NSW provides a safe, integrated, and efficient transport system. We connect people, communities and industry every day.

Join us

Our workforce is as diverse as the community we serve. If you’d like further information on our inclusion and diversity initiatives, visit Transport careers.

Flexible work options may be available. Learn more via Flexible work options and policy

Apply today

Applications close 11:59 PM Thursday 19 November 2026

For more information about this role, please contact NICHOLAS.BRADY@TRANSPORT.NSW.GOV.AU.

Aboriginal people and people living with disability are supported throughout the recruitment process and at work, and we encourage you to apply. Visit Supporting Aboriginal People or Supporting People with Disability for more information or speak to your talent team member to arrange any adjustments to how you interact with us.

title: Clinical Data Manager
description:
Job Title:Clinical Data Manager

Job Location: Bangalore

Department: Clinical Data Management

About Syngene: Syngene () is an innovation-led contract research, development and manufacturing organization offering integrated scientific services from early discovery to commercial supply.

At Syngene, safety is at the heart of everything we do personally and professionally. Syngene has placed safety at par with business performance with shared responsibility and accountability, including following safety guidelines, procedures and SOPs, in letter and spirit

Mandatory expectation for all roles as per Syngene safety guidelines

  • Overall adherence to safe practices and procedures of oneself and the teams aligned
  • Contributing to development of procedures, practices and systems that ensures safe operations and compliance to company’s integrity & quality standards
  • Driving a corporate culture that promotes environment, health, and safety (EHS) mindset and operational discipline at the workplace at all times.
  • Ensuring safety of self, teams and lab/plant by adhering to safety protocols and following environment, health, and safety (EHS) requirements at all times in the workplace.
  • Ensure all assigned mandatory trainings related to data integrity, health, and safety measures are completed on time by all members of the team including self
  • Compliance to Syngene’ s quality standards at all times
  • Hold self and their teams accountable for the achievement of safety goals
  • Govern and Review safety metrics from time to time

Core Purpose of the Role:

To independently perform and coordinate clinical data management activities for assigned clinical studies, ensuring accurate, complete, consistent, and GCP/regulatory-compliant clinical trial data. The role is responsible for data review and validation, query management, discrepancy resolution, reconciliation activities, and support for database cleaning and lock activities. Additionally, the role assists in stakeholder communication, ensures adherence to established processes and timelines, and provides guidance to junior team members to support high-quality study deliverables.

Role Accountabilities

  • Accountable for executing assigned clinical data management activities in accordance with study requirements, timelines, SOPs, and regulatory guidelines.
  • Accountable for performing data review, validation, and cleaning activities to ensure data accuracy, completeness, and consistency.
  • Accountable for raising, tracking, and facilitating timely resolution of data queries with investigative sites and internal stakeholders.
  • Accountable for monitoring CRF/eCRF completion, query status, and data discrepancies to support study milestones.
  • Accountable for supporting CRF/eCRF review, database testing, and User Acceptance Testing (UAT) activities as assigned.
  • Accountable for conducting routine data quality checks and escalating data issues, risks, or trends to the Data Manager in a timely manner.
  • Accountable for supporting data reconciliation activities, including SAE, laboratory, and other external vendor data reviews as applicable.
  • Accountable for maintaining accurate, complete, and inspection-ready study documentation and tracking records.
  • Accountable for supporting database lock and study closeout activities through completion of assigned data cleaning tasks.
  • Accountable for ensuring compliance with applicable SOPs, ICH-GCP guidelines, protocol requirements, and sponsor expectations.
  • Accountable for preparing study metrics, status reports, and data management deliverables as requested.
  • Accountable for collaborating effectively with cross-functional teams to support smooth study execution and issue resolution.
  • Accountable for sharing knowledge, supporting onboarding activities, and providing guidance to junior team members when required.
  • Accountable for identifying opportunities for process improvements and contributing to quality and operational excellence initiatives.
  • Accountable for completing assigned tasks within agreed timelines while maintaining high standards of quality and compliance.
  • Accountable for performing additional responsibilities assigned by the reporting manager in support of departmental and organizational objectives.

Leadership & Team Support

  • Provide guidance, coaching, and training to junior data management team members.
  • Support timely delivery of study milestones while ensuring data quality and compliance.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement of data management processes and best practices.
  • Support audit and inspection readiness activities and ensure adherence to SOPs and quality requirements.
  • Assist management with resource planning and workload coordination, as needed.

Syngene Values

All employees will consistently demonstrate alignment with our core values

  • Excellence
  • Integrity
  • Professionalism

Specific requirements for this role

Experience

  • 5-6 years of experience in Clinical Data Management within CRO, pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or clinical research organizations.
  • Experience managing Phase I-IV clinical trials, observational studies, and/or real-world evidence studies.
  • Hands-on experience in end-to-end clinical data management activities including study startup, database review, data cleaning, query management, and database lock.
  • Experience in CRF/eCRF design, edit check specification development, and database validation review.
  • Experience using EDC systems and clinical databases.
  • Experience interacting with sponsors and cross-functional study teams.
  • Experience supporting audits, inspections, and quality compliance activities.
  • Experience mentoring junior team members and coordinating study-level activities.

Skills and Capabilities

  • Good understanding of Clinical Data Management processes and clinical trial data lifecycle.
  • Strong data review, validation, discrepancy management, and query resolution skills.
  • Proficiency in EDC systems and clinical databases.
  • Working knowledge of ICH-GCP, regulatory requirements, and data quality standards.
  • Familiarity with database lock and reconciliation activities.
  • Good analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks and meet timelines.
  • Effective communication and cross-functional collaboration skills.
  • Good documentation and reporting skills.
  • Demonstrates accountability, attention to detail, and a quality-focused mindset.

Education

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Life Sciences, Pharmacy, Biotechnology, Clinical Research, Health Sciences, or a related discipline.
  • Certification or training in ICH-GCP, Clinical Data Management, EDC systems, or regulatory compliance is desirable.

Equal Opportunity Employer:

It is the policy of Syngene to provide equal employment opportunity (EEO) to all persons regardless of age, color, national origin, citizenship status, physical or mental disability, race, religion, creed, gender, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, genetic information, marital status, status with regard to public assistance, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable legislation or local law. In addition, Syngene will provide reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities.

title: Global Technology Change Risk
description:
ABOUT US:

As a world leading provider of integrated solutions for the alternative investment industry, Alter Domus (meaning “The Other House” in Latin) is proud to be home to 90% of the top 30 asset managers in the private markets, and more than 6,000 professionals across 24 jurisdictions.

With a deep understanding of what it takes to succeed in alternatives, we believe in being different - in what we do, in how we work and most importantly in how we enable and develop our people. Invest yourself in the alternative, and join an organization where you progress on merit, where you can speak openly with whoever you are speaking to, and where you will be supported along whichever path you choose to take.

Find out more about life at Alter Domus at careers.alterdomus.com

Reporting to the Head of Technology, Security and Data Risk, the Global Technology Change Risk Senior Manager will lead the risk oversight of the unprecedented amount of technology change at Alter Domus. You will bring deep knowledge of modern technology architecture, infrastructure, data, applications and ai, have strong risk management experience and a good understanding of agile and waterfall project management.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Lead the technology change risk programme ensuring all material technology-driven changes (ai, data, system, migrations, automation, digital transformation initiatives) are assessed for risk prior to and during execution.
  • Partner with Tech, project delivery, and business stakeholders to embed risk controls into the change management lifecycle, from intake and impact assessment through testing, deployment, and post-implementation review.
  • Identify, evaluate, and monitor technology and operational risks arising from global change initiatives, escalating material issues to senior leadership and relevant risk committees.
  • Assess risks specific to AI adoption within change initiatives, including model governance, data privacy, algorithmic bias, and regulatory compliance, and ensure AI-driven tools and processes are incorporated safely into the change risk framework.
  • Provide guidance, training, and thought leadership to project teams and junior risk staff on technology change risk best practices, fostering a proactive risk culture across the organization.
  • Develop and maintain risk metrics, dashboards, and reporting to provide visibility into the change risk portfolio for executive and regulatory stakeholders.
  • As a senior leader, you will also be responsible for driving change when necessary, delivering communications and directions to the team in supporting the development and engagement of employees at all levels.
  • Promote and build the Alter Domus brand and culture both internally and externally, acting as an ambassador and role model to our people, clients, and customers to embed the Alter Domus Values and to promote our Employer Value Proposition.
  • As a director of Alter Domus, you will maintain a relentless focus on cost and budget discipline, driving a culture of accountability.
  • Drive a culture of compliance and risk control to mitigate financial, operational and reputational risks.
  • Ensure the company maintains the highest Environmental, Sustainability and Governance (ESG) standards.

PROFILE

  • Deep knowledge of modern technology architecture, infrastructure, data, applications and ai,
  • Strong risk management experience
  • Deep understanding of technology project delivery (agile and waterfall project management).
  • A motivation to built on the role and develop operational resilience to meet the expectations of our clients and regulators alike.

LEADERSHIP & BEHAVIOURAL COMPETENCIES

  • You will demonstrate super business insight and commercial acumen combined with strong technical expertise, analytical problem-solving skills
  • Hands-on subject matter expert capable of taking on a wide range of tasks with humility and flexibility.
  • You will possess strong interpersonal skills – influencing and building trust quickly, navigating complexity and ambiguity with confidence and negotiating with tenacity and focus. You will be decisive and persuasive to achieve the results and adept at engaging with C-level executives and high-profile clients.
  • You will have a proven track-record of working autonomously in a matrixed organisation and demonstrate strong partnering skills, using them to build internal networks to achieve your objectives.
  • You will have an intellectual curiosity and a global mind-set, allowing you to partner effectively across your region and beyond with agility and flexibility. You will challenge the current status quo to improve things, acting as a change agent to drive the business forward.
  • You will have high energy and passion to drive the business and positively influence others, you will avoid complacency and strive for the business to succeed, acting quickly to tackle any issues
  • You will be adept at managing competing demands on your time, actively prioritising and remaining calm under pressure while navigating complexity and challenges with confidence and resilience.
  • Possess personal learning agility and an ability to adopt and champion new skills and ways of working to role model and inspire others.
  • You will demonstrate a strong commitment to high integrity and ethics

KEY RELATIONSHIPS

  • Supervisory Board / Audit and Risk Committee, Group Executive Board
  • Regional Executives, Leaders, Directors and Senior Managers
  • Finance, IT and Human Resources

WHAT WE OFFER

We are committed to supporting your development, advancing your career, and providing benefits that matter to you.

Our industry-leading Alter Domus Academy offers six learning zones for every stage of your career, with resources tailored to your ambitions and resources from LinkedIn Learning.

Our global benefits also include:

  • Support for professional accreditations such as ACCA and study leave
  • Flexible arrangements, generous holidays, plus an additional day off for your birthday!
  • Continuous mentoring along your career progression
  • Active sports, events and social committees across our offices
  • 24/7 support available from our Employee Assistance Program
  • The opportunity to invest in our growth and success through our Employee Share Plan
  • Plus additional local benefits depending on your location

Alter Domus is an Equal Opportunity Employer: Equity Statement
All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status.

title: Senior Planner - Transportation Safety | Metropolitan Planning & Analysis
description:
About Houston-Galveston Area Council

The Houston-Galveston Area Council (H-GAC) is one of the largest regional planning commissions in the country with a diverse service area of 13 counties and more than 7 million people. We are the pulse of our region addressing issues that cross city limits and county lines every single day.

We make decisions that affect our transportation system, ensure the safety and well-being of our seniors, connect people to jobs, help families recover from natural disasters, preserve water quality for our children, and so much more. We work to make the region a great place to live, work, and thrive.

What Will I Be Doing?

H-GAC’s Safety and Operations division developed a comprehensive road safety plan that identifies projects, programs, and policies to reduce traffic fatalities and serious injuries across the eight-county Metropolitan Planning Area.
Under the general direction of the Supervisor of Transportation Safety, the Senior Planner of Transportation Safety will support a range of transportation safety planning, program development, project implementation, funding, performance monitoring, operations, and coordination activities. Responsibilities may evolve based on agency priorities, regional needs, and program development, and will include the following and other duties as assigned:
  • Support the development and implementation of transportation safety plans, programs, policies, and initiatives that reduce fatal and serious-injury crashes throughout the region.
  • Manage consultant-led projects, including developing scopes, schedules, budgets, and procurement documents; reviewing deliverables and invoices; and monitoring contract performance.
  • Coordinate transportation safety studies and project-development activities.
  • Develop technical guidance, data resources, and educational materials to help local agencies apply proven roadway safety practices.
  • Support calls for projects, project prioritization, and other funding initiatives. Provide technical assistance to local sponsors.
  • Support the administration of the Transportation Safety Committee and present safety information and recommendations to H-GAC committees, elected officials, partner agencies, and other stakeholders.
  • Convene and coordinate with local governments, TxDOT, law enforcement, public health organizations, school districts, transportation providers, advocacy organizations, and other multidisciplinary partners.
  • Perform other transportation planning, program-management and/or operations duties as assigned.

Key Qualifications
  • Experience working for a local government, county, metropolitan planning organization, or other regional public agency.
  • Collaborative, adaptable team member with strong project management, communication, and presentation skills.
  • Knowledge of transportation safety planning, performance management, and funding processes at the federal, state, and regional levels.
  • Experience translating adopted safety plans into programs, projects, funding strategies, and measurable outcomes.
  • Experience managing complex projects, including the oversight of consultants, contracts, budgets, and diverse stakeholders in accordance with applicable requirements.

Do you have…
  • Bachelor’s degree in an applicable academic discipline or related field of study
  • 5 years of experience in related job duties

Preferred Qualifications
  • A bachelor’s/master’s degree in urban planning, transportation planning, transportation engineering, public administration, public policy, geography, data analytics, or a related field.
  • Experience working for a local government, county, metropolitan planning organization, or other regional public agency.
  • Experience with geographic information systems, crash databases, safety analysis tools, data visualization platforms, or statistical analysis.
  • Experience conducting or overseeing crash analysis, network screening, safety performance monitoring, or before-and-after evaluations.
  • Experience managing consultant-led planning or technical studies.

All employees of H-GAC are required to reside within the agency’s region of service to support our commitment to excellence in service of our region.

H-GAC is an equal opportunity/ADA employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin, or protected veteran status.

title: Cleared Senior/Principal R&D Systems Engineer - Interconnectivity and Verification, Onsite
description:
About Sandia

Sandia National Laboratories is the nation’s premier science and engineering lab for national security and technology innovation, with teams of specialists focused on cutting-edge work in a broad array of areas. Some of the main reasons we love our jobs:

  • Challenging work with amazing impact that contributes to security, peace, and freedom worldwide
  • Extraordinary co-workers
  • Some of the best tools, equipment, and research facilities in the world
  • Career advancement and enrichment opportunities
  • Flexible work arrangements for many positions include 9/80 (work 80 hours every two weeks, with every other Friday off) and 4/10 (work 4 ten-hour days each week) compressed workweeks, part-time work, and telecommuting (a mix of onsite work and working from home)
  • Generous vacation, strong medical and other benefits, competitive 401k, learning opportunities, relocation assistance and amenities aimed at creating a solid work/life balance*

World-changing technologies. Life-changing careers. Learn more about Sandia at: http://www.sandia.gov


*These benefits vary by job classification.

What Your Job Will Be Like

We are seeking an R&D Systems Engineer to support our dynamic group in the Mobile Guardian Transport Program Management and System Engineering group.

On any given day, you may be called on to:

  • Use systems engineering principles to implement multidisciplinary engineering approaches to research, design, or develop structures, experiments, processes, systems, theories, or technologies; to construct or operate the same with full cognizance of their design or to forecast their behavior.
  • Initiate, design, develop, execute, and evaluate new processes, products, or systems through basic and applied systems engineering research.
  • Utilize creativity and critical thinking in Systems Engineering principles to proactively discern, identify, troubleshoot and mitigate requirements, design, and manufacturing challenges to ensure successful product realization in partnership with a variety of subsystem teams and sponsor needs.
  • Support preparation of all detailed system documentation, to include failure mode analysis, system behaviors, interface control documents, system design specifications, requirement verification reports, etc.
  • Support the analysis and interpretation of test data and recommend alternative solutions to problems and obstacles.
  • Work on a specific task basis to support or lead technical activities across multiple disciplines including electrical engineering, systems engineering, mechanical engineering, software engineering, and security.

Due to the nature of this work the selected applicant must be able to work onsite.

Salary Range

$117,500 - $235,700

*Salary range is estimated, and actual salary will be determined after consideration of the selected candidate's experience and qualifications, and application of any approved geographic salary differential.

Qualifications We Require

  • A Bachelor's degree in a relevant discipline and five (5) years of directly relevant experience, or an equivalent combination of directly relevant education and engineering or scientific experience that demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and ability to perform independent research and development.¿
  • Active DOE Q clearance or Equivalent

Qualifications We Desire

The ideal R&D S&E Systems Engineering candidate for Sandia National Laboratories will in addition possess the following:

  • Graduate degree in Engineering or a highly related field where an independent research project was a graduation requirement (e.g., independent project, thesis, or dissertation).¿
  • Experience working with Nuclear Security Enterprise (NSE) laboratories and plants including Pantex, Kansas City National Security Campus (KCNSC), Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL), Los Alamos National Laboratory, and Kansas City National Security Campus/New Mexico Operations (KCNSC/NMO).¿
  • Experience working on engineering design, qualification, production, or related modeling/simulation projects.¿
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills, ability to work effectively in multidisciplinary teams.

Also, for this posting we are seeking individuals with the following experience:

  • 4 years of system engineering experience
  • Demonstrated ability to conceptualize, understand, execute on, and communicate major elements of design, engineering, maintenance, processes, or policies.
  • Ability and confidence working in a classified environment and with classified components
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team in a fast-paced, dynamic environment
  • Ability to model behaviors that reflect Sandia's core values
  • Experience with:
    • Design Agency/ Production Agency partnerships
    • Working in a schedule, budget, or requirement constrained environment
    • Complex electrical, mechanical, software, and/or integrated system designs development, prototype, and test
    • Defining technical requirements, validating execution of requirements, planning, designing, integrating, implementing, and testing engineering solutions
    • Modified commercial of the shelf parts and definition
    • System and subsystem description documents
    • Documentation, design processes, and requirements including release in EIMS or PRIME
    • Ability to emphasize small details and orders of operations by breaking down systems into manageable and discrete parts for better understanding and troubleshooting.
    • Awareness of engineering principles and basic technical responsibilities, including design and systems technology, within a designated subject area

About Our Team

Mobile Guardian Transport Program Management and System Engineering (SE) department is responsible for the overall system design, requirement adherence, and performance of the next generation safe and secure transportation system. This system includes electrical, mechanical, and security components in a complex architecture with custom embedded software and requiring a diverse, technical SE team. In addition, we provide program leadership and coordination to the MGT program team.

Posting Duration

This posting will be open for application submissions for a minimum of three (3) calendar days, including the 'posting date'. Sandia reserves the right to extend the posting date at any time.

Security Clearance

Position requires a Department of Energy (DOE) Q security clearance to start, or equivalent active security clearance with another U.S. government agency (e.g., DOD). Sandia is required by DOE directive to conduct a pre-employment drug test and background review that includes checks of personal references, credit, law enforcement records, and employment/education verifications. Applicants for employment need to be able to maintain a DOE Q-level security clearance, which requires U.S. citizenship. If you hold more than one citizenship (i.e., of the U.S. and another country), your ability to obtain a security clearance may be impacted.

Applicants offered employment with Sandia are subject to a federal background investigation to meet the requirements for access to classified information or matter if the duties of the position require a DOE security clearance. Substance abuse or illegal drug use, falsification of information, criminal activity, serious misconduct or other indicators of untrustworthiness can cause a clearance to be denied or terminated by DOE, resulting in the inability to perform the duties assigned and subsequent termination of employment.

EEO

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status and any other protected class under state or federal law.

NNSA Requirements for MedPEDs

If you have a Medical Portable Electronic Device (MedPED), such as a pacemaker, defibrillator, drug-releasing pump, hearing aids, or diagnostic equipment and other equipment for measuring, monitoring, and recording body functions such as heartbeat and brain waves, if employed by Sandia National Laboratories you may be required to comply with NNSA security requirements for MedPEDs.

If you have a MedPED and you are selected for an on-site interview at Sandia National Laboratories, there may be additional steps necessary to ensure compliance with NNSA security requirements prior to the interview date.

title: Student Success Coach – Springfield
description:
Hiring Department

School of Medicine Expansion

Job Description

Position Summary

The Success Coach serves as a dedicated, non-evaluative case manager and primary point of contact for medical students from matriculation through graduation. Working daily with students, the Success Coach provides proactive, longitudinal coaching focused on career development, well-being, and personal growth. This role ensures consistency, equity, and early intervention across all phases of the medical education program. The position supports compliance with LCME standards related to academic support, career advising, student oversight, and student wellbeing, while fostering a student experience grounded in trust, safety, and accountability.

Role Characteristics

This position is intentionally non-evaluative to promote trust, transparency, and psychological safety. The Success Coach functions as a generalist with deep institutional knowledge, serving as a single, reliable source of guidance while coordinating career specialty-specific mentoring and faculty involvement. The role operates within established policy and procedure, emphasizing consistency, standardization, equity, and accountability across both campuses and all student cohorts.

Core Responsibilities:

Planning and Progress Monitoring 25%

Provides success coaching to assigned medical students from M1–M4, ensuring continuity of support across all four years. Establishes early relationship prior to matriculation and proactively monitors academic progression, milestones, assists with elective selection, and responds to other areas of concern with timely intervention to promote student progression.

Case Management and Resource Navigation 25%

Serves as the primary point of contact for student success–related needs, coordinating support, resources, and follow-up. Maintains documentation and records per campus policy and the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act. Assesses overall student wellbeing and makes referrals to a variety of resources to ensure comprehensive support.

Career Advising and Professional Development 20%

Delivers structured, continuous career advising across the pre-clerkship and clerkship years, including specialty exploration, elective planning, preparation for residency applications, and coaching through the entire match process. Supports informed career decision-making and readiness for postgraduate training through developmentally appropriate guidance.

Standardization, Equity, and Oversight 15%

Implements standardized coaching frameworks, checklists, and timelines to ensure consistency and equity across both campuses and all cohorts. Documents student interactions, interventions, and outcomes to support early alert processes, institutional assessment, and continuous quality improvement.

Collaboration and Transition Support 15%

Collaborates with faculty advisors, mentors, and student affairs leadership while maintaining primary responsibility for advising continuity, documentation, and follow-up. Supports students through key academic, personal, and professional transitions, recognizing distinct developmental needs at each stage of training.

Shift

Monday – Friday
8:00 a.m. – 5:00 p.m.

Minimum Qualifications

A Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education and experience and at least 2 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary

Preferred Qualifications

Education: Masters degree in Student Affairs, Counseling, Education, Social Work or related field.
Years of Experience: 3 years in higher education or similar related work experience is preferred. Experience in student success coaching, counseling, career counseling or academic advising is preferred.

Anticipated Hiring Range

Salary Range: $45,968 - $64,272 annually

Internal applicants can determine their university title by accessing the Talent Profile tile in myHR.

Other Information

The University of Missouri School of Medicine is entering a period of strategic growth and innovation, highlighted by the UM Board of Curators’ approval to expand the Springfield clinical campus into a full four-year medical program. This expansion will increase total enrollment across Columbia and Springfield to more than 670 medical students and strengthen the university’s commitment to addressing Missouri’s physician shortage, particularly in rural regions. Beginning in 2027, first-year students will be welcomed to the Springfield campus, with fully identical curricula delivered across both sites through shared faculty, expanded simulation resources, and bi-directional livestreamed instruction. This milestone underscores the university’s broader mission to enhance statewide access to high-quality medical education and clinical care.

Complementing this statewide investment, the School of Medicine’s MOmentum curriculum redesign is transforming how future physicians are trained. MOmentum builds on MU’s long-standing learner-centered approach by integrating cutting-edge technology, innovative teaching strategies, and comprehensive support systems to create a dynamic and effective learning environment. The redesigned curriculum emphasizes evidence-based education, active learning, individualized support, early clinical exposure, and the development of lifelong, self-directed learners prepared to navigate an increasingly complex health care landscape. Through MOmentum, the School of Medicine is charting a bold path forward, ensuring students graduate with the advanced skills, adaptability, and patient-centered mindset needed to excel in modern medicine.

title: Clinical Adviser
description:
Will you actively create a healthier future for tomorrow?

At Medibank we’re encouraged to think big. We have a clear purpose to impact better health outcomes for our customers, patients and our community.

We celebrate diversity of thought because we want to make better decisions for our customers. As we work towards our goal of better health for better lives, we value the knowledge and contribution of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islanders. We are working hard to create an inclusive workplace and develop Indigenous careers.

We have an opportunity for an experienced Registered Nurse to join our Clinical Advisory Services team as a Clinical Adviser, working part time at 0.6 FTE.

This is an opportunity to take the clinical knowledge and judgement you’ve developed throughout your nursing career and use it in a different way. Rather than providing direct patient care, you’ll review clinical information, assess complex cases and use evidence to make considered clinical decisions and recommendations.

If you enjoy problem-solving, interpreting complex clinical information and using your nursing experience to make a meaningful impact, this could be a great next step

What you’ll be doing

As a Clinical Adviser, you’ll work across a varied clinical caseload and use your judgement to support evidence-based decision-making.

You’ll:

  • Assess Pre-Existing Condition cases and make evidence-based clinical determinations
  • Review complex Clinical Ex-Gratia funding requests
  • Interpret medical histories, clinical information and supporting documentation
  • Respond to clinical queries and provide trusted clinical advice across the business
  • Review health-related content to help ensure information is clinically appropriate and evidence based
  • Work collaboratively with stakeholders and contribute to continuous improvement across clinical processes

You’ll move between detailed, complex assessments and higher-volume casework, so your ability to prioritise, make considered decisions and maintain quality will be important.

Importantly, this is a non-patient-facing role, giving you the opportunity to continue using your clinical expertise in a different environment.

You might already have the skills for this role if you…

  • Are a Registered Nurse with current AHPRA registration and a Bachelor of Nursing
  • Bring at least five years of nursing experience, including recent acute-care exposure
  • Are confident reviewing complex clinical information and using your judgement to reach evidence-based decisions
  • Have strong critical-thinking and problem-solving skills and enjoy working through complex clinical scenarios
  • Can balance detailed assessments with higher-volume work while maintaining accuracy and quality
  • Communicate clearly in writing, collaborate well with others and are comfortable working autonomously

Experience within Emergency, ICU or complex acute or surgical nursing would be particularly valuable, while Oncology experience would also be highly regarded.

Knowledge of private health insurance or clinical funding principles would be beneficial, but you don’t need to have worked in health insurance before.

The details

This is a 0.6 FTE position working three days per week.

The preferred working pattern is Wednesday, Thursday and Friday, with Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday also able to be considered.

The role is predominantly home-based, with opportunities to connect with the team in the office. Interstate applicants can also be considered, with quarterly travel to Melbourne expected.

A career with us

At Medibank, we believe work is something we do, not somewhere we go. Our modes of working, Collaboration, Connection and Concentration, help inform how your day is structured and where you choose to work will vary, depending on your role and requirements.

The wellbeing of our employees is our priority. We encourage you to talk to us about any additional support you may require during the recruitment process, as well as how this role can be flexible for you. We encourage applications from candidates with a disability, and if you require any adjustments or alternate formats of key information at any stage of the recruitment process, we welcome hearing from you.

If you’re ready to use your nursing expertise in a new way and help us work towards better health for better lives, we’d love to hear from you.

title: Children's Board Book Translation & QA/QC (Independent Contractor)
description:
Just Right Reader is a literacy publisher dedicated to helping children become confident, successful readers through engaging, research-based resources grounded in the Science of Reading. Our growing product line includes decodable and knowledge-building books, classroom resources, teacher guides, lesson plans, literacy games, family resources, and marketing materials designed for students from Birth through Grade 12.

About This Engagement

  • Position Type: Independent Contractor (1099)
  • Project Scope: 36 Early Childhood Board Books (Ages 0–36 Months) per Language
  • Contract Duration: Short-term / Project-based
  • Location: Remote

Project Overview

Just Right Reader is seeking experienced, detail-oriented freelance translators to translate and review a collection of 36 early childhood board books designed for infants and toddlers (ages 0–36 months).

We are recruiting individual contractors for the following five language assignments:

  • Mandarin Chinese (Traditional Chinese): Standard Written Chinese, localized for Mandarin-speaking audiences.
  • Cantonese Chinese (Traditional Chinese): Standard Written Chinese, localized for Cantonese-speaking audiences, particularly in Hong Kong.
  • Tagalog
  • Vietnamese
  • Korean

Each contractor will be responsible for translating and reviewing all 36 titles in their assigned language.

All source materials will be provided in English. Translations must preserve the original meaning while ensuring the language is developmentally appropriate, culturally relevant, natural, and engaging when read aloud to young children and their caregivers.

Scope of Work & Deliverables

  1. Initial Translation (English to Target Language)
  • Translate all 36 English board book manuscripts into the assigned target language.
  • Adapt rhymes, repetitive phrases, and foundational early childhood vocabulary to preserve meaning, readability, and natural language flow.
  • Maintain consistency in terminology, tone, and age-appropriate language throughout the collection.
  • Ensure translated text corresponds accurately to the appropriate page or spread and aligns with the visual context of each book.
  1. Translation Quality Assurance (QA/QC)
  • Conduct a thorough self-review of all translated manuscripts for grammar, spelling, punctuation, consistency, cultural appropriateness, and developmental suitability.
  • Verify that all source text has been translated accurately, with no omissions or unintended additions.
  • Confirm that translated content and page references align with the original English source materials.
  • Submit corrected, publication-ready translations for implementation into the final book layouts.
  1. Post-Composition Proofreading (PP1 & PP2)

Following translation and QA/QC, Just Right Reader's production team will implement the translated text into the book layouts using Adobe InDesign. Contractors will then complete two post-composition proofreading passes:

  • PP1 – First Proof: Review composed PDFs to verify translation accuracy, text placement, character rendering, punctuation, line breaks, and text completeness. Identify and annotate any necessary corrections.
  • PP2 – Final Proof: Review revised PDFs to confirm that all PP1 corrections have been implemented accurately and identify any remaining language or composition errors before final approval.

All proofreading corrections must be clearly documented using PDF annotations or an agreed-upon tracking method.

  1. Submission & Handoff Requirements

English source materials will be provided in PDF format. Completed translations must be submitted using one of the following methods, as agreed upon with Product Operations:

  • Adobe Acrobat: Provide translated text through clearly labeled comments or sticky notes associated with the corresponding page or spread.
  • Google Docs: Organize translations by book title and page number, with English source text and corresponding translated text clearly identified.

All submissions must be complete, organized, and ready for internal review and production implementation.

This engagement does not include internal people management, HR responsibilities, or administrative duties.

Contractor Requirements & Qualifications

  • Native-level proficiency in the assigned target language and strong English-language comprehension.
  • For Chinese-language assignments, proficiency in Traditional Chinese and familiarity with the appropriate regional language conventions.
  • Proven experience in translation, localization, or copyediting, preferably within children's literature, early childhood education (ECE), or educational publishing.
  • Strong understanding of age-appropriate vocabulary, early language development, and read-aloud conventions for children ages 0–3.
  • Excellent attention to detail and ability to independently review and proofread translated content.
  • Proficiency with Adobe Acrobat annotation tools and Google Docs.
  • Reliable communication and ability to meet agreed-upon project milestones and deadlines.

Engagement Details

  • Engagement: Fixed-scope contract covering 36 board books in one assigned language.
  • Production Workflow: One initial translation round, followed by translator QA/QC and two post-composition proofreading passes (PP1 and PP2).
  • Timeline: Project milestones, turnaround expectations, and final delivery dates will be established before work begins.
  • Compensation: Flat project fee or per-book rate, to be agreed upon in the final contract. Compensation must include the initial translation, QA/QC, and both post-composition proofreading passes.
  • Project Completion: The engagement concludes upon final delivery and acceptance of all 36 translated and proofread titles by Just Right Reader.

How to Express Interest

Please submit:

  1. Your resume highlighting relevant experience.
  2. A cover letter with a summary on why you are interested in and a fit for this role.

The Manager of Infrastructure Solutions provides the necessary leadership, analysis and design tasks related to support the development of technology solutions to ensure that solutions meet business needs and align with architectural governance and standards. L’Unità Operativa RAD3 presidia l’area neuroradiologica dell’ospedale. title: Senior Employment Counsel
description:
INTRODUCTION

At Burberry, our people and culture underpin how we deliver for our customers and our brand. We are building a high‑performance culture that encourages creativity and collaboration, and enables colleagues to do their best work.

Guided by our reimagined purpose, To Embrace the Elements with Open Arms, we bring together diverse perspectives, skills and expertise to create exceptional luxury products and experiences. Our purpose also informs the standards of behaviour we expect, how we lead and how we make decisions across the business.

JOB PURPOSE

The Burberry Legal team operates at the heart of this vibrant, creative and forward-thinking FTSE-listed organisation, partnering with stakeholders across the business to support strategic priorities, manage risk and enable growth.

As a key member of the Employment Legal team, this role provides strategic and practical employment law support across the UK and EMEIA. The successful candidate will serve as a trusted adviser to HR and senior business leaders, helping to shape decision-making on complex workforce issues, organisational change and employee relations matters.

This is a 12-month fixed-term contract (covering parental leave), based in our office 4 days a week, with 1 day of remote flexibility.

RESPONSIBILITIES

We are looking for an experienced, technically excellent and pragmatic employment lawyer who can lead complex employee relations matters and provide commercially focused legal advice across a broad range of employment law issues in the UK and EMEIA.

The role will include:

  • Providing clear, commercially focused advice to HR across the employment lifecycle, including hiring, performance, grievances, disciplinary matters, investigations, disputes and exits.
  • Supporting the delivery of organisational change and cross-border projects, including reorganisations.
  • Advising on senior appointments, promotions and negotiated exits.
  • Managing employment litigation in the UK and EMEIA, including case and settlement strategy and oversight of external counsel.
  • Supporting Burberry's readiness for the Employment Rights Act reforms and other strategic people-related projects across EMEIA, translating legal developments into practical guidance and partnering with stakeholders to implement change effectively.
  • Contributing to the continuous improvement of legal processes, templates, training and knowledge-sharing.
  • Managing external legal advisers and legal spend effectively.

PERSONAL PROFILE

The successful candidate will:

  • Have strong UK employment law expertise, with experience supporting employment matters across EMEIA jurisdictions and working effectively with local counsel.
  • Be able to operate autonomously with minimal supervision and provide advice directly to senior stakeholders.
  • Have experience supporting organisational change programmes and delivering practical solutions to complex workforce challenges.
  • Demonstrate excellent stakeholder management and influencing skills.
  • Be commercially minded, with sound judgement and the ability to translate legal risk into clear, practical recommendations.
  • Be organised and resilient, with the ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Have experience managing external advisers and external legal spend.

Behaviours:

  • Technical excellence and commercial judgement

Demonstrates strong technical legal skills, excellent judgement and the ability to provide practical, commercially focused advice.

  • Bring Clarity

Provides clear, pragmatic and commercially focused advice, enabling stakeholders to make informed decisions and manage risk effectively.

  • Create Connection

Builds trusted relationships across HR, Legal and the wider business, collaborating effectively across functions and geographies to achieve positive outcomes.

title: Commissioning Electrical Lead (Electrical Red Seal)
description:
Hiring now. Qualified candidates are being interviewed this week.

GrizzlyTrek is hiring a Commissioning Electrical Lead for our valued client's commissioning and startup (CSU) team in Edmonton, Alberta. You will be the electrical subject matter expert on an integrated field leadership team, taking electrical equipment and systems through inspection, testing and energization to first time start-up, and mentoring less experienced members of the team along the way.

A Journeyman Electrical Interprovincial Red Seal is required, with 7 to 15 years of experience, including 5 years leading commissioning and start-up.

At a Glance

  • Pay: $80.00 per hour
  • Location: Edmonton, Alberta. Field based, working on site.
  • Ticket: Journeyman Electrical, Interprovincial Red Seal (required)
  • Experience: 7 to 15 years of work experience, including 5 years leading commissioning and start-up
  • Safety Tickets: Six required (OSSA and CSTS), listed below
  • Scope: Electrical commissioning, testing and energization

Required Safety Certifications (OSSA and CSTS)

  • Construction Safety Training System (CSTS-20)
  • Basic Scaffold Safety (CSTS-20)
  • Fall Protection
  • Confined Space Entry and Monitoring
  • WHMIS
  • H2S Alive

The Seat

You will work inside an integrated field leadership team, planning, managing and preparing equipment and systems for first time start-up. Your work covers electrical equipment such as switchgear, transformers, ATS and UPS, from walkdowns and megger testing through functional performance testing, VFD programming and energization. As the electrical subject matter expert, you mentor less experienced members of the team and direct E&I resources to mitigate deficiencies.

What You'll Do

  • Perform static and dynamic commissioning, including continuity checks, insulation resistance (megger) testing, functional performance tests and VFD programming
  • Inspect and walk down electrical equipment (switchgear, transformers, ATS and UPS) visually and mechanically to verify installation against drawings
  • Identify, troubleshoot and resolve electrical issues and deficiencies during the startup phase, and direct E&I resources to mitigate them
  • Take part in system walkdowns and manage punch list items until every deficiency is resolved, within the Completions process, the Punchlist and Mitigation Plan and the CMS Plan
  • Coordinate and execute commissioning, testing and energization per the Commissioning Execution Plan and team directives, and support EHT testing and validation
  • Keep test result records, complete check sheets (A, B and C checks), write detailed technical reports, and make sure CSU documentation is collected, filed and archived to standard practice
  • Take part in Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT) and Site Acceptance Testing (SAT), documenting deficiencies
  • Read and apply detailed vendor settings, P&IDs, isometrics, single line diagrams, electrical and instrument drawings, manuals and loop diagrams, and track red-line changes
  • Identify, schedule and manage vendor and contractor needs on site, monitor progress, and coordinate with project managers for handover of electrical systems
  • Within the Electrical scope, assist the CSU Manager with review and edits of Commissioning Plans, Procedures and Strategy, and develop daily progress reports for the CSU Electrical Coordinator
  • Act as the electrical subject matter expert and mentor to the project team, sharing CSU experience and teaching less experienced members

What You Bring

  • Journeyman Electrical Interprovincial Red Seal
  • 7 to 15 years of work experience, including 5 years leading commissioning and start-up of electrical, instrumentation and automated electrical and mechanical equipment and process control systems
  • Strong electrical background in power generation, protection relay testing, interlock verification, VFDs, transformer testing, high voltage substation energization and EHT, with a high level of understanding of automated equipment commissioning
  • Experience meeting the high corporate safety and environmental directives and requirements of major industrial suppliers
  • All six safety certifications listed above

Nice to Have

  • Commissioning and start-up experience on electrical and instrumentation equipment in industrial gas, power generation and chemical facilities, including cryogenic technologies, air separation, syngas and CO2 capture

Why Electrical Leads Take This Job

This seat puts you in the lead electrical role on an integrated field leadership team, taking switchgear, transformers, ATS and UPS equipment from walkdowns and megger testing to energization and first time start-up. It pays $80.00 per hour.

Benefits

  • Life insurance plus AD&D with critical illness and cancer coverage
  • Extended health: drugs, hospital, hearing, orthotics, vision, and paramedical including mental health
  • Dental coverage, including orthodontic coverage for children
  • Travel insurance up to $5,000,000 per incident
  • Ongoing training and career development support

About GrizzlyTrek

GrizzlyTrek Group is a Technical Workforce and Indigenous Employment Partner. We recruit skilled trades and technical professionals across Canada's industrial sector and place them with reputable employers offering long term work, fair pay, and room to advance. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates and proudly support Indigenous employment.

Apply

Are you a Red Seal electrician who has led commissioning and start-up? Tell us your years leading start-up, the equipment you have tested and energized, and your safety tickets. Qualified candidates will be contacted quickly.

Apply today at www.grizzlytrekgroup.com
