title: Regional Product Line Manager, Industrial Hose
description:
Are you inspired by challenging the status quo? Do you thrive in collaborative environments that drive results? If so, Gates could be for you.

Gates is a leading manufacturer of application-specific fluid power and power transmission solutions. We push the boundaries of material science to engineer solutions that continually exceed customer expectations.

Let's simplify it, think belts and hoses. Found in motorcycles, conveyor belts, cars, tractors, blenders, vacuum cleaners, bicycles, & 3D printers just to name a few. Because why not do it all?

What To Expect

As an innovation leader, we look for ambitious, forward-thinking, open-minded, and well-rounded individuals to join our team. Located in our Denver, CO headquarters, you will report to the Senior Director, Product Line Management for Fluid Power North America.

The Regional Product Line Manager, North America Industrial Hose is responsible for the profitable growth, strategic direction, portfolio health, and competitive position of the industrial hose product line across North America. This role serves as the regional business owner for the portfolio, translating market, customer, channel, application, and competitive insights into clear product line strategies and executable commercial plans. The RPLM works closely with Sales, Global Product Line Management, Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Finance, Marketing, Quality, Pricing, and Product Application Engineering to align priorities and deliver sustainable growth.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Key responsibilities:

  • Own the regional strategy, commercial performance, profitability, portfolio health, and competitive position of the North American industrial hose product line.
  • Develop deep knowledge of industrial hose applications, end markets, customers, channels, specifications, regulations, industry trends, and competitors. Segment the portfolio and convert these insights and voice of customer into actionable growth priorities, supporting proposed actions with multiple business metrics, market attractiveness, and Gates’ ability to compete and win.
  • Lead annual and long-range product line planning, maintain documented priorities and action plans, provide accurate forecasts and timely performance reviews, and initiate corrective actions to achieve financial and service objectives.
  • Identify and prioritize growth opportunities across industrial markets and applications, including targeted verticals, strategic accounts, distributor channels, cross-selling opportunities, and competitive conversions.
  • Develop fact-based recommendations for pricing, mix, portfolio investment, lifecycle management, product rationalization, inventory health, and complexity reduction.
  • Shape product roadmaps and business cases for new products, line extensions, sourced products, and regional requirements; clearly define customer needs, market potential, financial returns, and launch requirements.
  • Lead commercialization of new and existing products, including positioning, pricing, channel readiness, sales training, demand generation, adoption plans, and launch-performance tracking.
  • Partner with Sales leadership and field teams to prioritize markets, accounts, applications, and opportunities; provide product-line expertise in strategic customer discussions, opportunity qualification, and competitive conversions.
  • Collaborate with Product Application Engineering and other technical resources to strengthen application knowledge, support field trials and product validation, resolve product and application gaps, and develop technical reference materials.
  • Influence Global Product Line Management, Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Finance, Marketing, Quality, Pricing, and Sales to align regional priorities; establish clear owners, milestones, and follow-up mechanisms; proactively escalate risks and barriers; and drive approved service, cost, productivity, and VAVE initiatives to completion.
  • Develop compelling value propositions, competitive tools, product and application training, and market-facing content that enable the commercial organization and distributor partners to win.
  • Monitor product line performance, market developments, customer needs, competitive activity, supply risks, and emerging opportunities; maintain accurate and current analyses; communicate material issues early; and provide senior leadership with concise, fact-based insights, clearly defined tradeoffs, recommendations, and next steps.
  • Represent Gates with customers, distributor partners, suppliers, industry organizations, trade shows, and relevant market forums.

Requirements and Preferred Skills

ABOUT YOU

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business, Marketing, or a related field from an accredited institution required.
  • Minimum of 5 years of relevant product line management, product management, engineering, technical sales, marketing, or commercial experience; industrial hose, fluid power, or industrial distribution experience strongly preferred.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently develop product line strategies and comprehensive market segmentation. Must be able to assess market size, profitability, growth potential, market attractiveness, and Gates’ right to win; distinguish historical reporting from strategic analysis; and translate insights into clear priorities and executable plans supported by multiple business metrics.
  • Strong business and financial acumen, including experience with pricing, profitability, forecasting, business cases, portfolio management, and performance analysis. Demonstrated ability to independently develop complete business cases supporting investment or resource allocation.
  • Technical curiosity and the ability to build credibility in industrial hose products, applications, standards, specifications, and customer operating environments.
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to influence across functions, levels, and locations without direct authority and present complex information as clear recommendations.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint, with demonstrated ability to independently manipulate, summarize, and analyze complex datasets and translate into concise business insights and recommendations. Must be able to select and create appropriate analytical visualizations, present analysis and insights professionally, and develop fact-based portfolio recommendations. Experience using analytical and market-intelligence tools preferred.
  • Experience supporting 80/20 initiatives to focus resources on high-value opportunities and simplify the portfolio is preferred; expertise is not required.
  • Independent, proactive, highly organized, and disciplined, with a high level of integrity, ownership, and follow-through.
  • Ability to travel up to 40% of the time, occasionally work outside regular office hours, and work in the office with teammates.
  • Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without company sponsorship.

Pay & Benefits

  • Full-Time
  • Salary Range: $135,000 - $150,000
  • Bonus Eligible
  • Relocation is not provided
  • Medical, Dental, Vision insurance and other voluntary benefit options: benefits begin on the first day of the month immediately following your date of hire
  • Eligible for 3 weeks of paid vacation + 11 holidays (9 scheduled & 2 floating) + 8 sick days. All vacation days are accrued
  • 401(k): 3% company contribution and additional 3% company match
  • Tuition Reimbursement

Why Gates?

Founded in 1911 in Denver, Colorado, Gates is publicly traded on the NYSE. While we might operate in a vast amount of time zones we operate as 'One Gates' and have a common goal of pushing the boundaries of materials science. We invest in our people, bringing real-world experience that enables us to solve our customers' diverse challenges of today and anticipate those of tomorrow.

Work Environment

Gates is an Equal Opportunity and is committed to ensuring equal employment opportunities for all job applicants and employees. Employment decisions are based upon job-related reasons regardless of race, sex, color, religion, age, disability, pregnancy, citizenship, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, genetic information, marital status, or any other consideration defined by law.
While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to sit; use hands and fingers to work with objects, tools, or controls; and use office equipment including computers, telephones, and/or copiers/scanners. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 10 pounds.
For individuals assigned and/or hired to work in Colorado, Gates is required by law to include a reasonable estimate of the compensation for this role. This compensation range is specific to the State of Colorado and takes into account various factors that are considered in making compensation decisions, including but not limited to the candidate's relevant experience, qualifications, skills, competencies, and proficiency for the role.

title: Clinician, TrueLife Recovery (Bilingual)
description:
Clinician, TrueLife Recovery

Bilingual Required

About Lifeline Community Services

Lifeline Community Services is a premier nonprofit organization in San Diego County, dedicated to empowering individuals and families to achieve self-reliance and long-term stability. Our diverse service portfolio spans housing, behavioral health, youth development, and anti-human trafficking initiatives, operating across multiple locations.

Position Overview

Lifeline Services is hiring a mental health clinician to support our growing team. The TrueLife Recovery Clinician, under the supervision of the TrueLife Recovery Program Manager, serves as the Licensed Practitioner of the Healing Arts (LPHA) and is responsible for the coordination of and delivery of clinical co-occurring and substance abuse services. The TLR Clinician will deliver individual, group, and family therapy services through a number of Evidence Based Practices (EBP)-via a strengths-based, trauma- informed perspective. The TLR Clinician will provide substance abuse and psychoeducational groups encompassing a variety of topics related to life domains, relapse prevention strategies and coping skills

Key Responsibilities

  • Provides screening for new clients with co-occurring mental health disorders.
  • Determines initial medical necessity for admission with a face-to-face interaction if SUD Counselor completed intake.
  • Provides clinical/recovery services and conducts mental health assessments.
  • Determines ongoing medical necessity by completing Diagnosis Determination Note, and Justification for Continuing Services within County timelines.
  • Works closely with SUD Counselors to complete Level of Care (LOC) and individualized Treatment Plans within County timelines.
  • Provides psycho-educational groups to assist clients with co-occurring disorders to manage mental health symptoms and the interaction of those symptoms with urges to use substances.
  • Provides holistic client assessment through the use of approved instruments: Addiction Severity Index (ASI) Lite, the American Society of Addiction Medicine (ASAM), and the Youth Level of Service/Case Management Inventory (YLS/CMI) for justice involved individuals.
  • Utilizes the ASAM, the risk and needs assessment tool, to complete a comprehensive bio-psychosocial assessment.
  • Conducts groups, individual counseling, and family therapy sessions with content and approach following evidence- based practice models for substance use disorder counseling and criminogenic risk factors, including Motivational Interviewing, Cognitive Behavioral Interventions, and Relapse Prevention.
  • Provides SUD educational groups that address at least the following areas: SUD physiological effects, SUD psychological effects, SUD social effects, SUD pharmacological aspects, characteristics of families with SUD problems, wellness, diet and exercise.
  • Provides job preparation, education and discussion groups to all clients needing these services as indicated on their Individual Treatment Plans.
  • Provides family violence education, discussion groups and individual counseling sessions to clients needing these services as indicated on their Individual Treatment Plans, and assists with referrals if needed.
  • Provides Tobacco Cessation education and nicotine testing to clients needing these services as indicated on their Individual Treatment Plans, and assists with referrals if needed.
  • Completes all other duties as assigned.

Education & Experience:

  • Master's degree in counseling, social work or related field
  • Licensed LMFT, LCSW, LPCC or registered AMFT/ASW/APCC.
  • Must possess knowledge of and experience in substance abuse assessment and counseling including possessing at least 1 year experience working with co-occurring and/or substance abuse services.
  • Bilingual English/Spanish required.
  • Demonstrated knowledge, training, and experience in Cognitive Behavioral Interventions, DBT, Seeking Safety, or TF-CBT Approach highly desired.
  • Must possess excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to demonstrate the interpersonal sensitivity and cultural competency needed for working with diverse populations.
  • Be able to respond quickly and effectively to many types of situations, including crisis situations and potentially hostile situations.
  • Must have good driving record and willing to use own, properly insured, reliable vehicle for the job (mileage reimbursed).
  • Employment subject to clearances, including background fingerprinting checks, driving record, tuberculosis testing, and drug testing.

Work Environment and Physical Demands:

  • Primarily based at North County Middle Schools and North County High Schools
  • Requires the ability to sit or stand for extended periods
  • Involves routine movement throughout school facilites
  • Occasional lifting of objects weighing up to 40 pounds
  • Travel within San Diego County as needed, requiring the use of a personal vehicle
  • Dynamic school environment with frequent interaction with students, faculty, and staff

Why Join Lifeline?

Comprehensive Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and full employer paid benefits package, including:
    • Medical, dental, and vision
    • Employee Assistance Plan (EAP).
  • Paid parental and bereavement leave of up to 80 hours for qualifying events
  • Mileage reimbursement

Professional Growth Opportunities:

  • Access to training programs and leadership development resources
  • Opportunities to contribute to innovative programs and initiatives that make a tangible difference

title: Associate ATS Engineer
description:
Requisition ID # 175514

Job Category: Engineering / Science

Job Level: Individual Contributor

Business Unit: Energy Delivery

Work Type: Onsite

Department Overview

Applied Technology Services (ATS) is a multidisciplinary team of engineers, scientists, and technicians providing specialized technical services across the Company. ATS solves complex technical problems and reduces risk through engineering, testing, failure analysis, technology evaluation, and application of industry best practices.

Position Summary

The Associate Electrical Engineer supports testing, evaluation, and application of technologies for electric transmission, distribution, generation, and substation assets. Under the guidance of senior engineers and technical staff, the position performs electrical testing, engineering analysis, equipment evaluations, and failure investigations in field and laboratory environments.

Assignments may include grounding and touch potential assessments, arc-flash studies, cable diagnostics, transmission line measurements, transformer and substation equipment testing, equipment condition assessments, failure investigations, asset monitoring, and evaluation of emerging technologies and test methods.

The position provides opportunities to develop technical expertise through progressively more complex assignments while supporting Company objectives for safety, asset reliability, wildfire risk reduction, operational excellence, and regulatory compliance.

The selected candidate must live within PG&E’s service territory.

PG&E is providing the salary range that the company in good faith believes it might pay for this position at the time of the job posting. This compensation range is specific to the locality of the job. The actual salary paid to an individual will be based on multiple factors, including, but not limited to, specific skills, education, licenses or certifications, experience, market value, geographic location, and internal equity. Although we estimate the successful candidate hired into this role will be placed towards the middle or entry point of the range, the decision will be made on a case-by-case basis related to these factors.​

A reasonable salary range is:

Minimum Base Salary (Bay Area) $90,000.00

Mid Base Salary (Bay Area) $113,000.00

Maximum Base Salary (Bay Area) $136,000.00

Job Responsibilities

  • Applies basic electrical engineering principles to perform testing, calculations, analysis, and equipment evaluations under the guidance of senior engineers.
  • Performs field and laboratory testing of transmission, distribution, generation, and substation equipment using established procedures, standards, and test methods.
  • Supports engineering investigations involving equipment failures, safety incidents, asset performance concerns, and wildfire-related events.
  • Evaluates electrical equipment, including transformers, circuit breakers, batteries, cables, insulators, grounding systems, instrument transformers, capacitors, regulators, and related apparatus.
  • Collects, analyzes, and documents test data, equipment condition information, inspection findings, and operational data.
  • Supports grounding and touch potential assessments, arc-flash studies, cable diagnostics, transmission line measurements, and equipment condition assessments.
  • Assists with failure and root-cause investigations through testing, equipment history review, technical analysis, and documentation of findings.
  • Supports development and evaluation of test methods, procedures, acceptance criteria, and condition assessment approaches.
  • Supports evaluation and deployment of monitoring, sensing, diagnostic, and data acquisition technologies for electric utility assets.
  • Assists with technical and economic evaluations of emerging technologies to improve safety, reliability, asset performance, and operational efficiency.
  • Prepares calculations, test plans, technical documentation, reports, presentations, and recommendations for review by senior engineering staff.
  • Coordinates with engineers, technicians, contractors, manufacturers, laboratories, and internal clients to complete assigned work.
  • Develops technical proficiency through field assignments, laboratory work, training, and mentorship.
  • Supports project planning, scheduling, cost tracking, documentation, and coordination.
  • Adheres to Company safety, quality, and applicable regulatory requirements.
  • Participates in technical initiatives and knowledge-sharing activities.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering with emphasis in a discipline related to assignments. (i.e., mechanical, civil or electrical engineering, etc.)

Desired Qualifications

  • Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering or a related discipline.
  • Engineer-in-Training (EIT) certification.
  • Up to two years of related engineering, internship, laboratory, utility, or field experience.
  • Basic knowledge of electrical engineering testing, analysis, and investigative methods.
  • Familiarity with transmission, distribution, generation, or substation equipment.
  • Basic analytical, investigative, and problem-solving skills.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to prepare clear technical calculations, documentation, and reports.
  • Ability to work collaboratively with engineers, technicians, and internal clients.
  • Basic understanding of quality assurance and quality control principles.
  • Ability and willingness to perform field assignments and travel as required.

title: Sr Manager, Automation, Borger Refinery
description:
Phillips 66 & YOU - Together we can fuel the future

As the Sr Manager, Automation, you will lead the site's automation organization that owns our distributed control, advanced process control, and automation systems that keep the refinery safe, reliable, and optimized. You’ll combine hands on technical leadership with people development, guiding controls engineers and specialists while shaping the long term automation and APC strategy for the site. This is an opportunity to influence high impact decisions, champion innovation, and collaborate across operations, maintenance, and engineering to improve process safety, operability, and profitability.

At Phillips 66, Lead Forward is our leadership approach. It defines how leaders show up, make decisions, and support their teams while delivering results in a complex, fast‑changing environment. Leaders at this level focus on setting clear direction, building trust, and helping their teams succeed. You’re expected to act with integrity, make timely and thoughtful decisions, and take ownership of outcomes while supporting collaboration across teams. This role is about leading people well, even when priorities change or the path forward isn’t always clear.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead and develop a high‑performing controls team, setting clear goals, managing performance, building capabilities, and modeling safety, integrity, and accountability in line with our leadership expectations.
  • Own the refinery’s control system strategy and lifecycle, including distributed control systems (DCS), PLC interfaces, advanced process control (APC), and other stand‑alone controls, to meet safety, regulatory, production, and optimization objectives.
  • Design, standardize, and continuously improve APC and process control solutions, including development and testing of APC applications, inferred properties, control strategies, and alarm management to drive process safety, operability, and profitability.
  • Oversee engineering standards, compliance, and cybersecurity for control systems, including networks, domains, system software upgrades, hardware migrations, documentation, and alignment with corporate standards, process safety management, and security requirements.
  • Lead a portfolio of automation and control projects from concept through commissioning and startup, managing scope, schedule, and budget while partnering with operations, maintenance, process and project engineering, vendors, contractors, and corporate experts.
  • Champion refinery safety and operational excellence by actively supporting the safety program, providing guidance during startups, shutdowns, and upsets, and participating in incident investigations and Management of Change reviews.
  • Break down barriers and build cohesive, cross‑functional relationships across the refinery and enterprise, managing stakeholder expectations and facilitating effective collaboration to solve complex issues and implement change.
  • Use data and strategic analysis to drive quality decisions, including reporting and optimization of control system performance metrics and contributing to longer‑term automation and APC roadmaps and budget planning.

What You’ll Bring – Required

  • Legally authorized to work in the job posting country
  • Bachelor’s degree in an engineering discipline
  • 10 or more years of engineering experience in the Energy, Chemical, or related industry
  • 6 or more years of experience managing teams and planning and organizing engineering resources
  • Possess a valid driver's license
  • Must be willing and able, with or without reasonable accommodation, to comply with the following:
    • Travel up to 5%
    • Operate company vehicle on site premises and/or public roads up to 10%
    • Work extended hours, which may include evenings, weekends, and holidays, and perform occasional on-call (24/7) duties
    • Transport articles up to 50 pounds
    • Climb ladders and stairs up to 200 feet
    • Work safely near large, hot, high-speed machines, around chemicals and hydrocarbons under high pressure and heat, and in harsh weather conditions
    • Wear fire retardant clothing and personal protective equipment
    • Maintain face daily for proper respirator/face mask seal (some examples include being free of facial hair and/or clean shaven)

What Makes You Stand Out – Preferred

  • Bachelor’s degree or higher in Chemical Engineering; advanced degree preferred
  • 12 or more years of engineering experience, including extensive leadership of controls or automation teams in manufacturing, refining, or chemical environments
  • Knowledge and understanding of distributed control systems, advanced process controls, networks, and operating systems
  • Direct experience in the refining and/or chemical industry, including automation and control applications in these settings
  • Knoweldge of Emerson DeltaV and DeltaV Safety Instrumented Systems
  • Experience with Honeywell ProfitSuite and other APC or optimization platforms
  • Experience with Alteryx, Tableau, or similar tools for data analytics, reporting, and visualization
  • Proven ability to lead complex automation projects, coach diverse technical teams, and make thoughtful, timely decisions in ambiguous or rapidly changing conditions
  • Ability to translate site/company direction into plans, prioritizing resources, developing team capability, and advising senior technical leadership

Compensation Range

This position has a base salary range of $158,400– $ 226,600.

At Phillips 66, we are committed to pay transparency and competitive, equitable compensation. Each role is assigned a salary grade with a defined pay range, benchmarked against industry peers. Where a candidate offer falls within the posted range depends on the candidate's experience, skills, and alignment with the role’s requirements. Offers are made to ensure internal equity and market competitiveness. Our compensation programs are designed to reward performance and support career growth.

The Borger Refinery is located in Borger, Texas, in the Texas Panhandle, approximately 50 miles north of Amarillo, Texas. Refinery facilities include crude distilling, naphtha reforming, fluid catalytic cracking, alkylation, hydrodesulfurization and delayed coking units. The refinery processes primarily medium sour crude oil produced locally, and heavy sour crude oil produced in Canada, all of which are delivered by pipeline. Borger produces a high percentage of transportation fuels, as well as petroleum coke, NGLs and solvents. Refined products are distributed to customers via pipelines from the refinery to West Texas, New Mexico, Colorado and the Midcontinent region.

title: Distribution Associate - Rockford, IL - Up to $31.91/hour!
description:
Begin a rewarding career as a full-time Distribution Associate!

Job Functions / Responsibilities:
You will be part of a dynamic, essential team dedicated to distributing the truck parts that keep the world moving! Within our state-of-the-art distribution center, Distribution Associates are cross trained thoroughly to become efficient in all areas of distribution including:
• Receiving – You will verify delivery bills and verify product received. You will learn to quickly recognize and address warehouse compliance issues such as overages, shortages, damaged product, packaging issues and incorrect parts.
• Stocking – We will teach you how to assess quantity, size, weight and volume to stock material in appropriate warehouse locations.
• Order Picking – You will process essential customer orders by utilizing our cutting-edge warehouse order picking software.
• Packing – We will train you on our best practices to pack items ensuring our customer’s products safe and undamaged.
• Shipping – You will be trained to prepare shipping documentation, weight, piece count and freight classification of all warehouse product.
• Become a valuable, fully trained Distribution Associate and assist in the training of new employees beginning their PACCAR journey!

LOCATION: Rockford, IL

SHIFT: 2nd Shift; (M-F) 3:00pm - 11:30pm

Qualifications:
• High School Diploma or GED
• Commitment to safety
• Willingness to be cross-trained and rotate through all warehouse functions as needed.
• Regularly lift and/or move up to 50 pounds with or without accommodation.
• Able to withstand heights up to 30 feet.


Compensation Information
As a U.S. PACCAR employee, you have a full range of benefit options including:
• 401k with up to a 5% company match
• Fully funded pension plan that provides monthly benefits after retirement
• Comprehensive paid time off – minimum of 10 paid vacation days (additional days are provided with additional seniority/years of service), 12 paid holidays, and sick time

• Medical, dental, and vision plans for you and your family
• Flexible spending accounts (FSA) and health savings account (HSA)
• Paid short-and long-term disability programs
• Life and accidental death and dismemberment insurance
• EAP services including wellness plans, estate planning, financial counseling and more
• This position may also be eligible for a holiday gift.

Salary
At PACCAR Parts, we value talent and promote growth and development. Starting pay rate of $26.74/hour with possible increases every six months up to $31.91/hour. This role is eligible for a full range of benefit options listed above.

Additional Job Board Information
• Relocation assistance may be available for this position.
• PACCAR Parts is an eVerify Employer.
• PACCAR is an Equal Opportunity Employer/Protected Veteran/Disability.
• PACCAR has success with diverse teams of employees working together to achieve excellent results. Having a diverse and inclusive work environment ensures PACCAR has the talent needed to conduct business today and in the future by leveraging different backgrounds, skills, and viewpoints. We believe diversity in the workplace increases innovation, results in better decisions, and increases employee engagement.

Company Information

PACCAR is a Fortune 500 company established in 1905. PACCAR Inc is recognized as a global leader in the commercial vehicle, financial, and customer service fields with internationally recognized brands such as Kenworth, Peterbilt, and DAF trucks. PACCAR is a global technology leader in the design, manufacture and customer support of high-quality light-, medium- and heavy-duty trucks under the Kenworth, Peterbilt and DAF nameplates. title: Senior Manager Signalling & Telecommunications Maintenance
description:
You’ll connect Queensland. We’ll connect you to an amazing career.

Queensland Rail are seeking an experienced Senior Manager Signalling & Telecommunications Maintenance to join our SEQ Assets team based in Brisbane CBD. This is a permanent, full-time leadership opportunity responsible for one of Queensland Rail's most critical infrastructure portfolios.

Reporting to the Asset Maintenance Delivery Director, you will provide strategic and operational leadership for the maintenance of Queensland Rail's South East Queensland signalling and telecommunications network while overseeing the statewide delivery of signalling and telecommunications construction activities. Leading a large, multidisciplinary workforce, you will drive asset reliability, operational performance, safety outcomes, and network readiness to support the growing demands of Queensland's rail network.

Progress That Counts

Queensland Rail is helping shape the future of transport in Queensland. As we prepare to welcome millions of visitors for the 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games, we are delivering one of the largest rail infrastructure investment programs in the state's history.

Major initiatives underway include:

  • Cross River Rail, transforming travel across South East Queensland and supporting a projected increase to more than 80 million passenger journeys annually over the next decade.
  • Introduction of the European Train Control System (ETCS) to modernise network operations and improve capacity.
  • Delivery of The Wave and the Beerburrum to Nambour Rail Upgrade.
  • Construction of three new stations on the Gold Coast line.
  • The $5.75 billion Logan and Gold Coast Faster Rail Project.
  • Introduction of 65 new rollingstock units from the Queensland Train Manufacturing Program.

Learn more about The Wave project Click Here

About the Role

As a member of the SEQ Asset Maintenance Senior Leadership Team, you will play a pivotal role in shaping maintenance and asset management strategies across Queensland Rail's signalling and telecommunications portfolio.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Providing strategic leadership within a complex passenger rail and infrastructure environment, balancing safety, customer outcomes, commercial performance, and operational excellence.
  • Leading the maintenance, reliability, and lifecycle management of signalling and telecommunications assets to optimise network performance and availability.
  • Driving operational readiness and the successful integration of new technologies, assets, major projects, and transformative ways of working.
  • Building strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders, including senior leaders, project delivery teams, industry partners, regulators, and other rail operators.
  • Leading a high-performing workforce that fosters collaboration, accountability, continuous improvement, and customer focus.
  • Delivering business objectives, performance targets, safety commitments, and financial outcomes across maintenance and construction activities.
  • Developing and implementing contemporary asset management, maintenance, reliability, and risk management strategies across a diverse and expanding asset base.
  • Delivering SEQ Assets transformation and change program.

About You

You are a highly regarded leader with deep technical expertise and a proven track record managing critical infrastructure within a complex operational environment.

To be successful, you will bring:

  • Extensive experience in signalling and telecommunications maintenance, construction, and asset management, ideally within the rail industry or another safety-critical heavy asset environment.
  • Demonstrated success in leading large-scale maintenance and infrastructure delivery functions at a senior management level.
  • Strong strategic leadership capabilities, with expertise in asset lifecycle management, reliability improvement, risk management, and operational performance.
  • Experience leading organisational change, operational transformation, and the integration of new technologies and infrastructure.
  • Outstanding stakeholder engagement, influencing, negotiation, and relationship management skills, with the ability to build trusted partnerships across diverse groups.
  • A commitment to safety leadership, people development, and fostering high-performing and engaged teams.
  • A track record of delivering measurable business improvements in service reliability, asset performance, customer outcomes, and financial performance

To learn more about this role - full Position Description here

Your journey matters. Make it with us.

There has never been a more exciting time to join Queensland Rail. We offer real opportunities for meaningful contribution, while shaping your career for the future.

Please apply to Senior Manager Signalling & Telecommunications Maintenance (12350) via our website by clicking onto the "Apply" button by 11:59pm (GMT+10:00 Brisbane) Monday 23rd November 2026.

Supporting a Diverse Workforce

Queensland Rail acknowledges the Traditional Owners and Elders of the lands and waterways our network traverses.

Our teams are People who Count. title: Sr Manager, Regional Product Line Management, Hydraulics
description:
Are you inspired by challenging the status quo? Do you thrive in collaborative environments that drive results? If so, Gates could be for you.

Gates is a leading manufacturer of application-specific fluid power and power transmission solutions. We push the boundaries of material science to engineer solutions that continually exceed customer expectations.

Let's simplify it, think belts and hoses. Found in motorcycles, conveyor belts, cars, tractors, blenders, vacuum cleaners, bicycles, & 3D printers just to name a few. Because why not do it all?

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

WHAT TO EXPECT

As an innovation leader, we look for ambitious, forward-thinking, open-minded, and well-rounded individuals to join our team. Located in our Denver, CO headquarters, you will report to the Senior Director, Product Line Management for Fluid Power North America.

The Senior Manager, Regional Product Line Management, Hydraulics North America is a player-coach responsible for the profitable growth, strategic direction, and competitive position of the North American hydraulics portfolio while leading and developing the Regional Product Line Management (RPLM) Hydraulics team. This role combines direct product line ownership with responsibility for building the capabilities, operating disciplines, and cross-functional alignment required to move the PLM organization from reactive support toward strategic product line leadership.

Key responsibilities:

  • Own the regional strategy, commercial performance, profitability, portfolio health, and competitive position of the North American hydraulics product line.
  • Build deep knowledge of hydraulic applications, customers, channels, market trends, industry indicators, and competitors; translate insights and VOC into regional strategies, global product line inputs, and actionable demand and supply plans.
  • Lead annual and long-range planning, forecasts, and performance reviews, with clear actions to achieve financial objectives.
  • Develop fact-based pricing, mix, portfolio, productivity, lifecycle, and rationalization recommendations that support profitable, sustainable growth and reduce excess and obsolete inventory.
  • Shape product roadmaps and business cases for new products, enhancements, and regional requirements; lead commercialization, including positioning, pricing, channel readiness, sales training, adoption plans, and launch metrics.
  • Lead, coach, and develop the RPLM Hydraulics team as a player-coach, establishing clear expectations, accountability, development plans, field-learning requirements, and a culture of ownership, constructive challenge, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
  • Build team capability in market intelligence, application knowledge, competitive analysis, VOC, business case development, portfolio management, value propositions, and commercialization; partner with Product Application Engineering and other technical teams to scale training and technical content.
  • Establish common PLM processes, operating cadences, decision frameworks, templates, and performance measures; identify recurring process gaps and lead structural, cross-functional solutions.
  • Partner with Sales leadership to prioritize markets, accounts, applications, and growth opportunities; serve as a subject matter expert in strategic customer discussions, competitive conversions, and opportunity evaluations.
  • Influence across Global Product Line Management, Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Finance, Marketing, Quality, Pricing, and Sales to align priorities, execute approved VAVE and productivity initiatives, and accelerate results.
  • Develop compelling product and application value propositions, competitive tools, training, and market-facing content; represent Gates in relevant industry organizations, trade shows, standards bodies, and market forums.
  • Provide senior leadership with concise performance reporting, market insights, risks, tradeoffs, and recommendations.

Requirements and Preferred Skills

ABOUT YOU

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Engineering Technology, Business, Marketing, or a related field from an accredited institution required; advanced degree preferred.
  • Minimum of 8 years of relevant product line management, engineering, or commercial experience; hydraulics or fluid power experience strongly preferred.
  • Demonstrated people leadership, coaching, and talent-development experience, with the ability to strengthen team capability and accountability.
  • Strong business and financial acumen, strategic thinking, and analytical skills, with experience translating market, customer, application, competitive, and financial insights into clear priorities, investment tradeoffs, and executable plans.
  • Exceptional interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to influence across levels, functions, and locations and present complex information as clear, executive-level recommendations.
  • Independent, proactive, highly organized, and disciplined, with a high level of integrity and ownership; proficient in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint, with experience using analytical and market-intelligence tools preferred.
  • Ability to travel up to 40% of the time, occasionally work outside regular office hours, and work in the office with teammates.
  • Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without company sponsorship.

Pay & Benefits

  • Full-Time
  • Salary Range: $165,000 - $195,000
  • Bonus Eligible
  • Relocation is not provided
  • Medical, Dental, Vision insurance and other voluntary benefit options: benefits begin on the first day of the month immediately following your date of hire
  • Eligible for 3 weeks of paid vacation + 11 holidays (9 scheduled & 2 floating) + 8 sick days. All vacation days are accrued
  • 401(k): 3% company contribution and additional 3% company match
  • Tuition Reimbursement

Why Gates?

Founded in 1911 in Denver, Colorado, Gates is publicly traded on the NYSE. While we might operate in a vast amount of time zones we operate as 'One Gates' and have a common goal of pushing the boundaries of materials science. We invest in our people, bringing real-world experience that enables us to solve our customers' diverse challenges of today and anticipate those of tomorrow.

Work Environment

Gates is an Equal Opportunity and is committed to ensuring equal employment opportunities for all job applicants and employees. Employment decisions are based upon job-related reasons regardless of race, sex, color, religion, age, disability, pregnancy, citizenship, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, genetic information, marital status, or any other consideration defined by law.
While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to sit; use hands and fingers to work with objects, tools, or controls; and use office equipment including computers, telephones, and/or copiers/scanners. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 10 pounds.
For individuals assigned and/or hired to work in Colorado, Gates is required by law to include a reasonable estimate of the compensation for this role. This compensation range is specific to the State of Colorado and takes into account various factors that are considered in making compensation decisions, including but not limited to the candidate's relevant experience, qualifications, skills, competencies, and proficiency for the role.

title: Reliability Engineer - Fixed
description:
You may not realize it, but you’ve likely used a product today made possible by the plastics and chemicals manufactured by Chevron Phillips Chemical. From medical supplies and electronics to food packaging and cosmetics, we create the building blocks for more than 70,000 consumer and industrial products.

Even as a global company with 5,000 employees, we maintain a “small company feel.” Our commitment to foster a culture of belonging ensures that regardless of your background or experience, your voice is valued and heard, empowering you to make a meaningful impact and grow both personally and professionally. Ask any Chevron Phillips Chemical employee what they like best about their job, and universally, the answer is “the people I work with!” We value work-life balance, and love to see our employees thrive both professionally and personally. There has never been a better time to work for Chevron Phillips Chemical. If you’re ready to grow with us and become part of our vision of being the premier Chemical Company, apply today!

Introduction

The Reliability Engineer for Fixed Equipment based in Cedar Bayou will play a key role in advancing equipment reliability and asset performance. In this highly collaborative position, they will lead efforts to identify and eliminate equipment reliability issues and improve overall asset availability while supporting CPChem's commitment to safe, reliable, and cost-effective operations. The role will work closely with Operations, Maintenance, Turnaround, and Engineering teams, while leveraging reliability data and engineering best practices to drive sustainable improvements in equipment performance and long-term asset health. Other responsibilities include leading equipment failure investigations, developing Asset Strategies, providing technical guidance, and contributing to site reliability initiatives that support business objectives and operational integrity.

The ideal candidate is a proactive and technically strong reliability professional who thrives on solving equipment challenges and driving continuous improvement. The role leads the Bad Actor program in their area of responsibility and recommends reliability improvements. This role offers an excellent opportunity to influence plant performance, support critical reliability and mechanical integrity programs, and contribute to a culture focused on safety, accountability, and operational excellence.

Responsibilities

  • Implements corporate Mechanical Integrity program at the site.
  • Collects and analyzes reliability metrics to identify bad actors.
  • Participate in the development, design and installation of predictive maintenance programs and technology applications to identify and eliminate defects.
  • Coordinates with site stakeholders to establish and maintain the proper stocking levels of parts and equipment required to provide maximum equipment uptime at the lowest possible costs.
  • Executes the identification and elimination of bad actors and the optimization of equipment availability.
  • Monitors field inoperable equipment logs for remediation needs.
  • Assesses and adjusts specific equipment tolerances and specifications.
  • Participates in equipment failure investigations and cause analysis and implement action items to prevent recurrence using Cause Analysis tools.
  • Plans and coordinates projects from inception to completion ensuring efficient implementation, timely completion, and compliance to budget. Contributes on larger capital projects (CAPEX).
  • Contributes to site efforts to implement Process Safety Management elements at the site.
  • Special assignments

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering
  • Minimum of 5 years of engineering experience in a refinery or chemical plant

Preferred Qualifications

  • Mechanical Engineering experience
  • 3+ years of Fixed equipment experience applying industry codes, best practices, and company standards.

Chevron Phillips Chemical offers competitive salaries, a comprehensive benefits package and at most locations, alternate work schedules. To learn more about Chevron Phillips Chemical and to be considered for a position, please visit us online today at www.cpchem.com.

Paper resumes will not be accepted. All job seekers must go to the web site to be considered for positions. If you are interested in applying for this position and need an accommodation to apply, please contact our Human Resources Service Center at 1-800-446-1422, option 4.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, pregnancy, veteran status or marital status.

title: Mechanical Technician
description:
Who we are

Fresh Consulting is a design-led, software development and hardware engineering company, offering end-to-end digital services to help companies innovate. We bring together amazing UX designers, sophisticated developers, digital strategists, and top-notch engineers to help companies create fresh experiences that connect humans, systems, and machines. We’ve been growing fast and need someone to help us continue to manage the delivery of high-quality work in a fast-paced environment. See more at

About the role

Fresh Consulting is hiring a Senior Prototype Technician (L4) to own prototype builds from build plan to working hardware. You'll lead build teams, run complex fabrication-heavy builds where specs are still changing, and grow our junior technicians.

This role suits a hands-on fabricator who has built high-precision prototypes or validation hardware, in aerospace, defense or product development, and has led teams under pressure. You'll work alongside mechanical, electrical and firmware engineers, help shape designs through review, and consult directly with clients. You'll build as much as you lead.

The position starts as a contract position to verify with both sides that this is a good long-term fit.

What you'll do

Builds and technical work

  • Own build plans, incorporating feedback from the project team.
  • Execute complex prototype builds where specifications may be incomplete or evolving.
  • Fabricate precision parts and assemblies using CNC machining, CNC waterjet or plasma, MIG and TIG welding, composites and structural fabrication.
  • Interpret CAD models, engineering drawings and GD&T callouts, and hold build tolerances.
  • Design and build prototypes, fixtures and back panel layouts.
  • Take concepts from the first sketch through iterated, functional prototypes.
  • Apply advanced troubleshooting across mechanical, electrical and electromechanical systems.
  • Give useful feedback in design reviews, especially on manufacturability.

Leadership and team

  • Lead build teams, delegate work and ensure project quality.
  • Lead lab and shop projects and day-to-day team operations.
  • Grow junior talent and guide technical excellence.
  • Train others on shop equipment.
  • Enforce safety standards in the lab and shop.
  • Improve manufacturing processes and mentor others in them.
  • Give peer input during the Fresh review cycle.

Collaboration and consulting

  • Support cross-discipline collaboration and project estimation.
  • Manage up to improve communication between the team and its leads.
  • Deepen your client and team consulting capabilities.
  • Seek out mentoring and build rapport across the hardware team.

What you bring

You're a seasoned fabricator with strong mechanical skills and real experience leading people. That means you can:

  • Complete builds independently from engineering data packages, build books and drawings, and draft build plans.
  • Run CNC equipment (mill, waterjet or plasma) and weld with MIG and TIG processes.
  • Work with metals and composites, choosing materials and processes for strength and manufacturability.
  • Read blueprints and GD&T, and navigate SolidWorks, CATIA, Fusion 360 or similar CAD to view, markup and pull build information.
  • Hold tight dimensional tolerances on assemblies, using measurement and inspection tools.
  • Run 3D printers and other prototyping equipment.
  • Perform verification and validation (V&V) procedures.
  • Lead BoM tracking, procurement, inventory and build kitting with engineers.
  • Manage vendors and self-manage your tasks and quality.
  • Support quoting and estimates.
  • Lead and train teams and make sound decisions under time pressure.
  • Document build notes, issues and as-built deviations, and write clear summaries and reports.
  • Use MS Office or similar apps.
  • Bring solutions along with problems and know when to reach out for support.
  • Have basic electronics skills (soldering, cable and harness building, reading schematics, using multimeters and oscilloscopes), or be ready to build them quickly with team support.

Nice to have

  • Experience in aerospace, defense or other high-precision prototype environments.
  • Welding certification and OSHA safety training.
  • Military or similar leadership experience.
  • A record of inventing or developing products from concept through prototype.
  • Experience mentoring or training other technicians.
  • Exposure to robotics, mechatronics or non-destructive testing (NDT).

Physical requirements and work environment

  • Comfortably lift 50 lbs.
  • Work on your feet for 10-hour days, 5 days a week, on a regular basis.
  • Take on "dirty" shop work such as scraping, painting and grinding.
  • Complete shop safety and equipment training, use PPE, and follow lockout and safe-operation procedures.

Most of the work happens in a prototype lab and machine shop with power tools, fabrication equipment and test benches.

Growth mindset

We look for technicians who seek out new tasks and skills and adapt quickly when the work changes. At this level you'll also seek mentors for yourself while mentoring others.

For a Washington-State-based role, the salary hiring range for this position is $35/hr to $55/hr. Compensation offered will be determined by factors such as location, level, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.

Equal employment opportunity: All qualified persons will be considered for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, marital status, familial status, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability for which a reasonable accommodation can be made, or any other status protected by law. Assistance will be gladly provided upon request for any applicant with sensory or non-sensory disabilities.

*Fresh Consulting is a participating E-Verify company.

title: (Senior) System Engineer Cloud Storage (m/f/d)
description:
Introduction text

Schwarz Digits creates the technological foundation for digital sovereignty in Europe. As the IT and digital division of the Schwarz Group, we develop and manage the IT infrastructures for the retail divisions Lidl and Kaufland, as well as Schwarz Production and PreZero. At the same time, we operate as an independent provider in the external market to support companies across Europe in their digital transformation. We bundle our core services in the areas of Cloud, Cyber Security, Data & AI, Communication, and Workspace.

Join us and contribute to digital sovereignty in Europe. With us, you will work at the intersection of agility and security: You will benefit from fast decision-making processes, enjoy genuine creative freedom in your projects, and be able to build upon the stable foundation of the Schwarz Group.

In this role, you will receive support from many internal service teams to continuously refine our services and build a long-term, stable, and reliable solution that our customers will be happy to use.

Your Tasks

  • Architecture: Together with your team, you are responsible for designing and maintaining a robust, efficient, and forward-looking storage architecture.
  • Stability & Reliability: You are responsible for maintaining and optimizing the stability and availability of our highly resilient storage infrastructure (Block, Object, Backup, and File Storage). You ensure this through proactive monitoring, independently resolving incidents, and implementing measures to prevent future occurrences.
  • Incident & Post-Mortem Analysis: You will take charge of processing major incidents involving storage as part of our incident and problem management process. Your goal is to derive and successfully implement mitigating measures for the future.
  • Automation: You automate provisioning and operating processes in the storage environment with a continuous drive to improve our products and get a little better every day.
  • Performance & Capacity Planning: You will analyze and optimize the performance of existing systems to support the future scaling of our landscape, including proactive, forward-looking capacity planning.

Your Profile

  • Must-Haves
    • Storage Expertise: Proven experience in the architecture, operations, and troubleshooting of storage systems. You must have deep hands-on experience with NetApp ONTAP.
    • Protocols & Architectures: Strong overall understanding of storage architectures and deep experience with associated protocols, specifically NFSv3, NFSv4.x, NVMe-oF.
    • Operating Systems: Robus, hands-on expertise with Linux operating systems, including a proven capability to effectively troubleshoot system issues.
    • Automation & IaC: Strong experience in automating configurations and operational tasks. You are highly proficient with Infrastructure as Code (IaC) frameworks and tools such as Ansible, Terraform, and OpenTofu, as well as scripting/programming (e.g., Golang, Python, Bash).
    • API Management: Experience in working with REST APIs.
    • Performance & Capacity Management: Proven experience in performance analysis, troubleshooting bottlenecks, and proactive capacity planning for complex storage landscapes.
    • Continuous Learning: You are highly motivated to dive into new technologies and have a keen interest in storage ecosystem integrations, such as virtualization, backup, and observability (e.g., Prometheus, Grafana, Elasticsearch).
    • Mindset & Language: You are a motivated team player who enjoys the challenges of operating complex storage systems (lifecycle, high availability, performance analysis). Excellent communication skills in English are required for our international, agile teams (German is an optional bonus).
  • Nice-to-Have Skills
    • Containerization: Experience using Kubernetes (K8s) and working within containerized system landscapes in a storage context.

title: Clinical Data Manager
description:
Job Title: Clinical Data Manager

Job Location: Bangalore

Department: Clinical Data Management

About Syngene: Syngene () is an innovation-led contract research, development and manufacturing organization offering integrated scientific services from early discovery to commercial supply.

At Syngene, safety is at the heart of everything we do personally and professionally. Syngene has placed safety at par with business performance with shared responsibility and accountability, including following safety guidelines, procedures and SOPs, in letter and spirit

Mandatory expectation for all roles as per Syngene safety guidelines

  • Overall adherence to safe practices and procedures of oneself and the teams aligned
  • Contributing to development of procedures, practices and systems that ensures safe operations and compliance to company’s integrity & quality standards
  • Driving a corporate culture that promotes environment, health, and safety (EHS) mindset and operational discipline at the workplace at all times.
  • Ensuring safety of self, teams and lab/plant by adhering to safety protocols and following environment, health, and safety (EHS) requirements at all times in the workplace.
  • Ensure all assigned mandatory trainings related to data integrity, health, and safety measures are completed on time by all members of the team including self
  • Compliance to Syngene’ s quality standards at all times
  • Hold self and their teams accountable for the achievement of safety goals
  • Govern and Review safety metrics from time to time

Core Purpose of the Role:

To independently perform and coordinate clinical data management activities for assigned clinical studies, ensuring accurate, complete, consistent, and GCP/regulatory-compliant clinical trial data. The role is responsible for data review and validation, query management, discrepancy resolution, reconciliation activities, and support for database cleaning and lock activities. Additionally, the role assists in stakeholder communication, ensures adherence to established processes and timelines, and provides guidance to junior team members to support high-quality study deliverables.

Role Accountabilities

  • Accountable for executing assigned clinical data management activities in accordance with study requirements, timelines, SOPs, and regulatory guidelines.
  • Accountable for performing data review, validation, and cleaning activities to ensure data accuracy, completeness, and consistency.
  • Accountable for raising, tracking, and facilitating timely resolution of data queries with investigative sites and internal stakeholders.
  • Accountable for monitoring CRF/eCRF completion, query status, and data discrepancies to support study milestones.
  • Accountable for supporting CRF/eCRF review, database testing, and User Acceptance Testing (UAT) activities as assigned.
  • Accountable for conducting routine data quality checks and escalating data issues, risks, or trends to the Data Manager in a timely manner.
  • Accountable for supporting data reconciliation activities, including SAE, laboratory, and other external vendor data reviews as applicable.
  • Accountable for maintaining accurate, complete, and inspection-ready study documentation and tracking records.
  • Accountable for supporting database lock and study closeout activities through completion of assigned data cleaning tasks.
  • Accountable for ensuring compliance with applicable SOPs, ICH-GCP guidelines, protocol requirements, and sponsor expectations.
  • Accountable for preparing study metrics, status reports, and data management deliverables as requested.
  • Accountable for collaborating effectively with cross-functional teams to support smooth study execution and issue resolution.
  • Accountable for sharing knowledge, supporting onboarding activities, and providing guidance to junior team members when required.
  • Accountable for identifying opportunities for process improvements and contributing to quality and operational excellence initiatives.
  • Accountable for completing assigned tasks within agreed timelines while maintaining high standards of quality and compliance.
  • Accountable for performing additional responsibilities assigned by the reporting manager in support of departmental and organizational objectives.

Leadership & Team Support

  • Provide guidance, coaching, and training to junior data management team members.
  • Support timely delivery of study milestones while ensuring data quality and compliance.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement of data management processes and best practices.
  • Support audit and inspection readiness activities and ensure adherence to SOPs and quality requirements.
  • Assist management with resource planning and workload coordination, as needed.

Syngene Values

All employees will consistently demonstrate alignment with our core values

  • Excellence
  • Integrity
  • Professionalism

Specific requirements for this role

Experience

  • 5-6 years of experience in Clinical Data Management within CRO, pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or clinical research organizations.
  • Experience managing Phase I-IV clinical trials, observational studies, and/or real-world evidence studies.
  • Hands-on experience in end-to-end clinical data management activities including study startup, database review, data cleaning, query management, and database lock.
  • Experience in CRF/eCRF design, edit check specification development, and database validation review.
  • Experience using EDC systems and clinical databases.
  • Experience interacting with sponsors and cross-functional study teams.
  • Experience supporting audits, inspections, and quality compliance activities.
  • Experience mentoring junior team members and coordinating study-level activities.

Skills and Capabilities

  • Good understanding of Clinical Data Management processes and clinical trial data lifecycle.
  • Strong data review, validation, discrepancy management, and query resolution skills.
  • Proficiency in EDC systems and clinical databases.
  • Working knowledge of ICH-GCP, regulatory requirements, and data quality standards.
  • Familiarity with database lock and reconciliation activities.
  • Good analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks and meet timelines.
  • Effective communication and cross-functional collaboration skills.
  • Good documentation and reporting skills.
  • Demonstrates accountability, attention to detail, and a quality-focused mindset.

Education

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Life Sciences, Pharmacy, Biotechnology, Clinical Research, Health Sciences, or a related discipline.
  • Certification or training in ICH-GCP, Clinical Data Management, EDC systems, or regulatory compliance is desirable.

Equal Opportunity Employer:

It is the policy of Syngene to provide equal employment opportunity (EEO) to all persons regardless of age, color, national origin, citizenship status, physical or mental disability, race, religion, creed, gender, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, genetic information, marital status, status with regard to public assistance, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable legislation or local law. In addition, Syngene will provide reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities.

title: Engineering Event & Special Projects Manager
description:
Founded in 1913 in Italy, the Prada Group was built on a tradition of excellence and with a vision of innovation. The Group, a world leader in the luxury sector, operates in more than 45 countries with the PRADA, Miu Miu, Versace, Church’s, Car Shoe and Luna Rossa brands, and has employees of over 100 nationalities.

JOB SUMMARY

The Engineering Event & Special Projects Manager supports the planning, setup, production, execution and breakdown of luxury retail events at both in-store and offsite locations. As well as coordination among departments for additional special project requirements. Reporting to Facilities Management, this position serves as the technical and operational liaison between Facilities, Events and other operational teams, ensuring required installations are executed safely, efficiently and in accordance with brand standards.

The role provides hands-on technical and engineering support for product launches, VIP events, activations, pop-ups, special installations and other brand initiatives. The Engineering Event & Special Projects Manager works closely with internal teams, venues, contractors and vendors to coordinate event infrastructure, electrical requirements, temporary installations, lighting, equipment, logistics and onsite technical support.

  • Partner with the Events team to review upcoming events, activations and product launches and identify technical, facilities and engineering requirements
  • Participate in site walks for boutiques and offsite venues to evaluate existing conditions and event requirements.
  • Review event layouts, production plans and vendor scopes to identify electrical, lighting, HVAC, structural, access and installation needs.
  • Develop technical requirements and execution plans for event setup and breakdown.
  • Coordinate required building or landlord approvals for temporary installations and event-related work.
  • Identify potential site constraints and proactively develop solutions prior to event installation.
  • Coordinate access, loading, deliveries, installation schedules and vendor requirements with boutiques, venues and building management.
  • Support budget development by obtaining proposals, reviewing vendor pricing and identifying cost-effective technical solutions.

Event Setup & Production

  • Provide hands-on support during event setup, production and breakdown.
  • Coordinate and oversee installation of temporary event infrastructure, displays, fixtures, lighting and equipment.
  • Support electrical requirements including temporary power, power distribution and coordination with licensed electrical contractors when required.
  • Coordinate event lighting and other technical equipment in partnership with production vendors.
  • Troubleshoot technical and facility-related issues during setup and live events.
  • Ensure temporary installations are secure, safe and consistent with approved plans.
  • Serve as an onsite Facilities representative during major event installations and productions.
  • Coordinate rapid response to unexpected facility or technical issues that could impact event execution.

Vendor & Contractor Coordination

  • Coordinate electricians, handymen, production vendors, equipment rental companies, movers and other specialty contractors supporting events.
  • Clearly communicate scope, schedule, access requirements and brand expectations to vendors.
  • Review vendor proposals with direct manager and confirm scope alignment prior to work.
  • Monitor vendor performance, quality and adherence to event schedules.
  • Verify completion of work and assist with resolution of deficiencies.
  • Support Facilities Management with purchase orders, invoices, estimates and related cost tracking.
  • Maintain strong relationships with reliable vendors capable of supporting high-profile and time-sensitive projects.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

Act as a key technical liaison between Facilities Management and the Events team, while collaborating closely with Retail Operations, Visual Merchandising, Marketing, Store Planning, IT, Loss Prevention, Logistics and external production partners.

Translate creative project concepts into practical technical requirements while helping preserve the design intent and elevated presentation expected within a luxury retail environment.

REQUIREMENTS

  • 5-7 years of experience in facilities, event production, engineering coordination, construction, retail operations or a related technical field preferred.

  • Working knowledge of electrical systems, lighting, HVAC and general building infrastructure.
  • Experience coordinating contractors, vendors and technical trades.
  • Ability to read basic floor plans, event layouts and technical drawings.
  • Strong understanding of event setup, production and breakdown processes.
  • Strong organizational and project coordination skills with the ability to manage multiple events simultaneously.

title: Senior AI Product Engineer
description:
Just Right Reader is a forward-thinking curriculum provider committed to advancing literacy for students from Birth through 12th Grade. Our comprehensive resources are designed to support all learners, including upper-grade students requiring additional intervention to develop foundational skills. Grounded in the Science of Reading, our high-quality materials and tools equip educators with the support they need to accelerate achievement and foster lifelong readers.

Position Overview:

Just Right Reader works with school districts and state education agencies to get kids books at the right reading level. Our platform is TypeScript, Next.js and Postgres, and it connects to the CRM, ERP and internal systems that run the business.

We're adding AI to the product. We have a list of projects we want to build and we haven't started on any of them, so we're hiring an engineer to do that work.

Key Responsibilities:

The projects are already scoped, so you wouldn't be coming in to figure out what we should build. You'd be building it, and making the technical decisions along the way: how we call models, what happens when the output comes back wrong, what we do about cost and latency, and how we test any of it.

That last part matters more than it might sound. Right now we'd have no way to tell whether a change to a prompt or a model made things worse, and we'd want that in place early rather than after something goes out badly.

Because we work with K-12 students, privacy and data handling come up in every design conversation instead of at the end of one. Recommendations also have to be defensible, and one that's wrong but sounds confident causes us more trouble than not making one.

You'd also do regular product work. We're a small team, so there's Next.js, schema design and integration work alongside the AI projects.

Qualifications:

You've built an AI product from scratch and shipped it to real users. We're specifically after someone who made the architecture decisions rather than building features on top of a system another team maintained, since that's the situation here. If every AI project you've worked on already had a gateway, an eval setup and a cost dashboard in place when you arrived, this will be a harder jump than it looks.

We'd want to hear about at least one thing you built that people depended on, and we'll ask a lot of questions about it.

Engineering

  • Senior-level experience as a full-stack or product engineer on systems that were genuinely in production, with real users and real consequences when something broke.
  • Strong TypeScript. Nearly everything you'd write here is TypeScript, across both the application and the services around it.
  • Next.js in production rather than familiarity with it. You should be comfortable with the App Router, server components, API routes, and the places where Next.js makes things harder than they need to be.
  • Strong backend skills: API design, server-side business logic, and the kind of debugging where the bug turns out to be three systems away from where the error showed up.
  • Strong PostgreSQL. Query design and optimization, schema and data modeling, and enough experience to know when the ORM is helping and when you should write the SQL yourself. A fair amount of the work here is SQL-heavy.
  • Third-party API integration where the interesting part was the failure cases. Retries, idempotency, rate limits, partial failures, and vendors behaving differently in production than their docs suggested.
  • AWS at the application level - S3, SQS, Secrets Manager, ECS/Fargate, Lambda, RDS, DynamoDB. We care more about whether you've debugged something running on them than whether you can list the services.

AI specifically

  • You know the ways LLMs fail in production: malformed structured output, schema drift, latency spikes, cost surprises, refusals, and answers that are wrong but sound certain. More to the point, you know what to build so that users don't have to deal with any of it.
  • You've had to evaluate quality somehow. Golden sets, scored runs, human review, regression checks before a deploy - whatever form it took, you've answered the question of whether a change made things better or worse with something other than a feeling.
  • Judgment about when a model is the wrong tool. A fair amount of what looks like an AI problem turns out to be a rules or SQL problem with a better interface, and we'd rather ship the boring version when that's the right answer.
  • Some sense of what running this costs and what to do about it.

Working here

  • We're small, so you'd be talking directly with the people in operations, customer success and fulfillment who use what we build. Being able to have those conversations well matters about as much as the code does.
  • Comfort treating internal tooling as a normal part of the job rather than a distraction from the interesting work.

Useful but not required:

  • Retrieval systems in production, eval tooling you've built or used seriously, Prisma, Terraform or general infrastructure literacy, Python, previous K-12 or FERPA work, and experience with systems like NetSuite, HubSpot, Shopify or Slack.

We're not doing model training, fine-tuning or research, so this isn't the right role if that's what you're after.

Why Join Us:

At Just Right Reader, we're transforming how children learn to read. You'll be part of a passionate, growing team committed to educational equity, literacy innovation, and joyful learning.

  • Mission-driven company focused on improving literacy and education outcomes.
  • Collaborative and innovative work environment with opportunities for growth and development.
  • Competitive salary and benefits package.
