title: Intern - R&D Graduate Summer - TITANS - Southwest Analysis Laboratories for Semiconductor Advancement (SALSA), Onsite
description:
What Your Job Will Be Like

We seek graduate student interns to join our SALSA (Southwest Analysis Laboratories for Semiconductor Advancement) TITANS Cybersecurity team for Summer 2027! Qualified candidates will be part of a larger family, namely Technical Internships To Advance National Security (TITANS), focused solely on cybersecurity, software, hardware and math analytics.

TITANS Cybersecurity (also known as the Center for Cyber Defenders or CCD) is seeking students who want to have a career in cybersecurity. We are focused on developing the next generation of experts in the field of computer security from the software stack down to microelectronic hardware components. You will use your foundational computer science/engineering, electrical engineering, materials science, math, analytics, and data science skills, but your work will be directed to cybersecurity topics. This posting is for who are currently pursuing graduate degrees in the field of Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Physics, or any closely related field of study and are interested in furthering their knowledge in the area of cyber security and information protection while working on their graduate degree.

Your job could consist of:

  • Manual and automated failure analysis and vulnerability assessment
  • Intrusion prevention/detection and response, penetration testing, and forensics
  • Information protection, and resiliency
  • Authentication and authorization
  • Cryptography
  • Mobile devices and smart technologies

And many more areas of research!

We are also looking for candidates with expertise in electrical engineering, physics, and materials science interested in:

  • Debugging hardware prototypes
    • Printed Circuit Board Layout
    • Design analysis
    • Prototype assembly
  • Identifying and fixing integrated circuit issues (failure analysis)
    • Focused Ion Beam (FIB) tools
    • Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM)
    • Laser Scanning Microscopy (LSM) tools
  • Design either at the integrated circuit or circuit board level, including tools such as
    • K Layout
    • Altium
    • Cadence Tool Chain
  • FPGA/microcontroller/embedded systems development
  • Electronic measurement equipment experience including oscilloscope, power supplies, waveform generators, etc.
  • RF or electromagnetics expertise

Your projects will be real-world cybersecurity hardware problems or embedded engineering challenges contributing to a cybersecurity challenge or mission space affecting national security. There's no busy work in the CCD! Your solution will exercise foundational math and analytic techniques and best practices in SW or HW engineering to help improve cybersecurity of our nation.

Due to the nature of the work, the selected applicant must be able to work onsite.

Salary Range

At Sandia, we value the important work done by our interns and its contribution to National Security. Because of this, our interns earn competitive pay rates. Our pay structure is based on earned credit hours, classification, and degree level. Your pay rate will be determined during the hire process and included in your offer package. You can view the Intern Pay Rate chart here.

Qualifications We Require

You bring the confidence and skills to be eligible for the job by meeting these minimum requirements:

  • Earned bachelor's degree
  • Currently attending and enrolled full time in the spring term immediately preceding the internship (or scheduled to graduate in the spring) in an accredited science, engineering, or math graduate program
  • Minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0/4.0
  • Ability to work up to 40 hours per week during the summer
  • Ability to secure and maintatin a U.S. security clearance which requires U.S. citizenship

Note: If you have not yet started your graduate program, please apply to an undergraduate intern position.

Qualifications We Desire

  • GPA of at least 3.2 on a 4.0 scale
  • Pursuing a graduate degree in an engineering or science related field, such as Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Physics, or other relevant SEM Disciplines

Posting Duration

This posting will be open for application submissions for a minimum of three (3) calendar days, including the 'posting date'. Sandia reserves the right to extend the posting date at any time.

About Our Team

The CCD gives computer science interns practical experience with computer systems, network operations, and information protection. The year-round program combines research with education and provides a venue for interns to perform experiments on attacking and defending computer systems with proper guidance and protective measures in place.

About Sandia

Sandia National Laboratories is the nation’s premier science and engineering lab for national security and technology innovation, with teams of specialists focused on cutting-edge work in a broad array of areas. Some of the main reasons we love our jobs:

  • Challenging work with amazing impact that contributes to security, peace, and freedom worldwide
  • Extraordinary co-workers
  • Some of the best tools, equipment, and research facilities in the world
  • Career advancement and enrichment opportunities
  • Flexible work arrangements for many positions include 9/80 (work 80 hours every two weeks, with every other Friday off) and 4/10 (work 4 ten-hour days each week) compressed workweeks, part-time work, and telecommuting (a mix of onsite work and working from home)
  • Generous vacation, strong medical and other benefits, competitive 401k, learning opportunities, relocation assistance and amenities aimed at creating a solid work/life balance*

World-changing technologies. Life-changing careers. Learn more about Sandia at: http://www.sandia.gov


*These benefits vary by job classification.

Security Clearance

Sandia is required by DOE to conduct a pre-employment drug test and background review that includes checks of personal references, credit, law enforcement records, and employment/education verifications. Applicants for employment need to be able to obtain and maintain a DOE L-level security clearance, which requires U.S. citizenship. If you hold more than one citizenship (i.e., of the U.S. and another country), your ability to obtain a security clearance may be impacted.

Applicants offered employment with Sandia are subject to a federal background investigation to meet the requirements for access to classified information or matter if the duties of the position require a DOE security clearance. Substance abuse or illegal drug use, falsification of information, criminal activity, serious misconduct or other indicators of untrustworthiness can cause a clearance to be denied or terminated by the DOE, resulting in the inability to perform the duties assigned and subsequent termination of employment.

EEO

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status and any other protected class under state or federal law.

NNSA Requirements for MedPEDs

If you have a Medical Portable Electronic Device (MedPED), such as a pacemaker, defibrillator, drug-releasing pump, hearing aids, or diagnostic equipment and other equipment for measuring, monitoring, and recording body functions such as heartbeat and brain waves, if employed by Sandia National Laboratories you may be required to comply with NNSA security requirements for MedPEDs.

If you have a MedPED and you are selected for an on-site interview at Sandia National Laboratories, there may be additional steps necessary to ensure compliance with NNSA security requirements prior to the interview date.

title: Stormwater & Environmental Inspector
description:
Job Description

Starting Hiring Salary - Stormwater and Environmental Inspector: $31.31 to $33.19 hourly

Stormwater and Environmental Inspector: $31.31 - $42.89
Senior Stormwater and Environmental Inspector: $34.33 - $47.03

The City of Brighton is looking for an individual to fill the role of Stormwater and Environmental Inspector for the Utilities Department. The Utilities Department strives to provide their staff with training and learning opportunities for organizational development and growth. We would like to fill the position as an inspector and hold the opportunity for the senior title to allow the individual who fills the role the opportunity to further grow and advance with the city.

DEFINITION:
The Stormwater and Environmental Inspector/Senior Stormwater and Environmental Inspector will ensure completion of inspections and documentation of the construction, illicit discharge, post-construction and pollution prevention/good housekeeping programs under the City's Phase II Municipal Separate Storm Sewer System (MS4) Permit. This position must work well independently and with teams, while providing excellent, respectful customer service and human-relations skills, which support the City of Brighton's mission and values.

SUPERVISION RECEIVED AND EXERCISED:
This position reports directly to the Stormwater and Environmental Manager. This position does not supervise other employees.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES:
Stormwater and Environmental Inspector
Conducts and documents inspections, per requirements of the MS4 Permit and the City of Brighton Erosion and Sediment Control (ESC) permit, at construction sites in Brighton City Limits.
Assists with providing education and compliance assistance to construction site operators and stormwater administrators.
Conducts and documents inspections, per requirements of the MS4 Permit at post-construction sites where permanent stormwater quality control measures have been implemented.
Assists with providing education and compliance assistance to stakeholders such as HOAs and property managers of their responsibilities to maintain private storm infrastructure.
Conducts and documents inspections, per requirements of the MS4 Permit at municipal-owned facilities.
Assists in and documents response, investigation and remediation efforts of illicit discharges.
Assists in and documents enforcement response, per Division Standards Operating Procedures, under the construction, illicit discharge, post-construction and pollution/prevention/good housekeeping programs of the MS4 permit.
Performs various maintenance tasks on City-owned and maintained stormwater infrastructure.
Participates in public education and outreach activities, which may include occasional work on the weekends.
Prepares necessary calculations, data entry, spreadsheets, summaries and reports.
Performs related duties as directed/assigned by the Stormwater and Environmental Manager, Assistant Director or Director

Senior Stormwater and Environmental Inspector
In addition to the job duties mentioned above:
Performs independent inspections and provides direct judgement for enforcement cases to the Stormwater Manager with minimal need for guidance.
Performs enforcement actions, such as the issuance of a Stop Work Order, independently when Analyst and Stormwater Manager are not available.
Assist in the completion of maintenance projects for City owned stormwater facilities that require third party resources
Assists Stormwater Manager and Analyst with data collection and evaluation for City’s Annual Report to the Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment.
Performs State inspections as needed for City owned and maintained CDPHE General Construction Stormwater Discharge Permits.
Ability to explain general federal, state, and local laws, rules and regulations pertaining to stormwater/environmental fields
Maintains understanding of all required elements of a stormwater management plan (SWMP) per federal, state, and local regulations.
Ability to explain stormwater control measure standards and specifications effectively to applicable parties.

QUALIFICATIONS:
Knowledge of:
Practices, techniques and principles of science as it relates to stormwater and environmental issues, regulations and projects,
Computer analysis techniques, statistics, basic report preparation and writing,
Federal, state and local regulations related to stormwater and environmental management; and
Standards and specifications as it relates to construction and permanent control measures.
Laws and safety requirements as they relate to vehicle operation and active construction sites.
Ability to:
Work with supervisor to develop and implement appropriate response for various complex issues,
Follow standard operating procedures,
Read, understand, interpret and convey, plans, applicable standards and specification and maps,
Maintain professionalism and composure under stressful work situations,
Operate equipment associated with assigned area of responsibility,
Demonstrate intermediate to advanced level skills using Excel, Access, Word, and Outlook,
Establish and maintain effective working relationships with Department supervisory staff, coworkers, private contractors and others contacted in the course of work,
Drive a City-owned truck, van, or car and safely operate on City business; and
Utilize GPS and ArcMap systems preferred.

EDUCATION AND TRAINING:
Inspector
Required:
Associate degree from a two (2) year college or technical school and a minimum of one (1) year of environmental regulatory compliance experience or related field; an equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.

Senior Inspector:
Required:
Bachelor's Degree in a related field.
Erosion and sediment control certification(s)

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:
Physical demands are heavy (exert up to 100 lbs. of force occasionally, and/or in excess of 50 lbs. of force frequently, and/or in excess of 20 lbs. of force constantly to lift, carry, push, pull, or otherwise move objects). Execution of required tasks in the field require full range of body movements including climbing, balancing, stooping, kneeling, crouching, reaching, handling, feeling, talking, standing or walking much of the time, as well as lifting. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus. The ability to differentiate color is helpful. Data entry and reporting tasks may involve working at a computer for several hours. Approximately 75% of this position is spent in the field and 25% spent in the office.

SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS:
Possession of a valid driver's license with safe driving record.
Bilingual English/Spanish speakers are eligible for a bonus per City policies.
Ability to complete FEMA ICS 100 and IS 700 training within six (6) months of hire.

title: Manager Market Investment Policy

description:
The Manager Market Investment Policy will play a key role in the preparation and implementation of Victoria’s first auction for the development of offshore wind. The Manager provides leadership and advice to deliver auction investment strategies, market integration reforms and supports the progression of the offshore wind auction.

The Manager will develop and implement investment policy and strategy for offshore wind auctions, including design of, and integration with funding and financing vehicles and entities (such as the proposed national Electricity Services Entry Mechanism (ESEM) scheme); legislative design (as required); cost benefit analyses and Gateway reviews; updating of tender documentation; and industry engagement and insights. The role will provide robust, timely policy advice to drive value for money, enable timely informed decision-making, undertake research and analysis, manage input from external advisers and prepare submissions, ministerial briefings and papers. Strong inter-personal and stakeholder engagement skills and policy, research and analytic capabilities are required, together with a collaborative and engaging approach to form influential stakeholder relationships.

description:

Job Summary:

The Manager of Critical Infrastructure Protection (CIP) has primary responsibility for CIP compliance at High and Medium Facilities and shared responsibility for cyber security and compliance for all NRG Control Center and generation control systems. The Manager has direct reports which cover administrative and technical performance all CIP standards at the enterprise level as well as the High and Medium Facilities.

Essential Duties/Responsibilities:

  • Provide leadership, direction, and mentoring to the CIP Team to support team performance, operational efficiency, knowledge development, and personnel growth.
  • Lead NERC CIP compliance activities, including asset classification, policy and procedure development and maintenance, access management, and other administrative compliance functions.
  • Serve as a responsible owner for assigned NERC CIP Standards and oversee enterprise compliance activities supporting CIP systems and High and Medium Impact BES Cyber Systems.
  • Lead the implementation and continuous improvement of OT cybersecurity initiatives, technologies, and controls to strengthen the security and resilience of operational technology environments.
  • Lead the implementation, administration, and continual improvement of the CIP workflow automation application to improve compliance execution, documentation, and reporting.
  • Oversee SME execution of assigned NERC CIP controls, including tracking deliverables and reviewing RSAW responses and supporting evidence to ensure compliance and audit readiness.
  • Support CIP management, specialists, and SMEs in the development of self-reports, Requests for Information (RFIs), Technical Feasibility Exceptions (TFEs), mitigation plans, and evidence supporting mitigation completion.
  • Identify compliance, cybersecurity, and process improvement opportunities and lead initiatives to address control gaps and improve the effectiveness and efficiency of the CIP program.
  • Promote cross-training and knowledge sharing across the CIP Team to strengthen program resiliency and continuity.
  • Identify and escalate potential NERC CIP violations, near misses, and compliance concerns, and support root cause analysis, corrective action development, and validation of identified deficiencies.

Working Conditions:

  • Primarily work from home
  • Open office environment up to 1-2 days per week as required
  • Some overtime is required as special projects arise.
  • Travel up to 25%

Minimum Requirements:

  • Minimum of 3 years of experience developing, administering, or managing a NERC CIP compliance program.
  • Demonstrated experience developing RSAWs, preparing audit evidence, and supporting or leading NERC CIP audits.
  • Previous management or leadership experience, including responsibility for team development, performance, and execution of compliance or cybersecurity objectives.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Engineering, Management Information Systems, Information Technology, or a related technical field. Equivalent relevant experience may be considered.
  • Relevant cybersecurity, OT/ICS security, or compliance certification preferred, such as CISSP, GCIP, GICSP, CISA, or equivalent.
  • 5 to 8 years of experience in NERC CIP compliance, OT/ICS cybersecurity, power generation control systems, or IT/OT network infrastructure.
  • Working knowledge of industrial control systems, plant control equipment, network architecture, cybersecurity controls, and the operational requirements of power generation environments.
  • Experience supporting or leading NERC CIP compliance activities, regulatory audits, evidence development, remediation activities, and implementation of compliance controls.

Additional Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

  • Working knowledge of security, industrial controls, and networking concepts and security tools
  • Demonstrated ability to communicate (verbal and written) with all levels of internal and external customers.
  • Demonstrated presentation and development skills
  • Demonstrated project management skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently and as a team member.
  • Demonstrated ability to set priorities and respond to changing demands from multiple sources.
  • Ability to exercise discretion and independent judgment in applying established techniques, procedures, or standards.
  • Demonstrated analytical and problem-solving skills.

Physical Requirements (Demand and Frequency):

  • Occasionally requires lifting as appropriate to perform duties and responsibilities.

title: Cleared Experienced RD Systems Engineer - ISA Data Management Lead, Onsite
description:
About Sandia

Sandia National Laboratories is the nation’s premier science and engineering lab for national security and technology innovation, with teams of specialists focused on cutting-edge work in a broad array of areas. Some of the main reasons we love our jobs:

  • Challenging work with amazing impact that contributes to security, peace, and freedom worldwide
  • Extraordinary co-workers
  • Some of the best tools, equipment, and research facilities in the world
  • Career advancement and enrichment opportunities
  • Flexible work arrangements for many positions include 9/80 (work 80 hours every two weeks, with every other Friday off) and 4/10 (work 4 ten-hour days each week) compressed workweeks, part-time work, and telecommuting (a mix of onsite work and working from home)
  • Generous vacation, strong medical and other benefits, competitive 401k, learning opportunities, relocation assistance and amenities aimed at creating a solid work/life balance*

World-changing technologies. Life-changing careers. Learn more about Sandia at: http://www.sandia.gov


*These benefits vary by job classification.

What Your Job Will Be Like

The opportunity exists for an experienced R&D Systems Engineer to lead Integrated Surety Architectures (ISA) data management activities. The ISA program has qualified multiple systems in recent years and is currently executing over-the-road missions supporting the secure transportation of nuclear weapons. The effort to prepare for use, accept, transport, return, and re-accept ISA hardware spans multiple agencies across the Nuclear Security Enterprise, from Sandia to the Hub, and the Office of Secure Transportation. The ISA Data Management Lead will provide technical leadership for integrating and streamlining interrelated but disparate mission, engineering, configuration, test, surveillance, and operational data into a common data environment, including DataSEA, to support current and future secure transportation activities. The lead will partner with digital engineering, ISA, weapon system, surveillance, and software teams to develop scalable analysis tools and automated workflows that improve how mission data are organized, evaluated, visualized, and used for engineering decisions.

The role will also lead the integration of mission data with model-based systems engineering and digital-engineering approaches, including system architecture, state models, and analytical workflows that relate system requirements, configuration, and observed performance. These efforts support weapon systems currently implementing ISA, including W88 Alt 940 and B61-12/13, while establishing scalable approaches for future systems such as W93 Alt 950 and emerging ISA technologies. The integration of mission-data sources, analytical tools, automation methods, governance practices, system models, and technology roadmaps is captured in the ISA Data Management Plan, which is maintained and revised as the program evolves.

On any given day, you may be called on to:

  • Serve as the technical point of contact for ISA mission-data architecture, governance, analysis, software and tool development, automation, and digital-engineering integration across multidisciplinary ISA teams
  • Lead continued development, implementation, and maturation of the ISA data-management strategy and technical roadmap
  • Partner across Sandia (e.g. weapon systems, secure transportation, data engineers), the Nuclear Security Enterprise (e.g. KCNMO, the Hub), and the Office of Secure Transportation to lead and implement the ISA data management strategy
  • Provide technical direction to digital engineers to develop analysis tools, automation tools, and explore artificial intelligence implementation
  • Lead the Mission Data Working Group; analyze and assess system state of health, identify and investigate anomalies, and coordinate analysis activities.
  • Coordinate with subsystem surveillance engineers and program data representatives to ensure mission observations, anomalies, configuration changes, test results, and state-of-health assessments are consistently captured and available for broader ISA analysis
  • Integrate mission data with model-based system engineering and state modeling activities, which utilizes system requirements plus performance data to validate mission data and support troubleshooting
  • Revise and release the ISA master data management plan annually

Salary Range

$117,500 - $235,700

*Salary range is estimated, and actual salary will be determined after consideration of the selected candidate's experience and qualifications, and application of any approved geographic salary differential.

Qualifications We Require

  • A Bachelor's degree in a relevant discipline plus five or more years of experience, or an equivalent combination of directly relevant education and engineering or scientific experience that demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and ability to perform independent research and development
  • Active DOE Q clearance

Qualifications We Desire

The ideal R&D S&E Systems Engineer candidate for Sandia National Laboratories will in addition possess the following:

  • Graduate degree in Engineering or a highly related field where an independent research project was a graduation requirement (e.g., independent project, thesis, or dissertation)
  • Experience working with Nuclear Security Enterprise (NSE) laboratories and plants including Pantex, Kansas City National Security Campus (KCNSC), Lawrence Livermore Laboratory (LLNL) and Kansas City National Security Campus/New Mexico Operations (KCNSC/NMO)
  • Experience working on engineering design, qualification, production, or related modeling/simulation projects
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills, ability to work effectively in multidisciplinary teams

Also, for this posting we are seeking individuals with the following experience:

  • Experience successfully leading multidisciplinary technical efforts or coordinating work across systems engineering, analysis, software, digital engineering, test, or program teams
  • Experience with data architecture, metadata management, database systems, or enterprise data platforms, such as DataSEA
  • Experience with model-based system engineering tools, such as Simulink, Stateflow, and System Composer
  • Proficiency with MATLAB and/or other engineering analysis and automation tools
  • Experience developing or guiding automated engineering or analysis workflows
  • Experience with the application of AI-enabled tools to engineering analysis, documentation, or software development
  • Understanding of the data architecture, governance, security, validation, and human oversight needed to support future AI-assisted engineering capabilities
  • Experience with secure transportation systems i.e. Safeguards Transporter
  • Experience with Integrated Surety Architectures hardware e.g. trailer modules, Multiapplication Transportation Attachment Device, Alt hardware
  • Experience with nuclear weapons development, testing, and/or production qualification activities
  • Experience with nuclear weapons engineering documentation e.g. engineering authorizations, drawing definition, PRIME
  • Experience in successfully developing productive relationships within the Nuclear Security Enterprise such as NNSA, management, senior management, nuclear deterrence systems organizations, digital engineering organizations, transportation (e.g. SGT) organizations
  • Proven ability to communicate through both written (e.g. writing delivered documentation) and verbal (e.g. giving presentations) avenues
  • Ability to work onsite full-time
  • Active DOE Q-level security clearance

About Our Team

The Special Projects department was established to focus on the successful deployment of Integrated Surety Architectures (ISA) applications for reentry body and air delivered systems into the transportation safeguards system embodied by the Safeguards Transporter (SGT). The organization serves as the ISA project integration office at Sandia to the NNSA enterprise for over the road (OTR) applications. Currently, there are two major ISA efforts underway at SNL for ALT 940 and the Multi-application Transportation Attachment Device (MTAD) for air delivered systems. As such, the organization interacts extensively with the NW development and stockpile systems capabilities within the laboratory in addition to the transportation safeguards program.

Posting Duration

This posting will be open for application submissions for a minimum of three (3) calendar days, including the 'posting date'. Sandia reserves the right to extend the posting date at any time.

Security Clearance

Position requires a Department of Energy (DOE) Q security clearance to start, or equivalent active security clearance with another U.S. government agency (e.g., DOD). Sandia is required by DOE directive to conduct a pre-employment drug test and background review that includes checks of personal references, credit, law enforcement records, and employment/education verifications. Applicants for employment need to be able to maintain a DOE Q-level security clearance, which requires U.S. citizenship. If you hold more than one citizenship (i.e., of the U.S. and another country), your ability to obtain a security clearance may be impacted.

Applicants offered employment with Sandia are subject to a federal background investigation to meet the requirements for access to classified information or matter if the duties of the position require a DOE security clearance. Substance abuse or illegal drug use, falsification of information, criminal activity, serious misconduct or other indicators of untrustworthiness can cause a clearance to be denied or terminated by DOE, resulting in the inability to perform the duties assigned and subsequent termination of employment.

EEO

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status and any other protected class under state or federal law.

NNSA Requirements for MedPEDs

If you have a Medical Portable Electronic Device (MedPED), such as a pacemaker, defibrillator, drug-releasing pump, hearing aids, or diagnostic equipment and other equipment for measuring, monitoring, and recording body functions such as heartbeat and brain waves, if employed by Sandia National Laboratories you may be required to comply with NNSA security requirements for MedPEDs.

If you have a MedPED and you are selected for an on-site interview at Sandia National Laboratories, there may be additional steps necessary to ensure compliance with NNSA security requirements prior to the interview date.

Join Excellence Property Care Solutions Inc.

Why Work With Us?

Position Overview

Contractors will perform a wide range of property maintenance, handyman repairs, plumbing services, roof leak inspections, electrical troubleshooting, HVAC diagnostics, appliance repairs, and residential/commercial improvement projects.

The ideal contractor should have hands-on experience in one or more maintenance trades and be comfortable diagnosing problems, identifying causes of failure, preparing repair estimates, completing approved work, and documenting service visits according to professional standards.

We particularly welcome multi-trade technicians who can independently handle different types of property maintenance and repair service calls.

  • Shelving and mounting services.

  • Preventive maintenance services.

  • Property inspections and maintenance assessments.

  • Punch-list completion.

  • Property make-ready services.

  • Minor construction and improvement projects.

Plumbing Maintenance & Repair Services

Roof Leak & Exterior Maintenance Services

Experience with residential roofing, leak detection, and exterior waterproofing is preferred.

Electrical Maintenance & Repair Services

Contractors may receive electrical work orders involving:

  • Light fixture installation and replacement.

  • Electrical outlet and switch replacement.

  • GFCI outlet troubleshooting and replacement.

HVAC Maintenance & Repair Services

  • Heating system troubleshooting.

  • Furnace inspection and repair.

  • Heat pump diagnostics and repair.

  • Thermostat replacement and troubleshooting.

  • Capacitor and electrical component replacement.

  • Air filter replacement.

  • HVAC system inspections.

Experience with central air conditioning, heat pumps, furnaces, mini-splits, and residential HVAC systems is preferred.

EPA certification and applicable trade qualifications are preferred for technicians handling refrigerant-related work.

Appliance Repair & Maintenance Services

Contractors may receive appliance-related work orders involving diagnosis, troubleshooting, repair, and replacement of residential and commercial appliances, including:

  • Refrigerator and freezer diagnosis and repair.

  • Washing machine repair and troubleshooting.

  • Dryer repair (gas and electric).

  • Oven, range, and cooktop repair.

Experience with major household appliances, including refrigerators, washers, dryers, dishwashers, ovens, and cooking appliances, is strongly preferred.

Contractor Responsibilities

  • Diagnose maintenance and repair issues accurately.

We Welcome Experienced Professionals From:

Skills That Help You Succeed

Experience in one or multiple trades is highly valued, especially:

  • Plumbing troubleshooting and repairs.

  • Roof leak detection and repairs.

  • Electrical diagnostics and troubleshooting.

  • HVAC troubleshooting and repair.

  • Residential appliance diagnosis and repair.

  • Refrigerator and freezer repairs.

  • Washer and dryer repairs.

  • Heating and cooling systems.

  • Carpentry and drywall repairs.

Multi-trade technicians who can independently handle plumbing, roofing, electrical, HVAC, appliance repair, and general maintenance work are especially encouraged to apply.

title: Supervisor, Coordinator Services
description:
Description

Manage administrative support staff to include, allocation of tasks and activities, resource planning, performance management, training and development, mentoring, coaching, and process improvements for one or more departments/functions. Effectively partners and supports relationships with key stakeholders, e.g., business partners, department heads and business leaders to coordinate and achieve the expectations of Management. Responsible for administrative support to high level business leaders.

As an employee of Boehringer Ingelheim, you will actively contribute to the discovery, development and delivery of our products to our patients and customers. Our global presence provides opportunity for all employees to collaborate internationally, offering visibility and opportunity to directly contribute to the companies' success. We realize that our strength and competitive advantage lie with our people. We support our employees in a number of ways to foster a healthy working environment, meaningful work, mobility, networking and work-life balance. Our competitive compensation and benefit programs reflect Boehringer Ingelheim's high regard for our employees

Duties & Responsibilities

  • Create a performance-based culture with clear accountabilities and a sense of urgency for achieving results. Effectively partners with Manager to ensure appropriate resource allocation, training and process efficiencies are achieved.
  • Interfaces with the Management team to ensure highest degree of consistent and professional support. Coordinate expectations of management by gathering feedback and identifying and resolving operational challenges.
  • Ensure consistent practices with other administrative support teams across the HP business.
  • Applies an advanced level of knowledge to a wide range of interdepartmental responsibilities and requirements while managing the overall functioning of the group.
  • Lead (recruit, hire, coach, develop, motivate, manage and monitor performance) professionals in department specific knowledge, process and procedures. Set job expectations, provide regular feedback, identify performance challenges, create action plans and monitor the effectiveness of those action plans.
  • Forecast volume of departmental activities, timelines and resource allocation to ensure seamless operations within assigned business unit(s). Design, develop and implement strategic resource allocation plan(s) to ensure adequate resource coverage. Provide recommendations to management and related partners on resource allocation needs based on business objectives and deliverables.
  • Design and implement training/development opportunities that will ensure cross-functional capabilities and development of staff. Ensures results of training programs/materials produce high quality, consistent deliverables across groups.
  • Provide back-up for each staff member with up to date desk procedures to refer to for seamless coverage.
  • Collaborates with manager in the monitoring and reconciliation of department budget.
  • Proactively identify process issues by following established policies/procedures. Develop process improvements (e.g. local SOPs/WIs) that will ensure consistency and alignment across groups. Educate and communicate with key stakeholders regarding process improvement opportunities and resolutions. Standardize best practices and create action plans to achieve integration and alignment.
  • Monitors productivity levels, analyzes internal and external trends and identifies opportunities to create new state of the art business support.
  • Performs a variety of complex administrative activities in support of functional areas as assigned within the HP business.
  • Performs all Company business in accordance with all regulations and Company policy and procedures. Demonstrates high ethical and professional standards with all business contacts and BIPI employees in order to maintain the Company’s excellent reputation within the medical and pharmaceutical community.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree from and accredited institution with minimum of six (6) years’ experience or Associates degree from and accredited institution with ten (10) years’ experience in an administrative or customer service environment required.
  • Understanding of administrative support role relevant to job function. Incumbent must have adequate knowledge of administrative support requirements necessary to provide the depth and breadth to lead group.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to be clear and concise in a variety of communication settings.
  • Proven leadership skills, effective decision making, proactively identifying and solving problems related to improving efficiencies.
  • Solid understanding of and experience with financial business processes, such as budget and capacity planning.
  • Proven organizational skills and demonstrated ability to multi-task.
  • Excellent time management skills with the ability to work well under pressure.
  • Demonstrated computer skills necessary to function in role.
  • Knowledge of current industry standards and trends.
  • Ability to form strong relationships with all levels of the organization and influence without authority.
  • Strong demonstration of BI leadership and AAI competencies.
  • Understanding of administrative support role relevant to job function.
  • Experience in the development of successful training/education programs preferred.
  • Proven organizational skills and demonstrated ability to multi-task.
  • Excellent time management skills with the ability to work well under pressure.
  • Adherence to government regulations (e.g., FDA, ICH), company SOPs, local working instructions and role specific training.

Desired Skills, Experience and Abilities

  • Five (5) or more years of previous administrative experience with BI preferred; three (3) or more years of management responsibilities preferred
  • Successful experience in leading and managing a group relative to recruiting and staffing, performance management, development and engagement preferred.
  • Experience in the development of successful training/education programs preferred.

Compensation

The base salary range for this position is $87,000 to $115,776. The position may be eligible for a role-specific discretionary bonus, relocation assistance, and/or other compensation elements. We continuously review market data and may adjust salary ranges as needed in the future. Actual compensation will be based on job-related factors such as skills, experience, qualifications, and other factors permitted by law. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, retirement savings opportunities, paid time off, paid holidays, disability and life insurance benefits, and other company-sponsored benefits. For additional information regarding our benefits and Total Rewards offerings, please click here.

title: Manager, Facilities In-House Construction (04936), Onsite
description:
About Sandia

Sandia National Laboratories is the nation’s premier science and engineering lab for national security and technology innovation, with teams of specialists focused on cutting-edge work in a broad array of areas. Some of the main reasons we love our jobs:

  • Challenging work with amazing impact that contributes to security, peace, and freedom worldwide
  • Extraordinary co-workers
  • Some of the best tools, equipment, and research facilities in the world
  • Career advancement and enrichment opportunities
  • Flexible work arrangements for many positions include 9/80 (work 80 hours every two weeks, with every other Friday off) and 4/10 (work 4 ten-hour days each week) compressed workweeks, part-time work, and telecommuting (a mix of onsite work and working from home)
  • Generous vacation, strong medical and other benefits, competitive 401k, learning opportunities, relocation assistance and amenities aimed at creating a solid work/life balance*

World-changing technologies. Life-changing careers. Learn more about Sandia at: http://www.sandia.gov


*These benefits vary by job classification.

What Your Job Will Be Like

We are seeking an experienced Manager for Department 4936 In-House Construction that can run a construction organization and build a predictable, transparent planning cadence which provides in-house construction services for small facilities projects, including work in high-security spaces.

The selected candidate will be responsible for developing and maintaining a 6+ month look-ahead schedule, shaping and sequencing the work with partners and customers, and level-loading execution so the craft workforce remains productive and appropriately challenged throughout the year.

On any given day, you may be called on to:

  • Provide leadership for in-house construction execution for small projects, including work planning, scheduling, field coordination, and delivery.
  • Oversee the continual development and maintenance of a resource-loaded schedule with at least a 6-month look-ahead. Accountable for monitoring and reporting on adjustments to the plans as priorities and constraints change.
  • Establish a scheduling and communication system that clearly communicates planned work to craft, planners, team leads, and stakeholders (e.g., quarterly outlook, 6-8 week rolling plan, weekly commitments).
  • Strategically coordinate with partners/customers to align execution windows, resolve constraints, and maintain a healthy backlog to keep crews productively engaged year-round.
  • Lead a workforce of approximately 66 reports including planners, team leads, plumbers, electricians, carpenters, painters, laborers, and apprentices.
  • Lead with compassion and respect, listening to concerns, setting clear expectations, and fostering a culture where people feel valued and heard.
  • Provide management and oversight for a represented craft workforce, addressing performance, engagement, and workforce needs while maintaining strong working relationships.
  • Manage budgets related to labor and materials and/or project budgets, including forecasting, cost control, and reporting.
  • Promote safe work practices and compliance with construction safety requirements, including OSHA 29 CFR 1926, through planning, field presence, and reinforcement of safe behaviors.
  • Participate in project execution team with peer managers (e.g., project management, design, construction management, portfolio management) to align scope, schedule, and resources.

Due to the nature of the work, the selected applicant must be able to work onsite.

Salary Range

$138,600 - $235,700

*Salary range is estimated, and actual salary will be determined after consideration of the selected candidate's experience and qualifications, and application of any approved geographic salary differential.

Qualifications We Require

  • Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Engineering, Architecture, Business, or related field plus eight (8) or more years of directly related experience; Or equivalent combination of relevant education and experience.
  • Minimum of five (5) years of construction leadership experience leading supervisors/foremen/team leads and craft personnel (self-perform and/or subcontracted work).
  • Experience in the following:
    • Building and maintaining a resource-loaded schedule with at least a 6-month look-ahead, including coordinating execution windows with customers/stakeholders.
    • Load-level work and manage backlog to keep crews productive year-round (balancing planned work and emergent work).
    • Budget management experience (annual operating budget and/or project budgets), including forecasting and controlling labor/material/subcontract costs.
    • Construction safety requirements, including OSHA 29 CFR 1926, with experience leading safe work planning and field execution.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain an active DOE Q-level security clearance.

Qualifications We Desire

  • Minimum of two years of demonstrated leadership experience.
  • Demonstrated experience partnering with customers and cross-functional stakeholders to define scope, negotiate priorities and execution windows, manage expectations, and resolve conflicts/constraints.
  • Experience with one or more of the following:
    • Implementing a formal scheduling and communication system (cadence, meetings, dashboards/reports) used by both craft and leadership.
    • Leading a represented/union craft workforce and working in a collective bargaining environment.
    • Executing work in high-security or otherwise highly regulated/high-compliance environments.
    • Developing and executing a design/build or fast-track process that aligns design with construction in one integrated schedule.
  • Knowledge of project controls practices such as estimating, production tracking, change control, and risk management.
  • Relevant professional certifications (e.g., PMP, CCM, PE, etc.).
  • GB-98 General Building Contractor license in New Mexico.
  • Active DOE Q-level security clearance or equivalent (e.g., DOD Top Secret).

About Our Team

In-House Construction (Org. 4936) provides agile construction services for small projects, delivering general construction capabilities across mechanical, electrical, plumbing, and related trades. The department continues to develop emerging specialties in secure and highly technical work environments, including SCIF's, STC door installations, communications infrastructure, and welding, further expanding our ability to meet evolving mission and facility needs.

Posting Duration

This posting will be open for application submissions for a minimum of three (3) calendar days, including the 'posting date'. Sandia reserves the right to extend the posting date at any time.

Security Clearance

Sandia is required by DOE to conduct a pre-employment drug test and background review that includes checks of personal references, credit, law enforcement records, and employment/education verifications. Applicants for employment need to be able to obtain and maintain a DOE Q-level security clearance, which requires U.S. citizenship. If you hold more than one citizenship (i.e., of the U.S. and another country), your ability to obtain a security clearance may be impacted.

Applicants offered employment with Sandia are subject to a federal background investigation to meet the requirements for access to classified information or matter if the duties of the position require a DOE security clearance. Substance abuse or illegal drug use, falsification of information, criminal activity, serious misconduct or other indicators of untrustworthiness can cause a clearance to be denied or terminated by DOE, resulting in the inability to perform the duties assigned and subsequent termination of employment.

EEO

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status and any other protected class under state or federal law.

NNSA Requirements for MedPEDs

If you have a Medical Portable Electronic Device (MedPED), such as a pacemaker, defibrillator, drug-releasing pump, hearing aids, or diagnostic equipment and other equipment for measuring, monitoring, and recording body functions such as heartbeat and brain waves, if employed by Sandia National Laboratories you may be required to comply with NNSA security requirements for MedPEDs.

If you have a MedPED and you are selected for an on-site interview at Sandia National Laboratories, there may be additional steps necessary to ensure compliance with NNSA security requirements prior to the interview date.

title: Financial Reporting Manager
description:
Company Information

PACCAR is a Fortune 500 company established in 1905. PACCAR Inc is recognized as a global leader in the commercial vehicle, financial, and customer service fields with internationally recognized brands such as Kenworth, Peterbilt, and DAF trucks. PACCAR is a global technology leader in the design, manufacture, and customer support of high-quality light-, medium- and heavy-duty trucks under the Kenworth, Peterbilt and DAF nameplates. PACCAR designs and manufactures advanced diesel engines and also provides customized financial services, information technology and truck parts related to its principal business.

Whether you want to design the transportation technology of tomorrow, support the staff functions of a dynamic, international leader, or build our excellent products and services — you can develop the career you desire with PACCAR. Get started!

Position Summary

PACCAR External Reporting team is seeking a motivated Financial Reporting Manager to lead one permanent staff and a rotating team of accounting professionals from various PACCAR divisions in the preparation of PACCAR forms 10-Q, 10-K, 8-K, Employee Benefit Plans and related filings. The position will contribute to process improvements, ensure adherence to department procedures and offer an opportunity to gain exposure to PACCAR’s global operations. The position reports to the Assistant Director of Financial Reporting within Corporate Accounting team.

Job Functions/ Responsibilities:

  • Manage the preparation of PACCAR Inc’s SEC filings (including 8-K, 10-Q,10-K and 11-K), annual reports and employee benefit plan financial statements.
  • Perform detail reviews of footnotes, MD&A and other workpapers and analyses prepared by the External Reporting team.
  • Assist with review of XBRL tagging of financial statements and footnotes.
  • Prepare peer and benchmarking analyses.
  • Coordinate with external auditors during the quarterly review process and annual audit.
  • Perform technical GAAP / SEC research including interaction with various divisions.
  • Assist with the adoption of new accounting pronouncements.
  • Assist in monitoring emerging GAAP and SEC regulations and evaluate impact to the Company’s financial reporting.

title: Senior Wiresaw Engineer
description:
Requisition Number: 79765

The company built on breakthroughs. ​
Join us.​

Corning is one of the world’s leading innovators in glass, ceramic, and materials science. From the depths of the ocean to the farthest reaches of space, our technologies push the boundaries of what’s possible. ​

How do we do this? With our people. They break through limitations and expectations – not once in a career, but every day. They help move our company, and the world, forward. ​

​At Corning, there are endless possibilities for making an impact. You can help connect the unconnected, drive the future of automobiles, transform at-home entertainment, and ensure the delivery of lifesaving medicines. And so much more.​

​Come break through with us.

Our Solar business delivers industry leading, U.S.-made solar components. We manufacture hyper-pure polysilicon, high-quality solar wafers, and innovative photovoltaic modules, leveraging our leadership in advanced manufacturing to serve growing energy demand. You will be a part of advancing critical U.S. supply chains and delivering unmatched quality and reliability to customers.

Role Purpose

We are seeking a highly experienced, hands-on Wire Saw and Wafer Manufacturing Engineer to serve as the technical authority for ingot conversion and wafering operations in a solar wafer manufacturing facility.

This is a manufacturing-floor role for an individual who works directly with wire saws, operators, technicians, maintenance, process engineering, quality, and upstream/downstream manufacturing teams. The successful candidate will improve wafer yield, quality, throughput, equipment uptime, consumable utilization, kerf loss, breakage performance, process stability, and manufacturing cost.

The ideal candidate has deep practical experience with silicon ingot cropping, squaring, grinding, wire sawing, wafer cleaning, drying, inspection, sorting, handling, and packaging. The candidate must be comfortable working directly on production equipment, observing process behavior, adjusting and validating recipes, troubleshooting failures, leading trials, and sustaining improvements in a high-volume wafer manufacturing environment.

Key Responsibilities

  • Provide hands-on technical leadership for silicon ingot conversion and wafer manufacturing, with particular expertise in wire-saw operation, wafering processes, equipment setup, troubleshooting, process optimization, and production support.
  • Develop, optimize, and control wire-saw recipes and critical process parameters to improve wafer thickness, TTV, bow, warp, surface and edge quality, geometry, breakage performance, cutting yield, kerf loss, consumable usage, cycle time, and overall conversion cost.
  • Lead troubleshooting and root-cause analysis for wire breaks, cutting instability, wafer breakage, dimensional variation, contamination, process excursions, equipment downtime, and other wafering defects using production data, equipment trends, metrology, defect analysis, and downstream performance feedback.
  • Establish robust manufacturing controls, including equipment recipes, operating windows, setup instructions, first-article requirements, in-process controls, inspection criteria, reaction plans, preventive maintenance requirements, and standard work. Implement and sustain corrective and preventive actions through documented process controls and operator training.
  • Partner with equipment engineering and maintenance teams to improve reliability and process capability, including wire-feed and tension systems, guide systems, table motion, spindles, slurry/coolant delivery, filtration, temperature control, sensors, vision systems, material handling, calibration, preventive maintenance, and equipment recovery.
  • Lead process development, experimentation, and qualification activities, including structured trials, DOEs, capability studies, validation plans, equipment commissioning, and qualification of new or upgraded wire saws, cleaning systems, inspection equipment, automation, and critical consumables.
  • Support new product and technology introduction, developing manufacturing-ready processes for new ingot sizes, wafer thicknesses and geometries, crystal types, resistivity ranges, and customer requirements, including advanced technologies such as ultra-thin and large-format wafers, low-kerf and diamond-wire cutting, automated handling, advanced cleaning, and in-line metrology.
  • Serve as the site technical subject-matter expert and cross-functional partner for wafering, working closely with crystal growth, shaping, cleaning, inspection, quality, product engineering, maintenance, suppliers, and downstream cell manufacturing. Train production personnel on equipment operation, material handling, defect recognition, troubleshooting, process controls, and new-process readiness.

Experiences/Education - Required

  • Bachelor’s degree in Materials Science, Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Physics, or a related technical discipline; equivalent extensive, directly relevant industry experience may be considered.
  • 10+ years of progressive engineering or technical manufacturing experience in high-volume, precision manufacturing environments, including significant hands-on responsibility for process optimization, equipment troubleshooting, yield improvement, and production support.
  • 8+ years of hands-on experience in silicon wafer manufacturing, ingot conversion, wire sawing, precision slicing, semiconductor wafering, or a comparable high-volume precision-materials manufacturing environment.
  • Demonstrated expert-level understanding of silicon wire-saw processes, preferably including diamond-wire sawing and associated wafer cleaning and inspection operations.
  • Proven ability to independently troubleshoot and optimize wire-saw recipes, wire-management systems, cutting parameters, consumables, equipment performance, and wafer-quality outcomes on the manufacturing floor.
  • Strong knowledge of wafer quality metrics and failure modes, including thickness, TTV, bow, warp, kerf loss, surface damage, edge quality, breakage, cleanliness, and contamination.
  • Demonstrated success improving wafer yield, throughput, first-pass yield, silicon utilization, consumable cost, equipment uptime, and process stability.
  • Experience interpreting equipment trends, production data, dimensional metrology, inspection data, defect paretos, breakage records, and downstream performance feedback.
  • Experience using structured problem-solving methods such as DOE, SPC, PFMEA, 8D, A3, root-cause analysis, and corrective/preventive action.
  • Ability and willingness to spend the majority of the workday working directly on the manufacturing floor.

Experiences/Education - Desired

  • Direct experience with high-volume diamond-wire saw equipment used for silicon solar-wafer manufacturing.
  • Experience with large-format, thin, or ultra-thin silicon wafers and high-efficiency solar-cell product requirements.
  • Experience with in-line wafer metrology, including thickness, TTV, bow, warp, geometry, surface inspection, crack detection, contamination monitoring, and automated sorting.
  • Experience with wafer-cleaning and drying systems, chemical handling, water-quality control, recycling/reclamation systems, and slurry/coolant filtration.
  • Experience leading new equipment installation, equipment commissioning, production ramp-up, technology transfer, or new-product introduction.
  • Familiarity with crystal growth, ingot shaping, wafer recycling, and downstream solar-cell manufacturing requirements.
  • Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, DOE, or equivalent continuous-improvement training.
  • Experience using MES, SCADA, equipment historian systems, SPC tools, JMP, Minitab, Python, SQL, or advanced Excel for process analysis.

This position does not support immigration sponsorship.

The range for this position is $114,457.00 - $157,379.00 assuming full time status. Starting pay for the successful applicant is dependent on a variety of job-related factors, including but not limited to geographic location, market demands, experience, training, and education.

​

A job that shapes a life.

Corning offers you the total package.

Your well-being is our priority. Our compensation and benefits package supports your health and wellness, financial aspirations, and career from day one.

  • Company-wide bonuses and long-term incentives align with key business results and ensure you are rewarded when the company performs well. When Corning wins, we all win.
  • As part of our commitment to your financial well-being, we provide a 100% company-paid pension benefit with fixed contributions that grow throughout your career. Combined with matching contributions to your 401(k) savings plan, Corning’s total contributions to your retirement accounts can reach between 7% and 12% of your pay, depending on your age and years of service.
  • Our health and well-being benefits include medical, dental, vision, paid parental leave, family building support, fitness, company-paid life insurance, disability, disease management programs, paid time off, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) to support you and your family.
  • Getting paid for our work is important, but feeling appreciated and recognized for those contributions motivates us much more. That’s why Corning offers a recognition program to celebrate successes and reward colleagues who make exceptional contributions.

We prohibit discrimination on the basis of race, color, gender, age, religion, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, disability, veteran status or any other legally protected status.

Corning is committed to providing equal employment opportunities and considers requests for reasonable accommodations in accordance with applicable laws. Individuals with disabilities or sincerely held religious beliefs may request reasonable accommodations to participate in the application or interview process, perform essential job functions, or access other benefits and privileges of employment. To submit a request for reasonable accommodation related to disability or religion, please contact us at accommodations@corning.com.

title: Senior Engineer E&I
description:
OUR CULTURE

We are a joint venture between Tianqi Lithium Corporation and IGO Ltd. As pioneers in the Australian lithium industry, we've already achieved great things, including building the first battery-grade lithium hydroxide plant in Australia, paving the way for Australia to be a major player in the global transition to a clean energy future.

We’re looking for people who want to be a part of the industry of the future - people who work with purpose and urgency, take initiative, and rise to challenges. We're seeking individuals who empower others, embrace innovation, and want to work in an open and supportive environment, where teamwork and collaboration are valued.

At TLEA, you’ll be part of a team that is excited to be involved in a world-class project that benefits not only the Western Australian community but the world.

ABOUT THE POSITION

Are you passionate about making a real impact?

TLEA is welcoming applications for a full time, 2 Year Max term Senior Engineer E&I to join our team working at our Kwinana plant.

The successful applicant will be responsible for E&I design activities across all project phases. This includes developing design scopes, conducting technical reviews, and approving engineering design documentation to ensure alignment with project intent and quality standards. The role will also and coordinate improvements to Technical Standards and support the performance of engineering service providers.

What we are really seeking is a proven Engineer with a strong Instrumentation background, who has ideally worked for a design institute or consultancy with the following experience:

  • Review/input to PIDs
  • Developing instrument list
  • Developing instrument datasheets
  • Developing PCS I/O list
  • Developing instrument MTO
  • Developing instrument cable schedule
  • Selection of correct instruments according to the process/project requirements
  • Selection of the correct modulation valves/actuated valves according to the process/project requirement
  • Calculation skills for instruments
  • Developing functional specification according to process/project requirement

Equally, we are seeking strong Electrical design capability, with demonstrated experience in:

  • Review/input to electrical single line diagrams (SLDs) and load lists
  • Developing electrical equipment specifications and datasheets (e.g. HV/LV switchgear, MCCs, transformers, VSDs, UPS and motors)
  • Electrical load flow, short circuit, voltage drop, cable sizing and protection coordination/discrimination calculations
  • Developing electrical cable schedules, cable routing and general arrangement/layout drawings
  • Developing electrical material take-offs (MTO)
  • Hazardous area classification and the selection of suitably rated electrical equipment
  • Earthing, lightning protection and power distribution design for industrial facilities
  • In addition to possessing our core values of distinction, pragmatism, honesty, tenacity and innovation, this position will suit candidates with a background in Brownfields operations and environments.

DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Applies a strong understanding of Electrical & Instrumentation engineering terminology, theory, core processes and discipline specific activities.
  • Performs engineering tasks, validates construction methodologies, and provides guidance on engineering to ensure alignment with project, construction, and commissioning engineering standards
  • Ensure Electrical & Instrumentation system designs appropriately consider all interfaces with other disciplines including mechanical, process and civil.
  • Leads the design, review and approval of electrical power systems, including HV/LV power distribution, motor control, standby power, earthing and lightning protection.
  • Reviews electrical studies and calculations (load flow, short circuit, arc flash, protection coordination, cable sizing) and verifies electrical equipment specifications, single line diagrams and cable schedules.
  • Ensures electrical designs comply with applicable Australian Standards and statutory requirements, including hazardous area (explosive atmosphere) requirements, and supports electrical safety in design.
  • Reviews and signs off on all relevant engineering design documentation as the single point of accountability, engaging other disciplines as required during design reviews.
  • Applies specialised discipline expertise and provides leadership to meet TLEA's engineering and quality expectations.
  • Identifies and assesses risks, makes risk informed decisions, and builds a risk aware culture to support safe and productive performance outcomes.

WHAT YOU CAN BRING

  • Extensive experience in Electrical & Instrumentation Engineering role with relevant industry experience.
  • Demonstrated experience in electrical power system design for industrial or process plants, including HV/LV distribution, motor control centres, variable speed drives and protection.
  • Working knowledge of electrical design standards and software, such as AS/NZS 3000, AS/NZS 60079 (hazardous areas), AS/NZS 61439 and ETAP (or equivalent power systems analysis tools).
  • Bachelor’s degree or higher, Engineering.
  • Proven experience in project management from design through to commissioning.
  • Experience in refining plant operations
  • Strong analytical skills with a high level of attention to detail
  • Effective communications and leadership capabilities with the ability to convey technical knowledge clearly and concisely.
  • Demonstrated focus on following and upholding established processes.
  • Advanced Microsoft Office programs skills

WHAT WE OFFER

  • Contribute to a green and sustainable industry of the future.
  • Competitive salary with a performance-based discretionary bonus structure
  • Additional Superannuation
  • Award and recognition program
  • Long service leave option after 5 years (pro rata)
  • Supportive colleagues committed to your success and well-being
  • Inclusive and diverse work environment

LOCATION

TLEA proudly acknowledges and the Whadjuk and Gnaala Karla Boodja people of the Noongar Nation, as the traditional custodians of the Kwinana area, where we operate our plant.

Kwinana is 38 km from the Perth central business district, 20 km from City of Fremantle and just 7km from Rockingham.

HOW DO I APPLY?

To find out more about this unique opportunity, please submit your application by Monday 23rd November 2026 by clicking the 'Apply' button. All applications and discussions will be kept strictly confidential.

Applicants are advised that the shortlisting and interview process may commence before the closing date.

At Tianqi Lithium Energy Australia, we embrace and recognise the value of diversity. We are committed to providing a work environment where everyone is included, treated fairly and with respect. We welcome and encourage applications from people from diverse backgrounds.

title: Senior Engineer - Public Sector
description:
Lumen is the trusted network for the AI‑powered world, connecting people, data, and applications through our expansive fiber network and connected ecosystem. We enable secure, high‑performance connectivity across cloud, edge, and AI workloads for enterprises, governments, and communities.

At Lumen, you’ll work on infrastructure customers rely on today and build for what’s next, where performance, security, and resilience matter.

This is a high accountability environment where bold ideas drive real innovation for our customers, partners, and industry. The work is challenging, expectations are clear, and trust is built into how we operate. If you’re ready to take ownership, deliver meaningful impact, and help shape the future of AI‑ready connectivity, join us today.

The Role

The candidate will perform a wide variety of Engineering tasks, to include: installation, maintenance, product assembly, testing, training, documentation, measures of performance, accountability related to Product Quality Assurance and Operation, Quality Control of the Program Network Infrastructure, and associated Hydrogen Fuel Cell Engine/Hydrogen Fuel Storage Infrastructure. Also, the development, implementation, and maintenance of new products. These tasks are to ensure each facet of performance meets the customers’ requirements. Travel will be a major component of this position, 45 percent or more, as will the receipt of associated training enabling the candidate to retain and execute specialized tasks.

The Main Responsibilities

  • Have a minimum of five (5) years of hands on experience installing, maintaining, testing, documenting, and troubleshooting telecommunications equipment and systems, both Inside Plant (ISP), and Outside Plant (OSP).
  • Have the ability to interpret, redline, and critique Methods of Procedure (MOP’s), Engineering Design Packages (EDP’s), and associated As-Builts for the purpose of Quality Assurance (QA) and Quality Control (QC), and Maintenace on a by site and at a network level.
  • Must be able to learn new technologies which continually change due to network additions or upgrades to meet the customers’ requirements.
  • Must be able to work independently in the field and address/engineer on the spot solutions, and/or provide recommendations concerning installations, alarming, wiring, DC power, measures of performance, troubleshooting, and accurately document actions/observations on site.
  • Must be able to follow established SOP’s, Procedures, Guidelines, Policies, Processes, and Standards.
  • Will be involved working with Hydrogen Fuel Cell Technology, and associated equipment, fuel infrastructure, compressed air infrastructure, software/firmware, documentation, testing, installation, and maintenance of said equipment.
  • Must be able to perform strenuous physical activities to include, but not limited to: moving/lifting objects/material weighing at a minimum of fifty (50) pounds.
  • Must be able to work well with others to achieve a common goal, foster a cooperative climate with co-workers, and poses good communication and social skills.
  • Must have work experience and knowledge with related Telecommunications tools, test sets/kits, and materials to include, but not limited to: power meters, multi-meters, fiber splicing, fiber optic testing, fiber optic cleaning, ISP installation, maintaining of equipment, troubleshooting, and others.
  • Must have prior computer work experience with, but not limited to: Microsoft Office, PowerPoint, Visio, and be able to write procedures, produce MOP’s, update EDP’s, update As-Builts, perform Site Surveys, and provide end of day site visit forms.

What We Look For in a Candidate

  • A Minimum of Five (5) years Hands-On Experience in Telecommunications Field Installation, Test and Turn Up (TTU), and Maintenance of said systems.
  • Familiarity and/or Hands-On experience with Hydrogen, and Hydrogen Fuel Cell Technology/Infrastructure is highly desired.
  • Exceptional Telecommunications Troubleshooting Skills required.
  • Exceptional Communications Skills required.
  • Able to work independently and in a multi-disciplined team environment required.
  • DC or AC Power experience desired.
  • BICSI Certification in ISP/OSP a plus.
  • Technical Writing and Documentation Skills desired.

Education

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering, like discipline, or equivalent experience.

Security Requirements

  • US Citizenship Required
  • Active TS/SCI Required
  • Must maintain eligibility for access to classified information.

Compensation

This information reflects the anticipated base salary range for this position based on current national data. Minimums and maximums may vary based on location. Individual pay is based on skills, experience and other relevant factors.
